News.title: Migrant ‘taxi boat’ arrives at popular Spanish beach before men jump off and wade to shore in front of stunned tourists
News.content:
A BOATLOAD of migrants left sunbathers shocked when they jumped ship and waded ashore an idyllic Spnaish beach.

Dramatic footage shows several men leaping into the lapping blue waves and strolling onto the sands of Playa de San José in Níjar.



Nine men clambered out of the fishing boat just yards from the Mediterranean coast – as children played just a stone’s throw away.

Shocked onlookers filmed the arrival on Saturday and posted the dramatic footage on social media.



One sunbather in shorts can be seen fleeing the scene as the migrants made their impromptu landing.

The Níjar coastline has become a bustling hotspot for North African boats.

Although figures for 2026 are lower than the previous year, migrant landings and rescues have continued week after week.

Just last week Spanish authorities rescued nine Algerian men in a boat 41 miles off the Mediterranean coast.

The migrants had departed from Oran in Algeria and reportedly drifted through the sea to Europe for 38 hours.



Across August more than 150 migrants travelling in boats managed to reach or were intercepted on the Almeria coast.

The mass arrivals have triggered a thriving black market in fake passports and immigration documents, according to local media.

Underworld gangs are allegedly selling fake papers for thousands of pounds.

Sham rental agreements, false address registrations and bogus job offers can allegedly help people swindle the legal system.



Criminal business is reportedly booming in migrant landing hotspots – such as the nearby towns of Roquetas de Mar, El Ejido and Vícar.

Police investigations have uncovered hundreds of allegedly fraudulent documents and registrations.

In southern Spanish town Roquetas de Mar cops uncovered 188 fake address registrations – and arrested 18 suspects.

In one shocking case, more than 100 people had been documented as living inside one building.

Another probe revealed a criminal gang raking in more than €100,000 (£85,929) from fabricating fake documents.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Spanish cops have also smashed a smuggling ring that charged people entry onto so-called “migrant taxis” – before dumping them overboard.

The human trafficking gangs reportedly slash their victims with machetes and beat them to pulp aboard the 50ft boats.

News.title: Fresh twist in Baby April murder as mystery woman seen near grave 30yrs after tot wrapped in tissue bag & dumped in lake
News.content:
CHILLING CLUE Fresh twist in Baby April murder as mystery woman seen near grave 30yrs after tot wrapped in tissue bag & dumped in lake

A MYSTERY woman has been spotted by the grave of a newborn baby who was strangled and dumped in a lake over thirty years ago.

The visitor was seen at Bybrook Cemetery in Ashford, Kent back in June, where Baby April was buried, and appeared to be distressed.



Thought to have been just a week old, the tot’s tiny body was found wrapped in plastic bags at a local beauty spot on April 5 1995.

Cops have been unable to trace the child’s parents or any relatives, despite attempting a DNA test in 2011.



But now, they believe they have a lead, with onlookers describing the mystery visitor as a woman in her 40s, white, around 5ft 7in and of a slim build.

She was reportedly wearing a grey short cardigan, trainers and black trainers, with grey shoulder-length hair.

She was also seen carrying a small shoulder bag and a fabric holdall with a floral pattern, which appeared to be full.

Kent Police released a computer-generated image of the woman, according to the description, in the hope of making a breakthrough.



Cops are calling on the public for information that may help the investigation.

Baby April was discovered at Singleton Lake in Ashford by a teen couple.

She had been strangled with a pair of tights then wrapped up in Kleenex toilet bag before placed inside another plastic bag.

Cops say the baby had likely been born between March 25 and April 3 in 1995 – just a week before she was discovered.

The helpless tot was thought to have been born without medical intervention, due to the roughly severed umbilical cord.



Officers launched a murder investigation following the harrowing discovery but were unable to find the parents.

They exhumed her body in 2011 to analyse DNA before she was laid to rest again at the cemetery in Ashford.

In 2025, experts at the Kent and Essex Serious Crime Directorate hoped to progress the investigation using more advanced DNA profiling and forensic science.

DI Lee Neiles said: “This is a horrific case of a newborn baby girl being killed and discarded in a lake.”

“April would be 30 years old now and who knows what she would be contributing to society, but someone ended her life in the most unimaginable way and prevented that young baby growing up to be a girl and a woman.



“I have no doubt someone out there has information in relation to this case, and now that three decades have passed, it has to be the time to do the right thing and come forward so that we can get justice for April.

“Advances in forensic science, particularly familial DNA, now give us an even better chance of establishing who her parents are.

“We urge the mother of April to come forward now, rather than we come to you.”

Detective Chief Inspector Neil Kimber said: “Baby April was named after the month she was born.

“Despite ongoing inquiries since that time, her parents and true identity to this date have never been found.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We believe it is important to find the truth behind this tragic story and this woman might have information which could assist us in finding that.”

News.title: Migrant who raped teen after dodging deportation over his ‘human rights’ told her ‘I think you’ve had enough now’
News.content:
SICK ATTACK Migrant who raped teen after dodging deportation over his ‘human rights’ told her ‘I think you’ve had enough now’

A MIGRANT who raped a teen after avoiding deportation over his “human rights” told her: “I think you’ve had enough now”.

Nigerian national Gift Oladele, 24, dragged the terrified 19-year-old into woodland as she walked home from a night out in Wrexham, Wales.



The predator was already known to the authorities, having been jailed for two years in 2022 for the false imprisonment of a woman in Manchester.

Following his sentencing, the Home Office ordered his deportation but Oladele successfully appealed through the Asylum and Immigration Tribunal.



The court ruled removing him would violate Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which protects the right to respect for private and family life.

Once freed from jail, Oladele carried out the sickening sex attack – but was locked up for 25 years earlier this year.

The brave victim has now spoken out to reveal that after the horror, Oladele said: “I think you’ve had enough now.

“At least you have been raped by someone good-looking.”

Recalling the attack last September, the woman told how she tried to push Oladele away but he was “a lot bigger” than her.

She added: “He was covering my mouth. I was trying to get his arm off me, but he wasn’t budging. That’s when he raped me violently.



“He asked me if it was the first time I had been raped.

“Pictures of my family kept flashing in my head because I thought he was going to kill me.

“My brain just switched into survival mode. It was weird.



“It was either I do what he says, and I get home to my mum, or he is going to kill me.”

The woman revealed how Oladele also threatened to “put a black baby in you” and hit her six times – leaving a bruise in the shape of his hand.

He also said he would “find her” if she reported the rape but she immediately told her parents when she got home.

She said: “I came in screaming, saying ‘mum’ and then I walked into their room and I went, ‘you need to ring the police’.

“My mum said, ‘Why?’ and I said, ‘I’ve just been raped’ and my mum ran to the toilet to be sick.



“I felt numb. I was hysterical. My brain couldn’t figure out what had just happened. My dad called the police, and they came out in about 10 minutes.”

Oladele was arrested the next day at his cousin’s home in Wrexham.

The fiend, who born in Italy but a Nigerian national, arrived in the UK with entry clearance until 2014 but went on to live here illegally.

In 2022, he was arrested for holding the woman captive and later told cops he “just wanted to get it on with her”.

After his conviction for the broad daylight attack, the Home Office ordered his deportation under the UK Borders Act 2007.



Oladele submitted an appeal to the Asylum and Immigration Tribunal on June 24, 2023, claiming he has a family life in the UK with his partner and that he would face insurmountable obstacles if he was sent back.

The tribunal ruled in his favour and said the refusal by the Home Office to revoke the deportation order had been a “breach of the Appellant’s protected rights” under Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights.

Less than three months after his conviction, Oladele raped the 19-year-old.

Following Oladele’s arrest, police found evidence on his phone that showed a long standing interest in forced sexual abuse.

A Home Office spokesperson said after his conviction: “This is an absolutely horrific case, and our thoughts are with the victim of this heinous criminal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Foreign nationals who commit crimes should be in zero doubt that we will aim to remove them from the UK at the earliest opportunity.

“The Home Secretary has announced sweeping reforms to tackle illegal migration, which will make the UK less attractive for illegal migrants and make it easier to remove them.”

News.title: Disgusting moment newborn RAT is found wiggling in sauce of beef takeaway by horrified customer
News.content:
THIS is the revolting moment a newborn rat is found wriggling in the sauce of a beef takeaway by a disgusted customer.

One diner was left horrified in Hong Kong when her beef satay contained a second meaty surprise.



Horrifying footage shows a slimy malformed creature squirming beside the spaghetti in the £4.50 (HK$48) dish.

Pink, hairless and with limbs not yet fully formed the newborn rat can be seen wiggling its arms and legs from within the depths of a pale brown sauce.



The takeaway set meal should have included beef satay rice noodles, a ham omelete and a drink.

But when the customer opened the styrofoam box – she lifted the lid on a harrowing hygiene mishap.



The unlucky woman swiftly filmed the culinary catastrophe – and reported the Wa Jer Restaurant to the Food and Environmental Hygiene Departmenton Monday.

Officials have been left scratching their heads as to how the box could have been served with the newborn rat inside.

A health department spokesperson said they had prompty seized the foul food for testing – and after investigating the restauarant, found it to have “unsatisfactory hygiene conditions”.

The disgraced establishment has been ordered to make immediate improvements – and reportedly deep-cleaned the diner the day after the rat scandal.



Left shocked by the incident, the unnamed restaurant owner refused to speculate on whether the sickening dish was some sort of twisted prank.

The Wa Jer restaurant on Wah Sing Street opened just over a year ago and has so far not had any issues with vermin, he claimed.

Though he admitted that rodents run free in the city, he said the restaurant undergoes deep cleans every month.

The investigation by the Food and Hugiene department is ongoing.

A health department spokesperson said: “Regarding the suspected discovery of a baby rat in takeaway food, the department is conducting an investigation covering various aspects including food preparation, packaging, storage, and delivery.



“At this stage, it is inappropriate to jump to conclusions as to when and how the baby rat got into the food based solely on online video clips or the finding of a suspected baby rat in the food.”

Earlier this year The Sun interviewed a food safety officer on her filthiest food encounters.

Natalie Stanton has seen sex-mad chefs and rampaging rats – but one discovery left her sick to her stomach.

News.title: We fear we’ll be ‘first targets’ when 600 migrants overtake our town – huge detention centre lets them look in our homes
News.content:
ON OUR DOORSTEP We fear we’ll be ‘first targets’ when 600 migrants overtake our town – huge detention centre lets them look in our homes

RESIDENTS living just metres away from a new 600-person immigration centre fear they’ll be the “first targets” when migrants move in.

The Haslar Immigration Removal Centre [IRC] near Gosport in Hampshire is one of the closest IRCs to people’s homes in the country.



Locals have railed against the dust, noise, traffic and impact on house prices, brought on by the construction of the “appalling” IRC.

They claim their concerns about security and privacy have been overlooked.



The project has evolved since its proposal, with the original 130-person centre expanding to include three-storey blocks capable of housing 600 people.

David Robinson, 65, is a retired civil servant at the MOD who has lived at his home opposite the site for 20 years.



The Home Office claimed plans for the site always detailed a 600 person capacity.

David also raised concerns around privacy, but said that his complaints fell on deaf ears.

He added: “There will be 600 detainees – I’ll refer to them as detainees. The Home Office refers to them as residents but they’re not.

“We have got worries about the security for us all. It’s not like prison where the inmates have work like joinery or mail to keep them occupied. There will be 600 of them with nothing to do.

“And while some might be depressed or in a bad way, some could be hardened criminals from Albania. If they stage an escape we will be the first targets. We have worries about that.



“It’s also going to put massive strain on our medical system when people already have to wait six weeks to see a doctor.

“The Home Office say it’s not going to affect us because they have their own prefabricated medical room but if somebody in there has a heart attack or needs an x-ray, they’re going to need to go to the same hospital as everybody else.

“And if someone in there gets bail, where do they go? We don’t know who these people are.

“We’re all concerned about privacy. The high rise blocks will be 12 metres high and I’m only 17 metres from the fence.

“I accept we need IRCs but it really isn’t a suitable location. We’ve all complained about what it means for us but the government will just say it’s creating jobs and that money is going back into the local economy.



“Planning doesn’t really take into account how people feel. Wildlife has more rights than we do.”

The construction of the centre has been another ongoing issue.

David said: “It’s been about three years of this. A lot longer than we were told. They were looking at bringing 180 people in and said it would take six months. Our main opposition was about parking.

“But then they expanded the plans and it all kicked off. Instead of six months, it’s been three years of hell.

“I’m 20 metres away. We have vehicles parking opposite at 6am, we’ve had lorries reversing into the road, with three or four lorries being here at a time. It’s appalling.



“One of the lorries was a cement mixer that brought my telephone wire down and it had to be put back up.

“It’s been a constant battle. Now they want to put big blocks in to go up from 130 people to 600. The blocks will overlook all the properties on that side.”

Meanwhile, Andrew Hughes, 62, who is being forced to sell his house because his wife is sick and needs to go into care, has lost £50,000 after the property remained on the market for 18 months.

Andrew said: “It’s been an issue. I’ve had to sell my house for £50k less than what it would have been, but I had to sell because my wife is sick and is going into care.

“It took 18 months to sell. My wife’s very poorly and my daughter has adapted her house in the Midlands but it was very expensive.



“I haven’t found anywhere to live myself yet. If that hadn’t have been happening I’d have more money to help out with.

“I used to work over there. I worked in prisons and immigration for 37 years, and lived here for 12 years.

“It used to be an immigration detention centre but on a much smaller scale and it wasn’t open 24/7 like it will be. We had issues with parking but that was about it.”



And, Angela Bryant, 88, says her garden backs onto the centre and she worries people will be able to see into her home.

The retired BT telephonist said: “My garden backs out onto it. It will really harm the price of my house which won’t harm me but I’m leaving it to my daughter.

“It’s noisy and it’s going to get worse because the plan has just increased by 470 people. They will be able to see into my garden and my home when they go out for exercise.

“And there will be so much traffic. It will ruin the area.

“We have paid in all our lives, why should they get it? They shouldn’t be here in the first place.”



Graham Phillips, 75, has lived in Gosport his whole life but has struggled to sell his home because of the IRC.

He said: “I’m just fed up with it all. My house has been on the market for 10 months. It’s frustrating.

“It might sell if we drop the price down fast enough, someone might be willing it overlook the immigration centre, but that won’t help our children or our grandchildren.

“I was told it would be north of £700,000, but after three valuations it went down to £650,000. It’s got nowhere near that.”

He was offered £610,000 for his seafront property but the sale fell through.



He continued: “There will be three-storey buildings and a 24/7 bay carpark with a road going right past our garden.

“We just don’t know what it’s going to be like. We’ve never lived with a 600-person Immigration Removal Centre before.

“It used to have 130 people and you wouldn’t know it was there unless they were playing football on a Saturday afternoon.



“It’s the IRC that’s closest to residential homes anywhere in the country. I think there’s one in Oxford that’s a couple of hundred metres – but this is just metres away.”

It comes after swathes of masked “stop the boats” protesters descended on roads around the Port of Dover – bringing the town to a standstill on Saturday.

Holidaymakers and lorries were stuck in huge queues for hours as they battled to access the UK’s busiest ferry port during the anti-migrant rally.

Kent Police monitored the march but said no one was arrested, adding that the group had been dispersed by midday.

Far right activist Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo – an associate of Tommy Robinson – shared a video appearing to be from the protest.



The footage showed the phrase “blood is on your hands” seemingly scrawled near the port along with red paint.

Chants of “stop the boats” and “whose streets? Our streets” could be heard from the crowd during the chaos.

The Government condemned the behaviour of protesters who blocked the port “and the travel disruption it caused.”

Kent Police said no arrests were made after earlier confirming they had been “engaging with protesters” at the scene.

Asked about the Gosport IRC, local MP Dame Caroline Dinenage said: “Since announcing the expansion of Haslar to 600 beds the Government has done its utmost to avoid engaging with local people.



“Last week I invited the Home Office to a public meeting with residents but they failed to attend.

“The height of the buildings is a serious concern compounded by the fact it was revealed without warning at a small engagement session last year.

“Since then all planning decisions have been taken away from the local authority and there are limited opportunities for local people to have their say, something I have raised repeatedly with Ministers.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “We make no apology for significantly expanding our detention capacity which will see more than 45,000 additional foreign criminals and illegal migrants removed over the coming decade.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“All Crown Development planning applications require extensive engagement, and we encourage residents and stakeholders to share their views through the formal process.”



The Sun has contacted Gosport Borough Council for comment.

News.title: Moment jilted killer gets eyebrows plucked just hours after strangling his boyfriend to death in brutal murder
News.content:
THIS is the moment a jilted killer got his eyebrows plucked just hours after murdering his boyfriend.

Imran Uddin, 35, murdered Ismail Younis, 24, at home in Hockley, Birmingham, after a two-year campaign of coercive and violent behaviour.



Victim Ismail had told Uddin before the horror that he wanted to end the relationship after discovering the killer had been cheating.

CCTV showed Uddin in the hours that followed stalking his ex-partner around Birmingham city centre and repeatedly visiting his workplace.



Ismail was last seen on August 17 riding Uddin’s scooter to his home where he was strangled then stabbed multiple times even after he was killed.

After the murder, Uddin fled Birmingham and caught a train to Milton Keynes where he had family.

He was then captured calmly getting his eyebrows threaded and his hair cut.

Ismail’s body was discovered three days after the horror – with police launching a manhunt for Uddin.

He was arrested the next day but pretended to be shocked when told his partner was dead.

Bodycam showed him asking an officer: “Did you say murdered? They’re saying my partner got murdered, bro.”



Investigators found Ismail’s blood on Uddin’s phone, while the knife used in the murder had been washed and put back in its drawer at his home.

Uddin was found guilty of murder after a trial at Birmingham Crown Court and was jailed for life and ordered to serve a minimum of 21 years.

Detective Sergeant Jeanette Roberts, West Midlands Police Homicide Unit, said: “Ismail’s was life was taken by a coercive, controlling and manipulative partner.



“Enraged that Ismail had found the strength to take back his independence and end the relationship, he manoeuvred Ismail to his death.

“Uddin’s thoughts have only ever been for himself. He fled the scene and had no intention of facing the consequences of his actions.

“He has shown no remorse for his actions, or for the pain he has inflicted on Ismail’s family and loved ones.

“By his own agreement in court, he was a toxic narcissist who had to have it all his way.”

News.title: Heart-stopping moment boy, 5, dangles precariously from sixth-floor window after getting head trapped in bars
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a five-year-old boy dangles from a sixth-floor window and is rescued by a heroic caretaker.

Dramatic footage shows the young boy with his head trapped in window bars at a block of flats in Shuozhou, China.



The child can be seen hanging with his head wedged between the bars as he frantically kicks his legs and desperately tries to pull himself back up.

The courageous property manager, An Yilong, noticed the boy after he spotted residents below holding up a blanket in case the child fell.



He looked up in surprise and saw the five-year-old, who had shockingly been trapped for more than ten minutes.

An sprinted to the sixth-floor flat but nobody answered and he was unable to force the door open.



He quickly climbed out through the seventh-floor window and descended towards the boy.

He bravely gripped the child and held him firmly while firefighters raced to the scene.



A worried An feared the boy was going to fall at any moment as he was trapped up to his ears.

He kicked the grille to check how secure it was and swiftly scaled down to the child.

Less than 30 seconds later, firefighters arrived to free the boy.

A Shuozhou Fire Rescue Brigade spokesperson confirmed that firefighters had attended the incident and said: “Rescuing people is our duty.”

An joined them in lifting the youngster back through the sixth-floor window.



Supportive residents continued holding a blanket below in case the child slipped or fell.

The child was examined by medics and thankfully only suffered minor bruises.

The September 5 incident went viral on Chinese social media with many commending An’s actions.

An said: “I didn’t think about anything else at the time, I just wanted to save the child.”

The boy was left alone in the flat while his mother took his older sibling to a school parents’ meeting.



His family was quickly alerted of the situation by the property management team and rushed home.

News.title: Mum and stepdad wrongly jailed for 599 days after teen daughter ‘lied about sexual abuse’ as she faces prison
News.content:
‘LIES’ EXPOSED Mum and stepdad wrongly jailed for 599 days after teen daughter ‘lied about sexual abuse’ as she faces prison

FOR years a mother and her partner were wrongfully imprisoned after her teenage daughter lied about sexual abuse.

The wild miscarriage of justice was uncovered when the now 19-year-old woman fessed up to the fabrication after the pair spent 599 in custody and were sentenced to several years in prison.



In a new bombshell revelation, the young Swiss girl contacted the Zurich High Court and asked to speak with Christian Prinz, a senior judge.

When she was told he was unavailable, she left a simple message – she has something to tell him that she can’t tell anyone else.



When he returned the call, she revealed the accusations she made five years ago of sexual abuse and beatings against her stepfather and mother were false.

She confessed to Prinz that, as a 14-year-old, she initially “only wanted her freedom” and therefore lied.



The girl said never intended to file a police report but her biological father contacted the authorities and it snowballed from there.

The Zurich District Court sentenced the stepfather to 36 months in prison and the mother to 22 months in July 2021.

But, following appeals by the public prosecutor their sentences were drastically increased at the end of 2023.

The stepfather received 50 months for aggravated assault and multiple counts of child sexual abuse, and the mother 47 months for aiding and abetting.



As a result the authorities placed not only the then 14-year-old but also the mother’s other children in foster care.

Two days after her recent phone call confession, Prinz filed a criminal complaint against the young woman.

The Zurich City Youth Prosecutor’s Office subsequently opened criminal proceedings for false accusation, obstruction of justice, and unlawful deprivation of liberty.

The revelation has understandably sparked questions as to how a 14-year-old girl was able to dupe law enforcement and several experts to such an extent.

According to the Tages-Anzeiger the teen was reportedly known for lying at her school and spoke of hearing voices in her head was disregarded.



Several teachers testified that the 14-year-old had repeatedly lied in everyday school life.

Her apparent lying was evidenced in court by a WhatApp conversation from 2018 – a year before the arrest – when the then 13-year-old had been placed in a girls’ home after telling her friends about her abusive parents.

She later wrote to her mother and said: “Mommy after the holidays I have a meeting with the KESB (child protection services).

“I’m going to say I lied, that you didn’t hit me, that I was angry with you and had to lie.”

Experts also ignored the young girl’s mental health warning signs after she reported hearing voices and seeing threatening figures.



Despite this, her accounts of abuse did included seem genuine and included specific details – such as a white candle on the stove extension in the garden shed, which her stepfather had allegedly used during the assaults.

The girl also explained how she would protect herself from the alleged abuse by wearing several layers of clothing.

With these seemingly specific details four experts supported the fabricated abuse.

Their expert report was based on a review of three video interviews conducted by the Zurich city police and a single personal examination of the girl by the senior lecturer in psychiatry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The specialists attested to the accounts having a “high probability of credibility but in doing so, overlooked serious warning signs.



The mother and step-fathers convictions have now been overturned by the High Court.

News.title: Ports denied request to land 120 migrants in RNLI boats
News.content:
Requests to accept the landing of RNLI boats carrying 120 migrants intercepted off the Isle of Wight were refused by both Portsmouth harbour and Southampton Port.

When the migrants were landed on Sunday at Eastney, in Langstone Harbour, anti-migrant protesters blocked the road.

Associated British Ports (ABP), which operates Southampton, said it was not the closest port and it "did not have suitable reception facilities available".

The BBC understands the King's Harbour Master (KHM) Portsmouth also declined a coastguard request, but it would not comment directly on operational matters.

The protest followed a separate demonstration at the Port of Dover on the previous day.

The Langstone Harbour Master said the migrants were "recovered" onto two RNLI vessels in the vicinity of the Nab Tower.

They said they would have travelled at "quite a slow speed" to Langstone because the vessels were so overloaded.

An RNLI spokesperson said: "We are working with the relevant parties to understand the decision to deny access, and we are disappointed with the nature of the communication with our crews, who voluntarily give their time to save the lives of others at sea."

News.title: Harry and Meghan 'surprised' by King's letter making clear they remain non-working royals
News.content:
A spokesperson for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex says the couple were surprised to see a letter sent on behalf of King Charles clarifying that Prince Harry and Meghan remained non-working royals.

The spokesperson said the couple, who have recently moved back to the UK, "were a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance".

But royal sources say Prince Harry and Meghan were made aware of the letter, sent on Monday afternoon, before it was made public.

It is also understood a security committee, which includes Home Office representatives, is meeting this week to look at the level of taxpayer-funded security that should be given to the Sussexes who are now resident in the UK.

The Royal and VIP Executive Committee - known as Ravec - decides security for royals and public figures and Prince Harry has previously complained about a lack of adequate police protection in the UK.

The Home Office does not comment on such decision making - and would be unlikely to reveal the outcome of such a meeting.

"The UK government's protective security system is rigorous and proportionate. It is our long-standing policy not to provide detailed information on those arrangements, as doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals' security," said a Home Office spokesperson.

In terms of Prince Harry and Meghan being "surprised" by the King's message on Monday - it's understood that reflects the lack of time given to them to respond.

They were believed to have had only had sight of the letter about an hour before it was shared with the media. By the time his team had made contact with Prince Harry it's understood the letter was almost published.

News.title: Prince George attends first day at Eton College
News.content:
Prince George has officially started his first term at Eton College.

The 13-year-old, who is second in line for the British throne, was dropped off at the all-boys boarding school by his parents, the Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales.

The future king follows in the footsteps of his father in attending the elite private school, which has taught 20 British prime ministers and where fees are around Â£65,000 a year.

The BBC's royal correspondent Daniela Relph explains what the prince is likely to expect at his new school.

News.title: Trump shares misleading video of King and fainting worker
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has shared a misleading video on social media which appears to show King Charles shrugging and walking away from a man who fainted during a royal visit.

The footage, which has been edited, features in a video shared by Trump on his Truth Social platform which appears to show other world leaders being disrespectful. The video goes on to show a montage of clips where Trump is seen honouring fallen US troops, hugging veterans and shaking hands with law enforcement officers.

The clip of the King was taken from a longer video when, as Prince of Wales, he was visiting an Asda supermarket distribution centre in Bristol during the Covid pandemic in July 2020.

The full footage, which Trump did not use, showed Charles reaching out to the man as he fell before remaining close by as he received medical attention. The video posted by Trump edits out the King staying close to the worker.

Buckingham Palace declined to comment on the video. The White House has not responded to a request for comment.

News.title: Monty Don to leave Gardeners' World after more than 20 years
News.content:
Monty Don is to step down as the host of Gardeners' World after more than 20 years, the BBC has announced.

The 71-year-old, who is the programme's longest-serving head gardener, will leave at the end of the current series.

In a statement, Don said working on the show had been a "deeply rewarding experience," but added: "Now is the right time for a change."

The BBC said Don had "inspired and guided millions of viewers with his warmth, wisdom and passion for gardening" since joining the programme in 2003.

Don began presenting the programme at Berryfields, a rented garden in Stratford-upon-Avon, before it moved in 2011 to his own garden, Longmeadow in Herefordshire.

"Throughout that time - and around 700 programmes - I have had the privilege of sharing my own abiding passion for gardens and gardening with an equally passionate, and often equally knowledgeable audience," he said.

"That connection with millions, not just in Britain but across the world, who share a love of gardens, plants and the natural world is something I have always treasured and which I increasingly believe to be at the heart of a life well lived."

Don added he had "always relished the craft of programme making" and paid tribute to the "superlative BBC team" he worked with over the years.

"I look forward to continuing to work with and for the BBC on other projects, as well as following new avenues," he concluded. "And of course, I will still be gardening, dog by side, here at Longmeadow."

News.title: Iceland summons US ambassador over Trump's stars and stripes map
News.content:
Iceland has summoned the US ambassador after President Donald Trump posted a map on social media that appeared to show Iceland and several other countries covered by the American flag.

Trump posted the image on Truth Social on Monday, showing the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean covered in stars and stripes. The entire landmass was labelled "United States of America".

Iceland's foreign minister said the post was "completely inappropriate".

Trump's territorial ambitions have repeatedly strained relations with neighbouring countries, including his push to acquire Greenland and calls to make Canada the America's 51st state.

His post of the map did not include a caption and preceded a flurry of posts of maps renaming the US state of New Mexico as "New America".

Responding to Trump's post, Iceland's Foreign Minister ÃorgerÃ°ur KatrÃ­n GunnarsdÃ³ttir called in US ambassador to Iceland Billy Long, who formally took up the post last month, local media reported.

When an ambassador is summoned, it typically means they are being called for a formal meeting, where the host country will express displeasure over their government's actions.

The post also drew criticism from Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, who said on Monday that the position of Greenland's government and people had been made clear.

"The Greenlandic government and the Greenlandic people have said again and again that they do not want to be American," she told Danish news agency Ritzau in Nuuk.

"I hope no one is in any doubt about that, either in the United States or the rest of the world."

Trump's interest in Greenland has been a recurring theme on his social media accounts and in speeches since he took office again last year, claiming the island is necessary to the US to shore up its national security.

His post came shortly after the European Commission announced a â¬200m (Â£172m) investment in the Danish territory during a visit by Commission president Ursula von der Leyen and Frederiksen.

The European Commission said its investment would focus on education, internet connectivity, the use of raw materials in the country and hydropower energy.

Meanwhile, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico "is neither nor will be a colony or protectorate of any foreign country," after Trump's post.

"Proudly we are a free, independent, and sovereign nation," she wrote on social media.

News.title: Kane among three of England's World Cup stars to make Ballon d'Or shortlist
News.content:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is one of three England players nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham and Arsenal's Declan Rice join Kane, the favourite for the award, on the 30-player shortlist.

Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi, who is looking to win his ninth Ballon d'Or, has been nominated.

The 39-year-old scored eight goals as Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain in July, with Messi since retiring from international football.

Lamine Yamal is one of six Spain players that won the World Cup to be included.

Having scored the winning goal in the final, Paris St-Germain forward Ferran Torres, who joined the French club from Barcelona in the summer, makes the cut.

Back-to-back Champions League winners Paris St-Germain have nine players - excluding new signing Torres - nominated, including last year's winner Ousmane Dembele.

Real Madrid forwards Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr also make the shortlist, as do Arsenal defenders Gabriel and William Saliba.

The award is celebrating its 70th anniversary, having been created by France Football in 1956, and the winner will be announced at an ceremony in London on 26 October.

The "symbolic choice of venue" is in tribute to former England player Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the first Ballon d'Or.

News.title: Charli XCX says bye to Brat and Liam Gallagher's tambourine grin - Music Photography Awards 2026 shortlist
News.content:
Striking images of Oasis's reunion tour and Charli XCX bringing Brat to Glastonbury Festival are among the nominees at this year's Abbey Road Music Photography Awards.

The awards, which this year considered works by more than 24,500 submissions from 42 different countries, released a shortlist of 40 finalists across eight categories on Tuesday.

The likes of Kendrick Lamar, Fontaines DC, Tame Impala and Sombr also feature in the shots, while other images of stars including FKA Twigs have been selected - out of competition - for judges' awards.

All of the finalist photographs will go on display in the LED tunnel at entertainment complex Outernet London from 8 to 14 September.

These will include the five pieces picked out for consideration in the fan-voted music moment of the year award.

Voting is available online via the official website, external, and in person at the exhibition.

The winners will be announced at a ceremony at the London studios - made famous by the 1969 Beatles album of the same name - on 24 September.

News.title: Prince George begins first day at a rainy Eton College
News.content:
Prince George arrived on a rainy morning for his first day at Eton College, accompanied by his father and mother, the Prince and Princess of Wales.

Prince William and Catherine carried umbrellas as they brought George, wearing a jacket and tie, to be welcomed by the head teacher, Simon Henderson, and provost Sir Nicholas Coleridge.

"Welcome, good luck and enjoy," said the head teacher, shaking hands with Prince George.

They made small talk about the bad weather before the new pupil, parents and staff disappeared inside the historic school, where 13-year-old George will be a boarder.

George, who had travelled the short journey from his home at Forest Lodge in Windsor, was seen with his parents arriving at Eton's school yard, overlooked by the school's Tudor landmark of Lupton's Tower.

He was later photographed wearing the school's uniform, with black tailcoat, waistcoat and a stiff white collar.

The future king follows in the footsteps of his father in attending the elite private school, which has taught 20 British prime ministers and where fees are around Â£65,000 a year.

News.title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind
News.content:
English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.

The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.

The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.

Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.

The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025. The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.

Run by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Pisa tests assess teenagers on their ability to solve problems, think critically and communicate, before asking them a wider range of questions about their education in a questionnaire.

Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

England's schools minister, Georgia Gould, said the government wanted to "build on" the positive results and "go further so all young people leave school with strong literacy and numeracy".

News.title: I was fired from The Voice - I didn't want to leave, says Sir Tom Jones
News.content:
Sir Tom Jones has said ITV "fired" him as a judge on The Voice, and he did not want to leave as he "loves the show".

The 86-year-old singer from Treforest in Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, has appeared as an on-off coach on the singing competition since it premiered in 2012.

Following rumours that he may not return to the panel for the upcoming series, Sir Tom said the broadcaster decided a while ago, but he "was told recently".

He said on social media that he had been offered a reduced role - one he was "not thrilled" about.

The Voice confirmed Sir Tom would not be returning as a full-time coach for the new series.

A spokesperson for the show said: "We have loved working with Sir Tom Jones over the past nine years on The Voice UK.

"While he will no longer be a full-time coach on series 15, we continue to talk to Sir Tom and his team about his involvement in the next series."

In a social media post, Sir Tom said: "The reason given is because of a financial difficulty with insurance.

"They now say in the press they wanted to 'refresh' the show, and with a new coaching line-up there wouldn't be a chair for me.

"They are offering a much-reduced role where I would make an appearance but without being actually involved from the start, and I'm not thrilled about that.

"So the only thing I know right now is that there's never a good time to fire an 86-year-old who's still pretty good at his job."

The programme's 2027 series was due to begin production soon.

In the most recent series of The Voice UK, Sir Tom featured as a coach alongside McFly stars Tom Fletcher and Danny Jones, as well as US rapper Will.i.am and Destiny's Child singer Kelly Rowland.

Sir Tom has appeared alongside many famous coaches during his tenure on the show, including singers Jessie J, Olly Murs, Kylie Minogue and Rita Ora.

He has also mentored three winners on the programme, Leanne Mitchell in series one, Ruti Olajugbagbe in series seven and Anthonia Edwards in series 11.

News.title: Blind man sentenced for 150-mile drive while drunk
News.content:
A blind motorist who took his partner's car and drove for 150 miles (240km) at night while drunk has been handed a suspended sentence.

Anthony Hall, 50, who does not have a driving licence, was stopped by police on the M6 near Carlisle at 01:45 BST on 29 June after he was seen swerving the Vauxhall Meriva between lanes and onto the hard shoulder, a court was told.

Hall told police he had driven from his home in Huddersfield after he and his partner had drunk four bottles of wine.

Kirklees Magistrates' Court heard Hall, of Lees Close, had admitted charges including dangerous driving at a previous hearing and was sentenced on Tuesday to 36 weeks in prison, suspended for 18 months.

Hall had also admitted drink-driving, driving without a licence or insurance and taking a car without consent.

News.title: Pensioner with 'largest hoard' of child abuse images found in Scotland jailed
News.content:
A pensioner who amassed what is thought to be the largest collection of child sexual abuse material ever seized by police in Scotland has been jailed for four years.

Alan MacPherson, 83, from Stenhousemuir, was found to have more than two million images on various electronic devices after his home was raided in 2025.

More than 805,000 were identified as depicting child sexual abuse - much of it in the most serious category - while the overwhelming scale of his collection meant much of material was not checked and categorised.

MacPherson was told by Sheriff Mayram Labaki that the scale of his crime was "exceptional".

The sheriff said: "The quantity [of images] was so great that a substantial proportion could not be examined and categorised by forensic examiners.

"Every image records the abuse or exploitation of a child. The possession and circulation of such material perpetuates that abuse."

MacPherson will also be supervised for three years following his release from jail and placed on the sex offenders register for life.

The former volunteer archivist with the Royal Scottish Country Dance Society previously admitted downloading the material over a 14-year period.

Sheriff Labaki added: "Your views towards your offending and your victims are unconscionable.

"I refer specifically to the passages in the [social work] report where you state that not only were the children consenting, but they were willing participants.

"Your attitude is unremorseful".

News.title: Attacks victim's death 'potentially preventable'
News.content:
The death of a student killed in the Nottingham attacks was "potentially preventable", a public inquiry has heard.

Barnaby Webber - along with Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates - were killed by Valdo Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, on 13 June 2023.

On Tuesday, ahead of closing statements to the Nottingham Inquiry, external - which is examining the killings - the inquiry was told a "more rapid administration of blood products" could have meant Barnaby's death was "potentially preventable".

The inquiry also heard documents found in a bin at Calocane's address contained a list of explosives, which was not disclosed by Nottinghamshire Police until June this year.

A panel of medical professionals assessed the emergency medical response on the day of the attacks to assess "survivability", the inquiry was told.

In their assessment, the panel noted the hard work of the emergency responders in their care to the victims.

The panel found if blood products had been administered to Barnaby earlier and more rapidly, it could have increased his chances of getting to hospital with enough of a heartbeat to undergo surgery.

However, multiple other rapid and particular steps would have had to have taken place for him to have survived.

The inquiry heard Barnaby had a less than 50% chance of surviving his injuries, characterised as "potentially preventable", while Grace and Ian's deaths were "not preventable".

The families of the victims sobbed as the assessments were read out by counsel to the inquiry Rachel Langdale KC. Grace's father, Dr Sanjoy Kumar, left the hearing room.

Langdale said Nottinghamshire Police found the documents in a bin at Calocane's former property in Burford Road in Nottingham.

He wrote bullet points on one page about explosives under the heading "thoughts", including TNT and nitrate fertiliser.

Langdale said: "This piece of paper listing thoughts about a number of explosives was not identified or taken into account at the time."

She added it had not been made available by police to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) or to psychiatric experts.

Calocane was evicted from the Burford Road address on 11 June 2023 and travelled to London, before returning via to Nottingham shortly before midnight on 12 June, a day before his killings, the inquiry heard.

News.title: Borrowers expecting mortgage rates to drop have hopes dashed
News.content:
Nearly all the major mortgage lenders in the UK have announced increases in the cost of home loans in recent days.

Analysts are uncertain over whether there are more to come, but are urging people who need to find a new deal to act now.

Someone whose five-year deal is coming to an end faces paying more than Â£5,000 more a year on their next deal under a typical rate, if they borrow the same amount of money.

Many lenders allow people to lock in a new deal six months before their current one comes to an end, with an opportunity to switch if the costs come down before it kicks in.

"Borrowers expecting mortgage rates to drop in the coming weeks have had their hopes dashed," said Rachel Springall, from financial information service Moneyfacts.

"It is still essential borrowers do not delay seeking advice to navigate the mortgage maze."

News.title: What we know about the journey of the Portsmouth migrant boat
News.content:
Protests in Portsmouth broke out after the arrival of migrants who had come from France on a small boat - after a much longer journey than usual.

BBC Verify has been using ship-tracking websites to monitor activity in the English Channel at the time the migrant boat made its crossing on 6 September. BBC Verify correspondent Merlyn Thomas reports.

News.title: Real Madrid v Inter Milan LIVE: Jose Mourinho makes Champions League return against former side at Bernabeu
News.content:
Mourinho lauds Inter ahead of Champions League clash

Real Madrid host Inter Milan on the opening night of the Champions League as Jose Mourinho faces his former team on his return to the Bernabeu.

Mourinho has set his sights on winning his first Champions League with Real Madrid, more than 16 years after leading Inter to the Treble in the season before he arrived for his first spell in the Spanish capital.

The Champions League was the one prize that eluded Mourinho in his first spell at Real Madrid, who are under pressure to deliver this season after two trophyless campaigns led to the return of Mourinho after 13 years.

Following a stunning World Cup with France, star forward Kylian Mbappe will also be determined to win his first Champions League title, after watching his former club Paris Saint-Germain win back-to-back European crowns since he joined Real Madrid.

Lonnie Bunch is stepping down from the leadership of the Smithsonian Institution following a tumultuous year in which President Donald Trump tried to remake the portrayal of U.S. history by the Smithsonian museums and other cultural entities.

Bunch said in a news release Tuesday that he was departing the position he had held since 2019 “with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude.” The Smithsonian said he would leave the post at the end of the year.

Bunch’s departure comes two months after a White House report branded the leaders of the Smithsonian Institution, especially at the National Museum of American History, as radical activists who cannot be trusted, an indication that Trump could be preparing to install his own team.

Anthea M. Hartig, the first female director of that museum, faced growing scrutiny from Trump and other Republicans over the summer after the White House Domestic Policy Council’s report saying the museum’s leadership doesn’t tell history “in a way that is inspiring, unifying, and worthy of our great republic.”

Three weeks after the report’s release, Trump ordered his administration to install signs in front of the U.S. history museum telling visitors that some of the exhibits are inaccurate. Hartig pushed back, telling lawmakers during congressional hearings that the report "does not fairly or accurately characterize the full body of work at the museum.”

There had been speculation that firings were in the offing. Trump doesn’t have the power to fire leaders at the Smithsonian with the swiftness he’s managed at other top cultural institutions in Washington, most notably the Kennedy Center, where a board of his supporters named him chairman.

The Smithsonian operates outside the executive branch and museum directors report to Bunch, who is subject to oversight from a Board of Regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts, a bipartisan group of lawmakers and so-called citizen regents.

Roberts, who serves as Smithsonian’s chancellor, said in a release that Bunch had “pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story.”

The White House did not immediately return a message seeking comment.

The Smithsonian has been under examination by the Trump administration since 2025 as it has focused on the images and messages presented to the public as the nation approached its 250th anniversary.

A March 2025 executive order, Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History, led to signs being changed at federal parks, exhibits being altered or in some cases removed, and military bases being renamed. Trump specifically cited the National Museum of African American History and Culture and argued that the Smithsonian as a whole was engaging in a “concerted and widespread effort to rewrite our Nation’s history.”

Several months later, the White House ordered a wide-ranging review of the Smithsonian museums and exhibitions before the country’s 250th birthday, with a goal of aligning the institution’s content with Trump’s interpretation of American history.

In a letter sent to Bunch at the time, the White House detailed the steps it expected the organization to take as part of the announced review. The examination is of all public-facing content, including social media, exhibition text and educational materials, to “assess tone, historical framing, and alignment with American ideals,” according to the letter.

That review initially focused on eight museums — the National Museum of American History, the National Museum of Natural History, the National Museum of African American History and Culture, the National Museum of the American Indian, the National Air and Space Museum, the Smithsonian American Art Museum, the National Portrait Gallery and the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden.

Rory McIlroy has acknowledged that there are logistical challenges associated with Donald Trump visiting this week’s Amgen Irish Open, but said players would just "keep our heads down and play".

The United States president is in Ireland this week for an official two-day visit, with expectations that he will attend the DP World Tour tournament hosted at Trump International Golf Links Doonbeg.

Although extra security protocols will have to be put in place for the visit, McIlroy responded: "Who are we to say no?"

Speaking to BBC Northern Ireland, the world number two said: "It’s going to be different with him being here but we’re here to play a golf tournament and it’s a good golf course so we’ll keep our heads down and play.

"I think the weekend when he’s here crowds will be limited, obviously there’s a lot that goes on.

open image in gallery Trump is set to pay a visit to the Irish Open ( Getty )

"Logistically it proves some challenges, absolutely, but at the same time if he wants to come and watch the Irish Open who are we to say no?"

Trump has been an occasional visitor to golf events, most notably attending last year’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage.

McIlroy and Trump have played golf together in the past, and the US president sent a congratulatory message to McIlroy when he defended his Masters crown in April.

“Congratulations to Rory McIlroy on another Great Championship, The Masters!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

“He performed tremendously under intense pressure, something which few people would be able to even think about doing. With each year, Rory is becoming more and more a LEGEND!”

The following month, chose to skip the Cadillac Championship at Trump Doral after being invited to a state dinner during the visit of King Charles at the White House by Trump.

Explaining his decision, McIlroy said: “I know how fortunate I am and so lucky to be in this position in life and sometimes you have to enjoy the perks because I know that this isn’t going to last forever.

“There’s going to be a day where I’m not sitting up here and I’m not competing for major championships and I’m not doing what I’m doing. So I guess while I’m doing it, I have to enjoy it.”

More than 400 flights were canceled on Tuesday due to a technical issue in Britain's air traffic control system, the flight monitoring website Flightradar24 reported.

Britain’s National Air Traffic Services said a problem had been identified in its flight processing system and engineers were urgently working on the issue, which affected flights across the U.K.

In an update, it said it had “implemented a fix and our flight system is starting to recover.”

About 425 flights to and from U.K. airports, including Heathrow, were canceled, affecting services operated by multiple airlines, including British Airways, EasyJet, KLM and Lufthansa.

The affected airports, which also included Stansted and City in London, as well as airports in Manchester, Birmingham and Scotland, said the technical issue caused disruptions. They warned passengers to check the status of their flight with their airline.

Budget airline EasyJet said some of its flights were “unable to operate” and that the system failure caused “delays to flights across Europe.”

Some passengers took to social media to complain about being stuck on the tarmac for hours. Many expressed frustration about a lack of communication from airlines.

Heathrow's website showed that many short-haul flights departing for European destinations had been canceled or delayed.

Arriving flights did not appear to be affected. It was not immediately clear what caused the technical problem.

What about a hexagon?” is the sincere response that comes from Karen Brockman when her grandmother tells her a woman can be any size or shape she wants in the third season of Outnumbered. “Can they be a triangle?”

As much as diet culture was alive and well in the 2010s, the family sitcom was, of course, joking. Cut to 2026 and it feels like it somewhat predicted the future.

Last week, Marks & Spencer – a trusted brand for women to find hosiery and underwear – followed in the footsteps of Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand Skims to offer a “hip boost” bodysuit.

Essentially, a leotard with slits to stuff full of padding to give the wearer a surgery-free brazilian bum lift (BBL) that follows in the footsteps of M&S’s stick-on nipples – and padded bum shorts.

So, yes. A woman can be any size or shape that she wants – more so than ever before. Stick a nipple on here, boost your bum up there, or vanish almost entirely with GLP-1’s. Whether through surgery or shopping, bodies are marketed as malleable, and as such, everything from big boobs and big bums, to clavicles and collar bones are a cyclical fashion trend.

Curves for autumn! Ribs for spring!

Nothing exemplifies the periodic shift in what’s considered (as Marks and Spencer say in their marketing materials) the “perfect shape” as well as attempting to pad a bum back on to a smaller frame. This is a frankenbody, designed to make those after it strive – with both their money and their minds – after something entirely unnatural.

Down the surgical route, you can even get so-called zombie filler; a dead person’s fat pumped into your body to bring some of the plump back.

open image in gallery The bodysuit retails for £28 and follows in the footsteps of Kim Kardashian’s Skims’ sculpt wear ( M&S )

From a business perspective, the high street is more than happy to follow fashion’s lead. Thin has increasingly become “in” again, with smaller Hollywood physiques increasingly present and plus-size representation making up just 0.3 per cent of FW26 looks. In a recent report, it was predicted that one in eight Britons will be on weight loss drugs by 2027.

For those not on the jabs, this national shrinkage can present logistical challenges, as the high street’s stock of plus-sized clothing is scaled back.

Comparing listings for new dresses this July and August to 2024, retail data platform Edited found that there are now fewer styles above a size 18 available, particularly in the largest sizes of each style. At M&S, new dresses in an 18 or above fell by seven per cent. And while John Lewis had more plus-sized dresses available than the year before, the largest sizes made up three per cent less of its range.

open image in gallery Kardashian has been credited with popularising a surgically enhanced body type as the new norm ( PA Wire )

Edited also found that H&M had discontinued its 3XL and 4XL sizes (22-24 and 24-26) since 2025, while XXL was down three per cent from 13 per cent in 2025 and XL was two per cent lower, while sizes between XS and L had risen by three per cent. Meanwhile, Mango’s dresses between size 16 and 20 dropped from 6.6 per cent in 2025 to 0.5 per cent in 2026.

Both H&M and John Lewis said in a statement at the time that their selections reflected customer demand. Meanwhile, an M&S spokesperson denied their sizing decisions were driven by GLP-1s.

There may well be people in the world with a naturally snatched waist and boosted hips somewhere – but the bodies we see most commonly on our screens are working harder than ever to appear that way.

Four years ago, Kim Kardashian was squeezing into Marilyn Monroe’s archival dress by wearing a sauna suit to lose weight. Last May, she arrived at the Met Gala with a fibreglass breast plate accentuating the breasts, waist and hips she’d worked day and night to shrink.

open image in gallery The star underwent an extreme weight loss regime in 2022 before selling padded shorts in 2025 ( Alamy/PA )

Body shapes are nothing new. Anyone with a media diet of women’s magazines, Trinny and Susannah and Gok Wan knew the difference between pear, hourglass, and apple – and which swimsuits suited them – before hitting double digits. But, at least, they were somewhat based on something near to a woman’s body, rather than a work of contortion.

The cycles, it seems, only continue to keep spinning more swiftly; fast fashion for the flesh that women, famous or not, struggle to keep up with. Writer and body image content creator Stephanie Yeboah has expressed frustration at the fashion industry for satisfying the “nostalgia for curves” through design, rather than “rejecting thinness outright”.

"As someone who lives in a bigger body, this 'trend' is frustrating to watch play out," Yeboah told Marie Claire when asked about the AW26 shows that employed corsets and padding to create shape on slender models.

“Fashion wants the idea of my body — just not my actual body. It feels like curves are being aestheticised at the exact moment they’re being erased, which is a contradiction in and of itself,” Yeboah said.

The industry, she added, wants things both ways: to sell “the fantasy of femininity and shape” while maintaining the preference for thinness.

open image in gallery Inflated silhouettes dominated the runway at AW26 Fashion Week shows ( PA )

Half a year on, it’s clear that trend has trickled down to the high street.

“It’s a moving target of perfection, so women can never be comfortable in their body” says Dr Martine Robson, psychologist and co-author of Postfeminism and Body Image. “It looked like liberation, when there was suddenly a lot more representation of different body sizes and shapes.

“But in a way, it was still the same old story: that women are the wrong size, shape, appearance — but we can sell you the solution.”

“It’s political,” Robson concludes. “If you give women an impossible task, and get them really engaged in that, then you keep them out of the other spheres of life, don’t you? There’s only so much energy to go around.”

And there is no such this as the perfect shape.

Rory McIlroy admits there are some logistical challenges associated with Donald Trump visiting this week’s Amgen Irish Open but said the players would just “keep our heads down and play”.

The United States president is in Ireland this week as part of an official two-day visit and it is expected he will attend the DP World Tour event being hosted at Trump International Golf Links Doonbeg.

Extra security protocols will have to be put in place for the visit but McIlroy said: “Who are we to say no?”

The world number two told BBC Northern Ireland: “It’s going to be different with him being here but we’re here to play a golf tournament and it’s a good golf course so we’ll keep our heads down and play.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.
