“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign 40-goal striker, 16, from Premier League rivals days after transfer window slammed shut
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have snapped up another rising star from their Premier League rivals as their aggressive academy recruitment continues.

The Gunners have signed 16-year-old prospect Mylo Bernard from Crystal Palace, bolstering their youth ranks.



Bernard has penned a pre-contract with Arsenal, joining as a first-year scholar ahead of signing professional terms when he turns 17 next year.

The highly-rated striker scored more than 40 GOALS for Palace’s academy teams last season, catching the eye of clubs across the country.



His performances also earned him a call-up to Palace’s Under-18s team, where he netted six times in the U18 Premier League despite his young age.

Bernard is also an England youth international and has scored four times in his eight caps for England’s Under-16 side.

Bernard took to Instagram to close the chapter on eight years at Crystal Palace, he wrote: “After eight unforgettable years at Crystal Palace, I have decided to say goodbye.

“I have grown up playing for Crystal Palace and it has provided so many wonderful moments in blue and red.

“Crystal Palace has shaped me as a person and a player becoming a crucial part of my life.

“It has always been a pleasure playing at the club over the last few years and this part of my journey will always have a place with me.

“I will forever be grateful for the past eight years I’ve had with this club.”

The Gunners announced the capture of Manchester United duo James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye earlier this month.

Meanwhile, Elijah Upson – son of former Arsenal and West Ham star Matthew Upson – crossed the North London divide to join from Tottenham earlier in the summer.



Arsenal have also picked up future stars from other leagues, too.

Igor Tyjon has joined from Backburn Rovers, Axel Donczew has arrived from Cardiff City and Phoenix Blayney has signed from Northern Irish club Larne.

Sports.title: Man Utd suffer bitter transfer blow as top target Lewis Hall agrees new FIVE-YEAR contract with Newcastle
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have suffered a hammer blow after top target Lewis Hall agreed a new five-year deal at Newcastle.

The left-back, 22, will become one of Toon’s top earners after committing his future to the club until 2031.



The news comes after Sun Sport revealed on Wednesday that talks were underway over an extension with his previous package due to expire in 2029.

Now England international Hall has followed team-mates Lewis Miley, Sven Botman and Harvey Barnes in agreeing a new contract.



Sun Sport understands that United have identified him as the long-term successor to Luke Shaw.

However, they were knocked back this summer and told emphatically he was not for sale when they approached the North East club over a potential transfer.

The Red Devils could still make another move next year, though this development significantly strengthens Newcastle’s hand regarding any sale.

The Magpies brought in £228m this summer by selling captain Bruno Guimaraes plus fellow stars Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali but were adamant the ex-Chelsea man was going nowhere.

Sporting director Ross Wilson has admitted that more big hitters will have to be sold over the coming windows – though the ultimate ambition is to hang on to their most-prized young assets.

But he says the club are embracing the player-trading model in order to reach their ambition of becoming title challengers by 2030.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He told Sun Sport last week: “We hope they’re [star players] with us on our journey to 2030. But we’ve got a player trading model as well. Who knows what 2030 looks like in terms of the squad? I’m sure there’ll be players in the 2030 squad that aren’t in the 2026/7 squad – I hope there are anyway.

“Of course we want to have players here who are on a journey with us but equally if some of those players’ journeys go at rapid speed they might go somewhere else. But of course that’s normal, that’s part of football.”

Sports.title: Full list of Ballon d’Or nominees revealed including five Premier League stars as Harry Kane favourite for coveted award
Sports.content:
IT’S Ballon d’Or season, and the nominees for the most prestigious award in football have been revealed.

Thirty names have been announced on the male shortlist, with five Premier League stars included and Harry Kane is the favourite to land the golden ball.



Kane being the favourite feels apt, as the awards will take place in London this year on the 26th October, for the first time in history as they are usually held in Paris.

The men’s shortlist includes five players from the Premier League, with Declan Rice, William Saliba and Gabriel representing the Champions, Erling Haaland representing Manchester City, and Bruno Fernandes flying the flag for the red side of Manchester.



Former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella and previous winner Rodri are also nominated, with the latter also one of the favourites to win it.

It is one of the most open Ballon d’Or races we have seen in years.

There is no standout candidate, with the World Cup and Champions League campaigns playing a huge part in the voting, as well as looking at players who have had absurd individual campaigns, like Kane.

Lionel Messi will be in the running to collect a record NINTH trophy, having been nominated for his 17th Ballon d’Or this year.

He led Argentina to the World Cup final once more, and had a stunning international campaign as well as a good season for Inter Miami.

Several PSG players could also challenge him, including last year’s winner Ousmane Dembele, and the only player to win both the Champions League AND the World Cup – Fabian Ruiz.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arguably PSG’s best player last season, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia should also be in the running, but not participating in the World Cup with Georgia could hold him back.

World Cup winners Rodri and Lamine Yamal will also be high up in the final rankings, with the latter also starring as Barcelona won the league title.

You can also not rule out Kylian Mbappe, who scored heaps of goals for Real Madrid and for France at the World Cup, but could be held back by a lack of trophies.

Then there is Kane, who won multiple domestic trophies, a pretty good World Cup with England as they reached the semi-finals, and one of the best individual campaigns that the world has ever seen with a stunning 73 goals – only ever beaten by Messi in his prime.



England stars Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood are among the 30 candidates for the Women’s Ballon d’Or, as well as WSL stars Mariona Caldentey, Kerstin Casparij, Yui Hasegawa, Melvine Malard, Manaka Matsukubo, Vivienne Miedema, Alexia Putellas, and Khadija Shaw.

Aitana Bonmati, who has won the award for the past three years is absent from the 30-person shortlist, after missing a large chunk of last season with a fractured fibula for Barcelona.

Her former Barca teammate Alexia Putellas, who now plays for the London City Lionesses, is now the favourite for the trophy having scored 22 goals and bagging 12 assists and winning the Nations League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana, Copa de la Reina, and the Champions League.

As for the Kopa Trophy Lamine Yamal is among the nominees and could win a THIRD consecutive award.



Joining him in the nominees list are Ibrahim Maza, Eli Junior Kroupi, Warren Zaire-Emery, Lennart Karl, Yan Diomande, Ayoub Bouaddi, Karim Alajbegovic, Johan Manzambi and Pau Cubarsi.

Sports.title: What are the patches that players are wearing on their sleeves in the Champions League?
Sports.content:
THE new Champions League campaign gets underway TONIGHT, and fans have spotted that certain players are wearing a special patch on their kit.

The designs are new for this year’s European competition as part of a collaboration between Uefa and Fanatics.



Five English clubs are beginning their journeys in the Champions League this season, with Aston Villa starting first tonight with a trip to Club Brugge.

SunSport has all the information on the special patches that players are wearing in this year’s tournament.



What are the patches that players are wearing on their sleeves in the Champions League?

The patches in this year’s Champions League are for players making their debuts in the competition.

The new innovation comes amid Uefa’s partnership with sports merchandise company Fanatics.



Each patch will be given to Fanatics after matches and distributed to their trading card company Topps.

The one-of-a-kind debut patches will then be turned into signed trading cards.

Similar debut patches were worn by the likes of Noni Madueke and Anthony Gordon at the World Cup in North America.

And the initiative is now set to hit European club football, beginning as the League Phase gets underway tonight.



Stars set to make their Champions League debuts include the likes of Manchester United duo Bryan Mbeumo and Carlos Baleba.

Debut patches are also set to feature in the women’s game, starting with the 2027-28 Women’s Champions League campaign.

A similar initiative has already been rolled out in the NBA.

And a rookie debut patch card signed by 2025 No1 pick Cooper Flagg is expected to fetch a staggering $5million (£3.7m) next week.

Uefa initially signed with Fanatics in 2022 and the two parties have agreed a long-term extension to 2033.



President Aleksander Ceferin said: “Renewing our partnership with Fanatics for Ueefa club competitions reflects the strength of our collaboration and our shared commitment to delivering best-in-class products for fans and collectors globally.

“Fanatics know how to make big moments feel special. We are excited for what’s next.”

Sports.title: Hansi Flick sends message to Anthony Gordon after flying start for Barcelona following £69m transfer from Newcastle
Sports.content:
HANSI FLICK has called on Anthony Gordon to score more goals despite the Barcelona star’s electric start to the season.

Gordon, 25, is yet to find the back of the net since his £69.3m move from Newcastle this summer, but he has been setting them up for fun.



The England international has racked up four assists in his first four games, becoming only the third player to do so in the Spanish top flight this century.

But despite Gordon’s impressive playmaking, Barcelona boss Flick has urged the winger to add some goals of his own to his game.



Flick said: “I think as a striker, from his side, you want to score goals. He has had some chances and he missed them.

“But he has made the final pass to prepare the goals and this is also very important.”



Gordon scored 10 Champions League goals for Newcastle last season, a tally only bettered by Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

But his league return was less impressive, scoring only three times from open play across the whole season.

Ahead of Barcelona’s opening Champions League league phase clash against Feyenoord tomorrow evening, Flick is confident that the goals will come for Gordon once again.

The German manager added: “He will score goals, I have no worries about that.

“He’s doing good. I am happy with his performances in defence, but also in the offence. I think it is a good situation for him, but also for us.”

Barcelona are eyeing their first Champions League in over 10 years and Gordon’s teammate Lamine Yamal, has name-checked the former Toon ace as a reason they can finally get over the line.

Yamal said: “We already have the motivation to win the Champions League. I believe the whole team is motivated.

“The Champions League always motivates you because it is the most special competition.



“It motivates the good players too, like Rodri, Gordon, [Karim] Adeyemi, Gabriel [Jesus] and Joao [Cancelo].”

Gordon is just one of a host of superstar names that joined Barcelona this summer in a bid to finally win the Champions League again.

Sports.title: 'Most pressure in the NFL' Finally Allen's time to win Super Bowl?
Sports.content:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady is under the most pressure in the NFL as he seeks to lead Josh Allen's side from 'bridesmaid to bride', says Sky Sports' Phoebe Schecter.

The Bills renew their Super Bowl quest this season having endured more playoff agony earlier this year when they were beaten by the Denver Broncos in overtime of January's Divisional Round clash.

It had been deemed a premature end to one of their best opportunities yet to end prolonged Super Bowl agony, with Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs absent from the playoffs for the first time since 2014 and the likes of Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow also nowhere to be seen.

Sean McDermott was subsequently fired after nine campaigns in charge, with Brady being promoted to head coach from his post as offensive coordinator.

"Josh Allen will have had a say with Joe Brady coming in and taking on that role," said former Bills coach Schecter on Inside the Huddle.

"It was just odd at the time in terms of how it happened, that kind of firing in order to promote from within."

Allen's Bills have suffered four Divisional Round exits and two AFC Championship Game defeats since 2020, four of those losses coming against the Chiefs.

Their 73 victories in that period are notably more than any other team in the league, Allen consistently spearheading one of football's most potent offenses.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Inside The Huddle podcast Neil Reynolds, Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter give their predictions on who will make the Super Bowl in 2027

Buffalo sought to strengthen their quarterback's aerial options by trading for Chicago Bears wide receiver DJ Moore, who hasn't recorded a 1,000-yard campaign since 2023.

"You look at what DJ Moore does for the team when you bring him in," Schecter continued. "That already elevates an offense that has never really had a star receiver.

"They're still trying to keep that mentality, but you pair that with a fantastic running game. We saw James Cook all last season taking over, but it's a very interesting that we have so many teams in the AFC that were having a similar conversation around with your Lamar Jacksons, your Joe Burrows - when will these guys win a Super Bowl?

"That of all the teams the most pressure is on Joe Brady in terms of the expectation is for him to get to a Super Bowl because they've always been the bridesmaid, never the bride.

"It'll be fascinating to see how he manages that pressure, especially as they move deeper into the season. But everyone feels good about it. You've got a new stadium, you've got a new excitement around it and that kind of rejuvenation."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Inside The Huddle podcast, Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold discuss what a Patrick Mahomes return would look like after tearing his knee ligaments in December

The Bills also hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator to oversee a new-look unit that saw the likes of Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White depart in the offseason.

"Leonard is the key to this whole deal," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold. "Jim Leonard is a brilliant young coach, and if he can get that defense just a little bit better than it's been and better balance, this could be Buffalo's year."

Is this Burrow's time?

Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals stake their only claim as NFL 'nearly men' alongside both Allen's Bills and Jackson's Baltimore Ravens.

The Bengals have missed out on the playoffs for three straight years and managed just one postseason appearance since their defeat to the Los Angeles Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

Burrow, who has missed 16 games through injury over the last three seasons, demanded urgency from his team this offseason as he seeks to maximise, when healthy, one of the most explosive passing attacks in football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter discuss the prospect of Myles Garrett to the LA Rams and if he can lead them to Super Bowl glory

"He said it himself, we all know he's been injured so many times coming into this season, or they've had some big injury within the team, but the time is now and they've got to chase that success," said Schecter.

"The biggest complaint last year was how they were putting so much money into this defense and they were probably the worst performing defense.

"But bringing in Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, you get Kyle Dugger from the Patriots, you've got a smart defense. You've got a safety who can now organise everybody.

"They've got to be able to go down and capitalise on having this fantastic trio on offense with Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and go attack it. This city needs it.

"The fan base are so desperate for it and you don't have an endless clock with Joe Burrow, especially seeing his injury rate over the past few seasons."

Sports.title: Kane, Rice, Bellingham among Ballon d'Or nominees but no Ronaldo
Sports.content:
The 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees have been announced as the best male and female footballers of the year are identified.

Harry Kane is among those in the running for the men's prize and is the bookmakers' favourite to be crowned.

Kane scored 73 goals last season, enjoying one of the best campaigns of his career and he could become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane is joined the 30-man long-list by international teammates Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.

Other Premier League stars like Bruno Fernandes, Erling Haaland, Gabriel and William Saliba are among the other players included.

Lamine Yamal, Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe will be the likely challengers to Kane for the illustrious award but there is no nomination for Cristiano Ronaldo despite winning the Saudi Pro League with Al-Nassr.

England stars Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood are among 30 players nominated for the women's Ballon d'Or.

When is the Ballon d'Or ceremony?

The 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony will take place on October 26, 2026 in London.

How are the Ballon d'Or winners decided?

The shortlist was compiled by a group of journalists from France Football working alongside French sports publication L'Equipe.

For the men's Ballon d'Or prize, winners are decided by a voting system involving one journalist from each of the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations.

Each journalist casts votes for their top 10 players from the 30-player shortlist. The 10 players are awarded 15, 12, 10, seven, five, four, three, two and one point based on where they rank.

If players are tied on points, then whoever has the most first-place rankings from the 100 journalists finishes ahead on points. If that is tied, then it's the most second-places and so on.

Journalists are encouraged to consider three factors when deciding their vote:

Individual performances, decisive and impressive character

Team performances and achievements

Class and fair play

For the women's Ballon d'Or, the same process applies but only journalists from the top-50 ranked nations are invited to vote.

Sports.title: Nelson: Fury vs Joshua is less and less likely
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has 'every reason' to stand his ground in negotiations for the Tyson Fury fight, which is looking 'less and less likely', says Sky Sports expert Johnny Nelson.

Promoter Eddie Hearn has stated that Joshua signed a contract to fight Fury at Wembley amid an ongoing dispute over the location of the fight, with Madison Square Garden in New York also being considered as a potential venue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn released a statement last week saying that Wembley is still being considered as the host venue for the fight

Nelson believes Joshua and his team are even more determined to get the fight entirely on their terms after the unified champion displayed his vulnerabilities while being floored twice in his comeback win over Kristian Prenga.

"No, I don't [think Fury vs Joshua will happen]," Nelson told Sky Sports.

"Unless the other side decides to lay down and say: 'You know what, we'll give you what you want'. No, I don't.

"I think Anthony Joshua and [his promotional team] Matchroom Boxing have every reason to stand their ground.

"Firstly, because you look at Anthony Joshua's last performance; that doesn't fill you with confidence.

"Secondly, because they've signed a contract and so, if they're going to embark on this fight, they're going to say: 'This is what we asked for; if you don't want to do it, that's a you problem'."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury's manager Spencer Brown admits he is concerned about the delay in announcing the fight

Hearn has revealed that he held fresh talks with London Mayor Sadiq Khan in a bid to ensure the two Brits fight in front of a home crowd, despite concerns over a later curfew for Wembley Stadium.

But Nelson believes Joshua and his team's insistence that the terms of the contract should be followed could mean the bout is not agreed.

"I think it's less and less likely to happen," said Nelson.

"They have put the pressure on. Sadiq Khan has got involved, and he's said: 'We're going to do everything possible to make this happen and bring this business to the UK'.

"Anthony Joshua has said to Eddie Hearn, 'We've got a contract; stick to the contract. No nudging; this is what we're doing.

"Unless Turki Alalshikh [who is organising the fight] and Tyson [Fury], say: 'All right, let's do this.'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearn revealed he has spoken to Mayor of London Sadiq Khan about bringing the fight to Wembley

"I think that the chance of the fight happening is less and less.

"If I were Team AJ, I'd do the same, because AJ's performance didn't fill me with complete and utter belief that this will go our way.

"I'm quite sure if it was the other way around and Tyson Fury was the one who performed as AJ did in his last fight, even though he fought the night before, I'm quite sure this wouldn't be as much of an issue.

"I think it just adds to the issue."

Sports.title: Mac Allister 'very sad' over no new Liverpool deal
Sports.content:
Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister is "very sad" that he has not been offered a new contract and admitted he had "options to leave" in the summer.

The 27-year-old confirmed he has two years left on his Reds deal, which he signed when he joined the club in the summer of 2023.

The Argentina international's unhappiness comes after fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch penned new long-term contracts this year.

Speaking ahead of Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid, Mac Allister told a pre-match press conference: "There was a chance [he could have left the club in the summer].

"As everyone knows, I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which makes me very, very sad.

"Everyone can see I give my 100 per cent for this football club, every single day in training and games. Of course I can have very good games, very bad games like everyone. I always give my best.

"And I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts, and that makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I didn't get mine.

"Of course, there is still time. The fans don't need to worry because I will give my 100 per cent until the last day I'm here.

"We will see what happens. There were options to leave this summer, and I think right now I'm in the right club and I have the mindset to give my 100 per cent for this club."

Image: Mac Allister won the Premier League with Liverpool in 2024/25

Questioned whether talks were ongoing over a new contract, he replied: "Maybe. I don't know. It's going to depend on how I perform during this year. They are right to make the decision as well, but hopefully they change their minds."

Asked whether he was given a reason for no new contract, he said: "Not really. There wasn't any direct conversation with me - it was with my agent.

"I don't want to say things they never said, but what I got from my agent was that they were not in a position to renew me.

"It's really sad because we won a Premier League together, we've been through difficult times together, and I always give my best. We will see what happens, but of course it makes me a little bit sad."

Mac Allister was linked with a move to Manchester City this summer.

Questioned on why he did not leave Anfield, he replied: "Because this is the right club. I love being here, and this is something special."

He added: "I love this club, I love being here, I love the fans.

"As a player, you can be at a club for a long, long time and you don't really realise where you are - that doesn't happen to me.

"I know very well that this is an amazing club, that this city has something very special and I love being here."

'I've not spoken with Iraola over new deal'

Image: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (left) has not held any talks with Mac Allister over a new deal

Mac Allister has started in Liverpool's last two league games, which saw them draw at home to Nottingham Forest and then win at Ipswich to help give new Reds boss Andoni Iraola an unbeaten start.

But Mac Allister revealed he has not spoken about his future with the Spaniard, whom he had plenty of praise for.

"Definitely since I've come to pre-season and I worked under Andoni, I could see something special," he said.

"He's a really good coach. He knows very well what he wants to do, and we are trying to get there.

"I haven't had any conversations with him about it.

"When I see the way he wants us to play and train, I think this can be a successful season so that's why I think this is the right club and the right moment to be here."

Image: Mac Allister has two years left on his Liverpool deal

Iraola called Mac Allister an "important" player and says there is still time for his contract situation to be resolved.

He told a press conference: "We all have personal situations with different contracts. The important thing is he wants to be here and continue here.

"We haven't been together a long time but he has been an important player and I rate him very highly.

"Definitely there is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations."

He added: "I am very happy with his performances - he played really well on Friday [at Ipswich] and I hope I can help him to still improve.

"He is very experienced player who has already achieved massive things, but I hope I can help him in his development as a player and then everything goes well then those problems will definitely be solved".

Mac Allister was a key part of Liverpool's 2024/25 Premier League title, having also won the Carabao Cup the season before.

Asked whether he has anything to prove this season amid doubts over a new deal, the 2022 World Cup winner replied: "Not really because I'm always the same guy and player, and I'm not going to change.

"I think in these three years at the club I've done very good things. We went through difficult times; we went through a lot of things. We won a Premier League, we won a Carabao Cup, so for me it's a very successful period of my life.

"I don't think I have to prove something, but of course I have to show the level that I can perform, and hopefully that's the case."

Is Mac Allister in decline?

Sky Sports' Adam Smith:

Mac Allister's overall quality ratings have dipped season on season since he joined Liverpool in the summer of 2023, according to data provider Gradient.

Gradient rates each metric according to the quality of a player's actions, rather than simply the quantity of them.

What next for Mac Allister after contract admission?

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Vinny O'Connor:

"No scapegoating, no talk of anyone being thrown under the bus - just genuine upset that he's the odd one out.

"Alexis Mac Allister is the only one of Liverpool's 'first-choice' title-winning midfield trio from 2025 to be told the club is not in a position to offer new terms.

In the last six months, Ryan Gravenberch has signed up until 2032 while Dominik Szoboszlai has committed until 2031.

"Mac Allister says he's happy for them, they deserve it, but, reading between the lines, he's asking the question as to why is there nothing on the table for him?

"There's an irony that he was speaking before facing Atletico Madrid, one of the sides he's been linked with. There was also talk during the summer window of interest from Manchester City.

"He freely admitted he could have gone. There were opportunities. But, he stayed because Liverpool, in his mind, remains the right club for him and one that he is fully committed to, whatever the contract situation.

"Last season wasn't his best and there is an argument to say there is a sensibility about the decision taken on football reasons.

"So is this the beginning of the end of his time at Anfield?

"Not necessarily. In his manager's words: "There is still a lot of time to talk about these contract situations."

"Mac Allister's own take is that things can change, along with an admission he has to show the level at which he can perform.

"That is not necessarily a bad thing for Iraola, having a player of Mac Allister's quality with the added motivation of proving his worth.

"And, just as the tone was different to Mo Salah at Leeds last season - even if the openness with which Mac Allister spoke was no less surprising - it feels a similar outcome is far from set in stone at this stage.

"Yes, there was surprise in the room, but maybe we're not in for another drawn out transfer saga."

Sports.title: Ferrari vow to come back stronger after Monza 'failure'
Sports.content:
Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza.

There were big expectations for Ferrari at their home event after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were quick in Friday practice, only to miss out on the front row in qualifying before a dismal race on Sunday.

Hamilton dropped from fourth to 10th after going side by side with Leclerc at the first chicane, going through the gravel at Turn 2, which he was unhappy with.

Then Leclerc had a huge crash on the third lap which wrecked the car and left the Monegasque driver with initial eye issues.

Hamilton was up to third at one point in the race but lacked outright pace and finished sixth behind both Mercedes, Red Bull's Max Verstappen and both McLarens.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle and Nico Rosberg debate who was at fault for the near-collision between Lewis Hamilton and Leclerc at Monza

"We will come to Madrid with all the energy that we need to do a good result," said Vasseur.

"It's true that Monza, for us, even if I spend the week to say that it's a normal race, it's not, as you can imagine. With all the Tifosi, we were expecting to give them something else as a big thank you for the support and the enthusiasm that they have.

"We all have the feeling to have failed something, but be sure that we will come back much stronger."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leclerc crashed out the of the Italian Grand Prix

Vasseur: Ferrari missing pure power despite engine upgrade

Ferrari introduced their second and final engine upgrade of the season but were still slower than the Mercedes-powered cars on the straights.

Straight-line speed has been Ferrari's biggest weakness, something which will not be an issue around the new twisty Madrid circuit, and Vasseur says he was "not expecting" to make up the power-unit deficit to Mercedes.

"When you have a lack of pure power, then you start to play with deployment, to try to compensate in the straight line," he said.

"But if you deploy more somewhere, for sure you will deploy less somewhere else. Then you are going in the wrong spiral to try to play with this when you are fighting.

"Honestly, it's not about deployment. Even McLaren, they were playing a little bit Friday and Saturday morning. In the end, we are missing pure power."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rosberg says it is 'not feasible' for Ferrari to favour Hamilton at this stage of the season

After the first Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) review earlier this year, Ferrari were deemed to be more than four per cent behind benchmark engine manufacturer Red Bull.

It meant Ferrari could make two engine upgrades this year, and also for 2027, when the Scuderia will have a new engine.

"The process of the engine is mega long. The chassis you can make an upgrade from one day to the other very quickly and come back into the pace," said Vasseur.

"On the engine, the process is mega long because the lead time of the parts is long and the cost cap is not easy - you have to produce the engine for the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton says the team are 'too late' to implement any sort of 'Ferrari priority'

"And if you want to start to do the development, you have to produce a new batch of engines. We are not expecting to recover with ADUO 1 or ADUO 2. We are doing small steps.

"If you make a small step on the engine, keep in mind that behind us, it was hundredths of a second. In terms of position, even if you make a couple of horsepower, it's a good step on the grid. Now we will have a new engine next year. For sure, the target is to catch up as soon as possible."

Sports.title: Football Daily | Forget the hype machine – it’s the minnows who offer European interest
Sports.content:
CAN’T TOUCH THIS?

♫ ♪ 🎵 🎶 The champions ♫ ♪ 🎵 🎶! Bigger Cup is back, baby! Red-hot action from the world’s premier club competition across Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Bigger Vase and Tin Pot clubs must wait for their slice of European action until after an international break almost as long as the Geopolitics World Cup itself. Rather like Gianni Infantino’s North American investment roadshow, Bigger Cup, with its revolving Swiss system, 36 teams reduced to 24 following 114 matches, has become baggier than MC Hammer’s trousers [now there’s a reference for the young readers – Football Daily Ed]. Back in Clive Tyldesley’s ITV pomp, ties such as Liverpool v Atlético, Napoli v Arsenal, and Real Madrid v Inter moved the dial, filling boozers and column inches.

Now, paywalled away and despite the whir of Darren Fletcher and Ally McCoist’s unrelenting hype machine, these nights can feel more routine, a golden goose not so much terminated as gathering dust on the mantelpiece. A trinket retaining monetary value but not as cherished as it once was. That holders PSG are so minted they can afford to play separate teams across Ligue 1 and Bigger Cup says much about modern football, where clubs and competitions have become content providers feeding an attention economy. In this case, that attention will run a deficit until, just like the GWC, the juice is in the knockout stages. There are, though, different dimensions to take solace in.

Uefa suits would argue, for all the ennui surrounding Manchester City facing Real Madrid 14 times since 2012 – they don’t meet in this year’s group – Bigger Cup offers pluralism in the presence of minnows and newcomers. Think of them like plucky non-league clubs in the FA Cup third round. There’s Serie A arrivistes Como, a cracking away trip for fans, with Cesc Fàbregas as well-regarded young coach, and Nico Paz as a potential successor to Lionel Messi. No pressure. Austria’s Lask, from Linz, will make their group stage debut, having sunk Celtic in the playoffs and featuring the talents of former Mangotsfield, Wealdstone, Yeovil, Chesterfield, Swindon and St Mirren defender Miguel Freckleton.

Azerbaijani football has previously been represented by Qarabag but Sabah are the new Azeri force, from a small municipality on the banks of the Masazir, an actual salt lake. Their coach, Valdas Dambrauskas, will be reunited with Manchester United. Using the funds from a small, Who Wants To Be A Millionaire win on Lithuanian TV in 2002, having phoned a friend, gone 50-50 and asked the audience, he emigrated to England, eventually becoming a coach at United’s soccer schools in 2004, beginning his long personal journey back to Old Trafford. Then there’s Slovan Bratislava, coached by a 2009 Big Cup winner in Yaya Touré, who succeeded Vladimir Weiss in the summer. Touré becomes the first African coach to lead a team in the competition’s group stage, ending a wait that has lasted far too long. Throw in the return of Bodø/Glimt and questions of whether the club from the Arctic Circle can keep on doing interesting things and not everybody has to be a billionaire’s plaything, though come the spring, it will certainly help.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Rob Smyth fromn 5.45pm BST for hot Bigger Cup coverage of Club Brugge 1-2 Aston Villa, followed by Niall McVeigh keeping an eye on Porto 1-1 Manchester City, plus Daniel Harris on the rest of Tuesday’s action.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I can’t change it. The truth is that I really don’t care. I know how to analyse football, I know why [they have won Bigger Cup twice]. I don’t know everything about football but I know more than most” – Kylian Mbappé, there, not wanting to get bogged down in the details as to why PSG have been Europe’s best team in the two years since he left.

Sports.title: More than 100,000 people add names to complaint against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
More than 100,000 people have added their names to a complaint against Gianni Infantino, alleging the Fifa president has “at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty” through his interactions with Donald Trump.

The Reboot Fifa campaign was launched before the World Cup with the aim of delivering “the biggest complaint Fifa has ever received” over the organisation’s alleged failings of governance. The campaign has since extended the scope of its accusations to include the overturning of the red card awarded to Folarin Balogun at the tournament and the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The complaint was submitted on Tuesday to Fifa’s ethics committee and in a supporting letter the organisers of Reboot Fifa,the advocacy group Fair Square, call on the committee to take action. An original complaint, submitted in December of last year, failed to receive a response from the committee but has gained the backing of the Norwegian football federation and 50 European parliamentarians.

“The fact that 100,000 individuals added their names to this call for accountability is clear evidence of mounting public concern,” the Fair Square letter said. “As the independent judicial body tasked with the critical task of upholding the ‘integrity and reputation of football’, the ethics committee must not only act, it must be seen to act with appropriate haste, transparency and rigour.”

The letter lists eight incidents that form the basis of the Reboot Fifa complaint, which Fair Square alleges “provide compelling evidence that the Fifa president has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself with the US President.”

The incidents include the Balogun affair – where Trump admitted he asked Fifa to review the US striker’s red card – and the FFE scandal. They also cite the awarding of the Fifa peace prize to Trump, Infantino’s involvement in Trump’s Board of Peace in the Middle East and the Fifa president’s promise to work with Trump to “make not only America great again but also the entire world”, an act Fair Square suggests shows a failure to remain politically neutral.

Fifa, when approached for comment, pointed to a statement first published a month ago. “It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” the statement said. “Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”

Fifa confirmed on Sunday that Infantino would be seeking re-election for a fourth and final term next year despite pressure from Uefa and criticism from within the Asian confederation and Concacaf (the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation). Uefa has called on Infantino to stand down and recently announced its intention to pursue criminal claims in the US over the FFE plans.

Sports.title: Harry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or while Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood have been nominated for the women’s award.

The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October. Ousmane Dembélé, who won the men’s award last year, has been nominated again, as has his France teammate Kylian Mbappé, who made history when he overtook Lionel Messi for all-time World Cup goals (22) at this summer’s tournament.

In the women’s field, two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay are among the favourites to succeed Aitana Bonmatí. Winner of the past three awards, Bonmatí did not make the cut after missing most of the season through injury. The Spaniard returned at the end of Barcelona’s quadruple-winning season that included another Champions League title.

Kane is odds-on to win the men’s award after a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup for England, a tournament where Bellingham and Rice also shone, the latter also playing a key role in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for the Premier League title.

Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite to win the award, followed by his club and international teammate Rodri. Messi, who has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, is on the shortlist after guiding Argentina to a runner-up finish at the World Cup and winning Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.

Russo finished third in last year’s voting and enjoyed another successful individual campaign, scoring 24 goals in 40 club appearances. Manchester City captain Greenwood lifted the Women’s Super League and FA Cup last season.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ Liverpool did not offer him a new contract
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister has said he feels “very sad” after Liverpool declined to offer him a new contract and admitted he rejected the chance to leave this summer.

Mac Allister revealed unhappiness over his contract situation before Liverpool’s Champions League opener against Atlético Madrid on Wednesday. The Argentina midfielder has two years remaining on his deal and believes he is effectively playing for a new contract having been informed no extension is on the table. Mac Allister confirmed he had offers to leave – Real Madrid and Manchester City were among those linked – but chose to stay because Liverpool can accomplish “something special” this season under Andoni Iraola.

“There was a chance [to leave] of course, like everybody knows,” said the 27-year-old, clearly keen to get the matter off his chest. “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very sad. I think everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club, every single day in training. Of course I have good games and bad games, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts, which makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me sad that I didn’t get mine. Of course there is still time [to be offered a new contract]. Fans don’t need to worry because I will give 100% until my last day. We will see what happens. There was options to leave this summer. I think right now I’m in the right club.”

Liverpool signed Mac Allister for a cut-price £35m in June 2023 by activating a release clause in his Brighton contract, which meant he was on a lucrative salary from the moment he arrived at Anfield. He claimed a new deal from Liverpool “is going to depend on how I perform during these years,” although he will be approaching 30 by the time his existing contract expires.

Asked why he chose to stay at Anfield this summer, despite his obvious discontent, Mac Allister replied: “Because this is the right club, that’s why. I love being here, this is something special. I feel we can be successful, what I want is to win trophies, and I think we have the right players and the right mentality to do great things, but everyone had to be on the same page.”

Mac Allister’s negotiating position would not have been at its strongest this summer after a disappointing season under Arne Slot, although he enjoyed a fine World Cup with Argentina. Iraola suggested Liverpool’s decision on Mac Allister might not be final.

The head coach, who will take charge of his first Champions League game on Wednesday while Diego Simeone leads Atletico for the 129th time in the competition, said: “I don’t know how much my players earn. I know how to improve my players, to help them win games. The same with Alexis and everyone else. He is very experienced player who has achieved massive things but I hope he can develop as a player and if all goes well those problems will be solved.”

Sports.title: Premier League clubs face losing lucrative sponsors if unlicensed gambling firms banned
Sports.content:
Half of the Premier League’s 20 clubs have sponsorship or advertising deals with unlicensed gambling companies that could be illegal next year under plans being developed by the government.

An eight-week consultation on proposals to ban sponsorship from gambling companies not licensed in the UK closes on Wednesday, with licensed operators such as Ladbrokes and William Hill pitted against the Premier League in a battle that could cost clubs tens of millions of pounds.

The league is understood to be lobbying against a ban on the grounds that the services offered by primarily Asia-facing betting companies and online casinos are not available in the UK, although anyone with a VPN can open an account and place a bet in minutes.

Analysis conducted by the Guardian has found the number of top-flight clubs who have commercial relationships with unlicensed operators has risen from six to 10 over the summer.

The increase is likely to have been influenced by the league’s decision to impose a voluntary ban from this season on front-of-shirt sponsorship deals with gambling companies.

Everton announced a new three-year sleeve sponsorship deal with the crypto casino Stake.com, and Fulham moved their sponsorship with SBOTOP from the players’ shirts to their training kit, while eight other clubs including Chelsea and Tottenham have commercial deals that include perimeter advertising at their stadiums and/or player branding.

One company, 8XBet, which is licensed in the Caribbean island of Curaçao, has deals with Chelsea, Newcastle, Aston Villa, Ipswich and Coventry.

Unregulated betting has grown considerably in recent years, with unlicensed operators earning £379m from users in the UK in the first half of 2025 according to the Campaign for Fairer Gambling, giving them 9% of Britain’s £8.2bn online gaming marketplace, up from 2% in 2022.

The government has moved to clamp down on unlicensed operators because they do not offer the customer protections such as affordability checks and spending limits provided by regulated betting firms, and the growth of the unregulated market has been linked to financial harm, addiction and suicide.

Everton’s sponsorship deal with Stake has been seized upon by campaigners given that Andy Burnham is a fan of the club and attended their opening game of the season against Crystal Palace.

One of the UK’s biggest betting companies, Entain, which owns Ladbrokes, has written to all 10 Premier League clubs linked to unlicensed operators this week and its letter to Everton makes reference to Burnham’s position.

“The risk to football, sport integrity, and society is real,” the letter states. “Unlicensed operators are not required to offer the safeguards that licensed operators must, including Gamstop self-exclusion, deposit and spending limits, and affordability checks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Ladbrokes’ owner says Andy Burnham would ‘become a billboard for unregulated gaming’ in his team’s current strip. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

“This removes the protections most likely to prevent consumer harm, meaning vulnerable customers unfairly pay the price for the partnerships that their clubs make.

“Everton’s association with Stake.com is particularly at odds with the prime minister’s longstanding support for the club. It seems unimaginable that, having made his government’s opposition to unlicensed gambling agreements clear, Andy Burnham would become a billboard for unregulated gaming by wearing the club’s current strip.”

In correspondence with operators the gambling minister, Vicky Foxcroft, is understood to have made clear that the government plans to introduce the ban next year, although it will face pressure from the Premier League to allow existing contracts such as Everton’s to run their course.

The league’s insistence on protecting a significant revenue stream for the clubs is understandable but its reluctance to combat unlicensed gambling operators also contains an element of risk.

There is growing evidence that unregulated betting companies are a main fund of pirated sports rights through advertising. The growth of illegal streaming poses a potential threat to the Premier League’s £12bn TV rights deals.

The Campaign for Fairer Gambling’s 2024-25 national report highlighted the symbiotic relationship between sports piracy and unlicensed gambling, with 89% of illegal streams in the UK featuring adverts for black market bookmakers.

Football club sponsorship also appears crucial in driving punters towards the unregulated market, with a Frontier Economics study cited in the government’s consultation saying sponsorship deals are the second-largest driver of consumer awareness of unlicensed operators after social media advertising.

Sports.title: Champions League is fertile ground for new managers – but knowhow could be key later on
Sports.content:
A delve into the history of the Champions League shows that managers can and do win in their first season at a club, but also that experience matters. Which makes it interesting, given that tenures for the 2026‑27 crop range from newly appointed coaches to one with almost 15 years in charge. Some have managed more than 100 matches in the competition, others none.

It gets under way on Tuesday with 14 of the 36 clubs led by managers who have been in the role for less than a year. It cannot match the turnover of the Premier League, in which 11 of 20 managers were appointed in 2026, but the tenures of the head coaches involved this season break down neatly.

There are also 14 managers who have been in charge for at least two years. This leaves eight in the middle, who qualified for the Champions League in their first full season at their club and now get to show what they can do.

Being new to a team is no barrier to winning. Many who have led sides to the ultimate European club glory did so in their first campaign. Both Chelsea’s Champions League triumphs were secured by managers who got the job the same year. Carlo Ancelotti began both of his stints at Real Madrid by helping them to become champions of Europe in his year one, and in between Zinedine Zidane won three Champions League trophies on the bounce when he first managed the club.

Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique also won the competition with Madrid’s great rivals, Barcelona, at the earliest opportunity. Barcelona’s current manager, Hansi Flick, ended his first season at Bayern with a treble. Liverpool fans will hope Andoni Iraola can emulate his countryman Rafael Benítez by winning the Champions League immediately after settling into the Anfield hot seat.

Despite these examples making a decent case for new managers winning the competition this season, betting markets are favouring the more established coaches.

And predictably enough, Paris Saint-Germain are the favourites with bookmakers, but it has nothing to do with this being Luis Enrique’s fourth season at the helm. The two‑time defending champions have a deep squad and face nothing like the domestic demands of their rivals in other top leagues.

Barcelona, Arsenal and Bayern Munich make up the top four in the betting, with their managers also among the 13 longest-serving as the league phase begins. This contrasts with the next quartet of likeliest champions, all of whom have managers who took charge this year.

But do not assume freshness in the role automatically equates to inexperience. Real Madrid’s new manager, José Mourinho, has recorded 160 matches in the competition, the fifth most in history. Ancelotti leads on 218 Champions League games, ahead of three of the Premier League’s five “big beasts” of management: Alex Ferguson (206), Guardiola and Arsène Wenger (both 191). Mourinho and Jürgen Klopp (102 matches, seventh most) are the other members of modern English football’s most heralded managerial quintet.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Only Mourinho is involved in the Champions League this season and he will savour being the new kid on the block who is also the old hand. Mourinho will be confident of going past the last 16 for the first time since 2014 given the talent at his disposal.

The eight managers he will face in the league phase have collectively managed fewer Champions League games than he has. Indeed, the combined total of the 24 least experienced managers in the competition adds up to fewer than Mourinho will bring to Madrid. These relative rookies are not only managing outsider, either. Inter’s Cristian Chivu has 10 Champions League games under his belt, which is more than the managers of Manchester City (six), Manchester United (one) and Liverpool (none).

As the competition gets under way, the key number is 16. That tally of points in the league phase has proven enough to secure an automatic spot in the last 16. Whatever a manager’s level of experience, the first target is to finish above the playoff places. After that, Champions League knowhow could prove vital.

Sports.title: ‘Girl’s day’ controversy reignites debate over how women are treated in South Korean football
Sports.content:
It was a comment allegedly made by a referee during a WK League match that became one of the biggest controversies in South Korean women’s football. What began as an on-field dispute involving South Korea’s all-time top goalscorer, Ji So-yun, has since developed into a wider debate, prompting a response from the Korea Football Association and raising questions about the treatment of female players, the structural set-up of women’s football in Korea and accountability within its governing bodies.

It was around the 31st minute of the Suwon FC Women v Seoul City Hall game on 28 August when the incident happened. Suwon’s former Chelsea midfielder Ji appealed for a foul after what she felt were repeated rough tackles by the opposition. The female referee, Bae Sun-young, is then alleged to have made, over the officials’ radio system, a remark interpreted as referring to menstruation after describing Ji as “sensitive from the start”. Ji says she overheard the comment and footage from the game shows Ji visibly upset as she talks to the referee. Ji was shown a yellow card after confronting the official. In frustration Ji threw a water bottle as she approached the Suwon bench. Bae walked towards Ji, appearing to reach for a red card before deciding against issuing one, showing a yellow instead.

After the match Bae denied making the remark, saying later that it had been a private conversation between match officials. The KFA’s refereeing department has said that the word “period” was not used and that the comments were not directed at Ji, but there have been reports that the term “girl’s day” was used instead.

View image in fullscreen Ji So-yun was shown a yellow card after confronting Bae Sun-young. Photograph: KWFF

After the match Suwon asked the Korea Women’s Football Federation and the KFA to look further into the matter. The KFA has now begun disciplinary proceedings and said: “Considering the seriousness of the matter, we decided to refer the case to the fair play committee in accordance with referee regulations.” The KFA’s fair play committee will listen to explanations from those involved and will review the incident. It will then determine disciplinary action based on the outcome.

The KFA further announced that it will use this incident as an opportunity to prevent similar events and strengthen education to create a culture of respect for players, referees, and participants in the WK League.

The Korea Pro-Footballers Association said it does not see this as a mere dispute on the pitch, but a serious human rights violation and abuse of refereeing power. The organisation called for Bae’s expulsion and a complete overhaul of the refereeing system, characterising the alleged remark as sexual harassment.

The controversy has revived scrutiny of the KFA’s previous treatment of women’s football. Last year, the women’s national team threatened to boycott the 2026 Women’s Asian Cup over what the players described as discriminatory treatment. Players said they faced long journeys, were forced to stay in “inadequate” accommodation far from training grounds and felt their conditions were evidence of discrimination compared to those of their male counterparts. In a statement the team said they would suspend all training related to the tournament if the KFA did not respond to their letter. The KFA said in February the matter had been “resolved”.

With the investigation still under way it may be some time before the fair play committee reaches a final decision. Yet the incident has become about far more than Ji’s confrontation with a referee and has brought back into focus long-running concerns about the treatment of female players, and renewed questions about the KFA’s accountability. And that is no bad thing.
