Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has learnt from trusting volatile Premier League boss with key Arsenal decision
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has learnt from his mistakes by sending Ethan Nwaneri on loan to Borussia Dortmund.

That's the view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who expects the Arsenal youngster to thrive in Germany after a bumpy ride on loan at Marseille during the second half of last season.



2 Nwaneri has joined Dortmund on a season-long loan Credit: Getty

Nwaneri started promisingly with the French giants, where Mikel Arteta was happy to send the attacking midfielder to work under 'really courageous manager' Roberto De Zerbi – but De Zerbi's departure just weeks after Nwaneri's arrival threw a spanner in the works.

And Brassell thinks Arteta ought to have been more wary of De Zerbi's 'combustible' nature which might have precipitated his Marseille exit.

'A bad error'

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he said: "I think Mikel Arteta has learnt from the mistake he made with loaning Nwaneri to Marseille, because he sort of pinned his hopes on De Zerbi [who took over at Tottenham in March].



"De Zerbi wanted a No.10 to build the team around, but obviously De Zerbi was also on the edge of the volcano and Arteta should have realised that tying his player's fate to a combustible coach – who I think people around Marseille knew might not be that far off a complete rupture – [wasn't the best move].

"That was a bad error and that cost Nwaneri a little.

"I'm sure, on a human level, it was a growth experience for him – whereas with Dortmund, [manager] Niko Kovac is, I think, secure and in a good place, but really their idea of making the team younger and developing players, that's Ole Book the sporting director as well.



"So I think there's more of a balance, more of a calm at Dortmund, even though it's an equally enormous club. And that should really help him.

"I think he's got lots of other good young players that he can click with. This is a very different profile to the Marseille squad where it was loads of old dogs, I think you can say, on many occasions.



"Of course, they have some younger players as well, but the way they lent on expensive imports from the Premier League I don't think was a particularly positive thing for them."

But Dortmund should be a much more beneficial environment for Nwaneri, believes Brassell.

2 Nwaneri scored twice in 11 appearances for Marseille last term Credit: Getty

"It's completely different at Dortmund," he concluded. "They're playing a lot of games, including the Champions League as well. He'll get a lot of opportunities.



"I think this move is really going to work for him."

Dortmund's English influence

Nwaneri, 19, is one of two young English players in the Dortmund squad.

He's joined by Jobe Bellingham, who followed in his brother Jude's footsteps by signing for the eight-time Bundesliga champions last year.

And Nwaneri is off to a good start with BVB, playing an important part in a late match-winning own goal as his new team fought back from 2-0 down to beat Hoffenheim 3-2 on his debut last weekend.

The England Under-21 international, who became the youngest player in Premier League history when he made his Arsenal debut aged 15 years and 181 days against Brentford four years ago, will be hoping to feature again when Dortmund host Villarreal in their Champions League opener on Tuesday.

Sports.title: James Rodriguez on the brink of surprise move to second-tier club
Sports.content:
James Rodriguez on the brink of surprise move to second-tier club

James Rodriguez is reportedly closing in on a move to Serie B side US Avellino.

The ex-Real Madrid star has been a free agent since June following a brief spell in the USA having left Minnesota United.

4 Rodriguez last stepped onto a pitch at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

Rodriguez spent just over three months with the MLS outfit before leaving to prepare for the World Cup.

But he could now be set to end his four-month spell without a club, having been offered an intriguing route back into the game.

Rodriguez set for Italy switch?

According to Spanish outlet Marca, Rodriguez is set to join Italian second-tier side Avellino.

As per the report, the Colombia star is currently in talks with the Serie B side, with an agreement close to being reached between both parties.

Financial terms are yet to be finalised, with this the last obstacle between the playmaker and a move to Italy.

Should Rodriguez go through with joining Avellino, he will be managed by a familiar name to football fans.

Legendary former Italy and AC Milan defender Alessandro Nesta is the current manager of the Wolves.

The 2006 World Cup winner took charge of Avellino in June, signing a two-year deal with the Campania club.

Marca's report states that Nesta has held talks with Rodriguez himself, as he looks to convince the Colombian to help inspire a Serie A promotion charge.

Avellino finished eighth in Serie B last term, the last available play-off place, but were then eliminated in the preliminary round.

4 Italy great Nesta's latest managerial role has seen him take charge of Avellino Credit: Getty

4 Rodriguez failed to score in eight appearances for last club Minnesota United Credit: Getty

They currently sit fifth in the Italian second division after the first three matches of the new season, winning twice and drawing once.

James Rodriguez's career

With Rodriguez closing in on a move to Italy, he looks set to join the 14th club of his senior career.

The attacking midfielder burst onto the scene at the 2014 World Cup, when he starred in Colombia's run to the quarter-finals.

He scored one of the goals of the tournament, a stunning volley against Uruguay, and netted another five times while also providing two assists to win the Golden Boot.

Later on in the same summer, Rodriguez moved to Real Madrid in a £63million deal, and went on to spend six years on the Spanish giants' books.

He made 125 appearances overall for the Spanish giants, and registered 37 goals and 42 assists as well as winning both LaLiga and the Champions League twice.

4 Rodriguez previously spent a year in English football at Everton Credit: GETTY

Rodriguez spent the 2017/18 and 2018/19 seasons on loan at Bayern Munich, scoring 15 goals to help clinch back-to-back Bundesliga titles.

In September 2020, the playmaker joined Everton as he reunited with former Real Madrid boss Carlo Ancelotti.

He enjoyed a strong season with the Toffees, scoring six and assisting nine goals in 26 appearances across all competitions throughout the 2020/21 campaign.

However, Rafael Benitez took over as manager in June 2021 - a move Rodriguez has since revealed effectively spelled the end of his time in Merseyside - and he departed for Qatari outfit Al Rayyan in September of the same year.

Rodriguez has had a nomadic career since then, moving to Greek side Olympiakos in 2022, before leaving and spending a year in Brazil at Sao Paulo.

A return to Spain with Rayo Vallecano followed in the 2024/25 campaign, and he then moved on to Mexican outfit Leon, before an eight-game stint in MLS with Minnesota United earlier this year.

Sports.title: FA overturns two red cards from same bad-tempered Championship clash
Sports.content:
FA overturns two red cards from same bad-tempered Championship clash

Millwall midfielder Jenson Metcalfe and Bolton's Josh Sheehan have had their red cards from their recent Championship clash overturned on appeal.

The pair were sent off after clashing late on in Millwall's 4-0 win over the Trotters last Saturday, which led to a huge brawl between both sets of players.

4 Sheehan was shown a straight red card following a run-in with Millwall's Jenson Metcalfe Credit: Getty

4 The scuffle happened in the closing stages of the match Credit: Getty

Tempers flared after a rough challenge between Metcalfe and Sheehan in the 86th minute.

Sheehan ended up on top of Metcalfe, with his shin pressing against the back of his opponent’s neck.

The Millwall midfielder then appeared to lunge onto his Bolton rival while the players were off the ball.

Almost immediately, both were shown straight red cards for violent conduct, as a melee then unfolded between the two opposing teams.

Even substitutes ended up rushing onto the pitch in ugly scenes, before things gradually calmed down.

FA issue statements

While Metcalfe and Sheehan looked to be staring at respective three-match bans, it was then announced on Tuesday that both clubs have been successful in appealing against them.

An FA spokesperson revealed the two players had seen their suspensions overturned on the grounds of wrongful dismissal.

Regarding Metcalfe, an FA spokesperson wrote: "Jenson Metcalfe's three-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

"On Saturday 5 September, the Millwall midfielder was sent off against Bolton Wanderers for violent conduct."

At the same time on Tuesday morning, a similar statement was issued revealing Sheehan had also been granted a reprieve.

4 Jenson Metcalfe had appeared to react angrily following a challenge from Josh Sheehan, but both players have now seen their red cards rescinded Credit: Getty

Another FA communication read: "Josh Sheehan will be available for Bolton Wanderers' next three matches after a successful appeal of wrongful dismissal.

"The player was sent off for violent conduct during their EFL Championship match against Millwall on Saturday 5 September."

The news now means that Metcalfe will be available for Millwall's Carabao Cup third round tie against Newcastle on Tuesday night.

The clash marks the first meeting between the Lions and the Magpies since 1993.

Meanwhile Sheehan is free to play for Bolton against West Ham in the Championship the same evening.

This comes as a welcome boost for both teams, with Jenson and Sheehan both key players, having started all five of the two EFL teams' league games this term.

4 Sheehan has played every minute of Bolton's Championship campaign so far - apart from the final five minutes against Millwall Credit: Getty

Their clash on Saturday came on an eventful weekend in the second tier, which also saw a heated incident in Portsmouth's game against Cardiff.

In the Fratton Park meeting, Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik appeared to grab a young Portsmouth fan by the neck.

Bielik had been trying to retrieve the ball in front of the home fans, before a young-looking supporter proceeded to throw it over his head, prompting the player to angrily grab him around his neck.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy claimed that Bielik had been slapped in the face during the altercation, with Portsmouth manager John Mousinho apologising for what happened.

The Polish centre-back has been widely condemned for his actions, with talkSPORT presenter Sam Matterface calling for him to be handed a season-long ban.

Sports.title: Arsenal hit by travel chaos which forces cancellation ahead of Champions League clash
Sports.content:
Arsenal hit by travel chaos which forces cancellation ahead of Champions League clash

Mikel Arteta's pre-match press conference in Naples has been cancelled amid ongoing travel mayhem.

The Arsenal boss was due to speak to reporters on Tuesday afternoon, however, Arteta and his squad are not expected to arrive in Naples until 9:30pm on the same evening.

3 Arteta and his team remained at the club's training ground on Tuesday due to the delays Credit: Getty

The delay is due to Air Traffic Control issues that has affected passengers across the UK.

Thousands have been impacted by flight delays from London-based airports in the last 24 hours.

It is due to a technical problem that has been affecting air traffic control systems.

Arsenal are scheduled to fly out of London Luton Airport which is located close to the club's training ground.

The Premier League champions could now find themselves in hot water with UEFA ahead of Wednesday's Champions League opener with Napoli

UEFA have the power to fine clubs who fail to carry out their media obligations.

A penalty is handed out if press conferences are delayed by an hour although rules state that pre-match plans can be changed if affected by circumstances beyond their control.

The UEFA ruling reads: "Clubs may only change their MD-1 plans on account of force majeure and with the agreement of UEFA."

As the issue is out of the club’s control, there is a good chance that UEFA could bypass a sanction.

The Gunners will hope that the delays do little to upset their pre-match preparations ahead of the clash at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

3 A raucous Stadio Diego Maradona awaits Arteta's side on Wednesday night Credit: Getty

Napoli vs Arsenal: Preview

Arsenal begin their quest for a first Champions League trophy following last season's agonising final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Arteta's side recorded an unbeaten European campaign spanning 14 matches before losing to the French giants on penalties in Budapest.

Ahead of the Matchday one fixture, Arteta will be without Cristhian Mosquera who continues his recovery from a muscular issue picked up in the 1-0 win at Aston Villa last month.

But there is good news for the Gunners boss with Jurrien Timber fit enough to travel with the squad to Italy.

The Dutch full-back has not featured since May's Champions League final defeat.

Following the clash with Napoli, Arsenal face a tough run of fixtures in their quest to finishing in the top eight of the league phase which secures automatic qualification for the round of 16 stage.

3 Arsenal are hoping to go one better than last season's final defeat and win their first Champions League trophy Credit: Getty

Up next for the Premier League champions are crunch fixtures against Lille, Bayern Munich, Slavia Prague, Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Jordan Ayew lands Championship move months after Leicester release
Sports.content:
Jordan Ayew has secured a new club two months after leaving Leicester City.

The striker has joined Sheffield United on a free transfer, signing a deal until the end of the season.



3 Ayew has joined Sheffield United on a free transfer after his Leicester release Credit: Getty

Ayew had been a free agent since his Foxes deal expired at the end of June.

Despite making four appearances for Ghana at the World Cup, he had yet to find a new club before the end of the transfer window.

However, the 34-year-old has now joined the Blades on a one-year contract, returning to the Championship.



Ayew featured 42 times in the division for Leicester last season, scoring six goals.

His tally was not enough to help the Foxes avoid a second successive relegation, though, as they dropped into League One.



The Ghana captain and record appearance maker will be hoping to avoid a repeat with Chris Wilder's side this term.

Ayew joins Sheffield United

Unless he was registered prior to midday on Monday, Ayew will be unable to make his debut before the weekend.



Sheffield United face Blackburn Rovers at Ewood Park on Tuesday, with kick-off at 7.45pm.

Instead, Ayew could be in line to feature at home against Wolves on Sunday.

His last competitive action came in Ghana's round of 32 defeat to Colombia at the World Cup on July 4.

3 Ayew, who made four appearances at the World Cup, had been without a club since the end of June Credit: Getty



He now bolsters the Blades' attacking options, which already included five strikers.

Wilder has added Ayew to a forward line featuring Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell, Ben Brereton Diaz, Patrick Bamford and Ryan One.

His arrival comes just days after talkSPORT's Perry Groves urged Everton to consider a move for Ayew.

The Toffees have Thierno Barry as their only recognised senior centre-forward after a deadline day move for Folarin Balogun fell through.



Ayew's career so far

Ayew has scored eight goals in 63 Championship appearances for Leicester and Aston Villa.

He also featured for both clubs in the Premier League along with spells at Crystal Palace and Swansea.

3 Ayew has signed a deal through to the end of the season with the Blades Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, his 122 caps for Ghana are an all-time record for the national team.



Across those appearances, Ayew has scored 33 goals for the Black Stars, the fourth-highest in their history.

Sports.title: Dani Carvajal tipped for Premier League transfer aged 34 with relegation candidates among next club options
Sports.content:
Dani Carvajal tipped for Premier League transfer aged 34 with relegation candidates among next club options

For the first time since 2012/13, Real Madrid started a new campaign without Dani Carvajal in their defence.

The right-back, widely regarded as one of the greatest in the modern era, announced his decision to leave club during the summer after 13 glittering seasons.

5 Carvajal tasted huge success in European football at Madrid as he won 26 trophies, which works out at two a season Credit: Getty

Carvajal departed the Bernabeu as a four-time LaLiga winner and six-time Champions League victor, with a multitude of other honours to also show for his efforts.

He made 451 appearances at Madrid in addition to collecting a Euro 2024 winner's medal with Spain during his spell.

With the 2026/27 campaign already underway across Europe, Carvajal is one of many notable free agents with past success looking for a new challenge.

A move to the Premier League is one strong option for the 34-year-old, presenting him with the opportunity to play in what is argued to be the best league in football.

European football journalist Andy Brassell spoke to talkSPORT.com to assess the given options.

Who could Carvajal sign for?

"Fulham seems like the obvious one," he said, pointing to Carvajal's former Madrid teammate Alvaro Arbeloa who is now in charge at Craven Cottage.

"It depends how long Arbeloa can hang onto his job, obviously, because it's been a difficult start for him.

"But, I think the main difficulty I have with imagining Carvajal in the Premier League at this moment, is he's not really had a pre-season with a club.

"I think at 34, that is very difficult to get over, and even more so when you think that he would be expected to adapt to the Premier League as well.

"I could definitely see it happening at Fulham, if not Liverpool. We know Liverpool have had their issues at right-back of late. I can see it happening, I'm not sure it should be happening.

"I think for him to arrive at the pace after no pre-season is going to be extremely, extremely difficult for him.

5 Carvajal also boasts a wealth of experience at international level with 52 caps for Spain Credit: Getty

"But, in terms of what he can actually bring and him as a leader, there's just no argument really. He's as good as it gets, an absolute serial winner as well.

"And when you look at him and the moments where he's really come up big for Real Madrid, like the opening goal in the 2024 Champions League final [against Borussia Dortmund], him just being an excellent right-back is only part of the equation.

"He's got so much more to give and if you're Fulham and Liverpool, because they've arguably lacked a bit since all the changes last summer, that leadership has got to be a huge part of the equation.

"Not just getting him to play every week, but getting him to bring up standards and be a leader in the dressing room."

Fulham

After Marco Silva left for Benfica, Arbeloa was named as his successor at Fulham after spending the second half of last season with Madrid.

However, he has overseen a worrying start at Craven Cottage as they have lost all of their opening three matches, conceding seven goals.

5 Arbeloa, who made 26 appearances with Carvajal. may need the help of his ex-Madrid teammate at Fulham Credit: Getty

Fulham are 19th in the Premier League and, despite it still being early in the season, have already been touted for a potential battle against relegation to the Championship.

Carvajal would not only arrive as competition for Kenny Tete and Timothy Castagne at right-back but, as Brassell mentioned, provide a sense of leadership that could inspire them out of their rut.

Although, with Fulham possibly heading towards a season to forget, it may not be an attractive prospect for him amid the risk of having a relegation on his CV.

Liverpool

Spending in attacking areas was high at Liverpool during the summer as they completed deals for Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz worth a combined £157million.

But, these funds could arguably have been set aside to address the issue they have in the right-back position.

Conor Bradley remains sidelined with the knee injury that he suffered away at Arsenal in January, and Jeremie Frimpong has flattered to deceive since his £29.5m move from Bayer Leverkusen last summer.

Joe Gomez can play on the right-hand side of the defence but is still prone to fitness issues, with Barcelona loanee and natural centre-back Ronald Araujo playing there in the 2-0 win at Ipswich Town.

Bradley and Frimpong look set to be the long-term options at right-back for Liverpool and so, whilst injury issues continue to trouble them, Carvajal could be a smart stopgap for Andoni Iraola.

5 For Liverpool, the right-back role has become an area of concern so far this season amid injury issues Credit: Getty

Manchester City

Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have been given starting roles at right-back under Enzo Maresca for City this season, with Matheus Nunes another option.

Lewis is debatably the more natural player among the three and, at 21 years old, would likely benefit from some Carvajal-style influence.

The legendary full-back could also work himself into the leadership group at City, which was announced by Maresca last week.

Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma are the players trusted with being vocal in the dressing room, but none have the long-term reputation that Carvajal can offer.

Sports.title: Financial expert says Premier League have ‘screwed up’ Manchester City case amid ex-chairman’s explosive take
Sports.content:
Financial expert says Premier League have ‘screwed up’ Manchester City case amid ex-chairman’s explosive take

Football finance expert Stefan Borson has strongly refuted a claim that Manchester City should face restrictions on player trading.

City's 130 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules loom large, having initially been charged in February 2023.



3 Former City chairman David Bernstein is not a fan of City being able to freely spend with the charges hanging over their heads Credit: Getty

However, an official ruling is yet to be handed down, even though a hearing took place between September and December 2024.

In that time, City have been free to sign and sell players, including the nine-figure acquisitions of Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson this summer.

David Bernstein's verdict on Manchester City's financial breaches

But for former FA chairman Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 to 2003, believed a transfer embargo should have been in place once the club was charged.



"If in another industry, if say a bank, an individual banker, had 115 charges against him or her for let's call it bad behaviour," Bernstein said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Would they be allowed to continue acting as a banker, carry on their business and so on and so forth, dealing in whatever?



"I say they would not be, they would be in effect suspended for a period of time until their innocence, hopefully, was proved, in which case they could carry on.

"I wouldn't do it, certainly, by sort of banning the club from playing or anything, but I think I would do it by putting restrictions on its ability to buy and sell players.



"That's where we come back to this key central point."

Stefan Borson hits back at David Bernstein's embargo claim

However, Borson vehemently disagreed with Bernstein's stance.

Borson pointed out that, at this stage, City have not been officially charged, meaning they are only allegations at this point.

3 Fernandez joined City from Chelsea in an eye-watering £125m transfer on deadline day Credit: Getty

Because of that, Borson insisted that any punishment for a party under allegation 'is neither in the rules or legal'.

"It's not happened in terms of Chelsea, Nottingham Forest and Everton or anybody else," Borson said on White and Jordan.



"So the idea that you would hold City in some kind of status for two, three, four, five years is obviously not right legally and would create irreparable harm and prejudice.

"These are allegations until proven and there's a process by which they will be either proven or dismissed."

Borson was also scathing on the fact a verdict has not been handed down given the two-year anniversary of the hearing's conclusion is mere months away.

"When you screw the process up, and I say they've screwed it up, this happens," Borson continued.



3 City have won six major trophies since they were charged with the initial FFP breaches Credit: Getty

"You start the dialogue of people making silly allegations, suggestions that City should effectively wait five years between buying a player.

"These are not things that are possible, even under the rules. The rules are very clear. The Premier League investigates a scenario. If they believe that there is a case to answer, they bring it to an independent commission and the independent commission decides what the sanction will be. That's it.

"There is no process for penalising a club or suspending a club's operation before that process runs."

Sports.title: England have five batting options for three spots - this is who is closest to nailing down a place, the man most in trouble and the surprise return that can't be ruled out
Sports.content:
England have five batting options for three spots - this is who is closest to nailing down a place, the man most in trouble and the surprise return that can't be ruled out

There is fierce competition for a place in England’s top six ahead of the Test series in South Africa in December.

This summer has seen a major overhaul of the batting line-up, with Zak Crawley, Ollie Pope and Ben Stokes no longer around, Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox in, Jacob Bethell forced to miss the Pakistan series through injury and a return for Dan Lawrence.

Cox has made the best entrance, with two stylish half-centuries, and while Gay can match that tally, he has looked a touch scratchy and has shown weaknesses to his game.

So with the high pace of the Proteas to come this winter, it's still all to play for among England's leading batsmen. Here, Daily Mail Sport assesses the runners and riders, and their chances of nailing down a spot in the team.

Emilio Gay

An average of 23 from five Tests does not immediately suggest Gay is a long-term replacement for Zak Crawley. But batting this summer has been so tough that Joe Root has averaged 29, his worst record in a home season, while the average length of the Tests so far is 1,470 balls, the lowest in an English summer since 1954.

Gay has not enjoyed much luck either. He has twice been strangled down the leg side and at Lord’s two weeks ago received an unplayable shooter after batting with skill and guts in difficult conditions for 31.

Despite predictions he would be an lbw candidate, Emilio Gay has instead been opened up a couple of times outside off stump

England have not forgotten the start he made to his Test career, top-scoring with 57 against New Zealand at Lord’s and 53 at the Oval. On both occasions he batted for more than two-and-a-half hours, hinting at the kind of permanence that always seemed beyond Crawley.

But, despite predictions he would be an lbw candidate, he has instead been opened up a couple of times outside off stump – most notably by New Zealand’s Will O’Rourke at the Oval and Pakistan’s Mohammad Ali at Headingley. Again, though, this is not unusual for young English openers making their way in Test cricket after feasting on a diet of full-length deliveries in the county game.

‘Emilio’s been brilliant in the conditions we’ve had,’ said Root. ‘It would be unfair to have any kind of discussions on anything outside this game. He’s played some vital knocks and context is really important when you have low-scoring games.’

Jordan Cox

It summed up England’s chaos at the time that Cox’s debut, against New Zealand at the Oval, came at No7. He did his best in the circumstances, making 27 and – obliged to hit out with only the last man for company – 25. But his promotion to No3 for the Pakistan series following Bethell’s knee injury has allowed him to show off his full range, without worrying about wickets tumbling at the other end.

At Headingley, he outbatted Root while making 73 in seam-friendly conditions, and at Lord’s his patient 55 helped rescue England from a spot of bother on the first day at 120 for five. He has demonstrated calm, class and street-wisdom – the last of which was so often lacking during the Bazball era.

One option, once Bethell returns, is to move Cox up to open, where he spent 30 innings for Kent between 2019 and 2021, averaging 34. His career figures are better down the order, but No4 and No5 are filled by Root and Harry Brook, and Cox would be in danger of being wasted at No6.

Root refused to engage with the question of whether Cox might open, calling it ‘hypothetical’, but it is a card England may yet play – knowing full well that the player himself would not lack the confidence to do the job. His ability to keep wicket is another string to his bow.

Jordan Cox's promotion to No3 for the Pakistan series has allowed him to show off his full range

Dan Lawrence

A fish out of water when he opened against Sri Lanka two years ago, Lawrence has looked far more comfortable at No6 on his recall, adding an intelligent 54 in the murk of Lord’s to a resourceful 51 at Headingley. In between, he was wastefully run out for 17, but so far he is comfortably in credit.

Like Bethell’s left-arm spin and Cox’s wicketkeeping, Lawrence offers a secondary skill, operating as the closest England had to a spinner at Headingley and Lord’s, but bowling a grand total of three overs. Gay, by comparison, is the only one without another string to his bow.

Lawrence’s problem may come when England want a frontline slow bowler. But for his season-ending groin injury, Sam Curran might have played in Wednesday’s third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston for that very reason, because he offered an extra seam-bowling option while creating space for the off-breaks of Shoaib Bashir.

But that scenario will not arise until the two-Test series in Bangladesh in February, by which time Lawrence hopes to have made an unanswerable case for himself in South Africa.

Dan Lawrence has looked far more comfortable at No6 on his recall to the England team, adding an intelligent 54 in the murk of Lord’s to a resourceful 51 at Headingley

Jacob Bethell

Despite a quiet series against New Zealand, it will be a surprise if Bethell doesn’t return at No3 for the first Test against South Africa at the Wanderers on December 17.

In the early part of his career, he saw himself as an opener, but a lack of opportunities up the order at Warwickshire, and the make-up of the England team, funnelled him towards No3. That is now his preferred position, cemented with a stunning 154 at Sydney in January.

He has also become part of England’s leadership group, at the tender age of 22. He captained the T20 side in Ireland last year, and is close to Root and Brook, the Test and white-ball captains. Whoever misses out, it won’t be Bethell.

Despite a quiet series against New Zealand, it will be a surprise if Jacob Bethell doesn’t return at No3 for the first Test against South Africa at the Wanderers on December 17

Ollie Pope (left) has been in the England squad all series, and cannot be fully counted out

…and Ollie Pope?

Easily forgotten but not yet gone, Pope has been part of England’s squad all series, and is no more than a broken finger away from reclaiming the place he lost after the third Ashes Test in Adelaide.

He has had a decent summer with Surrey without banging the door down: 672 championship runs at nearly 45, with centuries against Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire.

But such is the inexperience in England’s top order that the selectors can’t quite bring themselves to move on from him.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Stewards charged over derby assault axed by Old Trafford security, outrage at club's cup tickets warning, new stadium clears next hurdle and injury boost for Amad Diallo
Sports.content:
Five stewards charged with the assault of a Manchester United fan at the Old Trafford derby have been axed by the security firm used by the club.

Daily Mail Sport revealed two months ago that the men are due to appear at Manchester Magistrates’ Court in January, accused of attacking the 49-year-old supporter in the East Stand during a peaceful protest following United’s goalless draw with Manchester City in April 2025.

None of the five stewards are employed by United. They are understood to have been supplied to Controlled Solutions Group, the security company contracted by the club on matchdays, by HR Security and Protection Services.

A spokesperson for CSG told Confidential that the men will not be on duty at Old Trafford again. He said: ‘The five staff that were supplied to CSG by HR Security and Protection Services are no longer allowed to work on any CSG operations.’

The protest was in response to ticket price rises, and there will be more demonstrations when United face City at Old Trafford on Sunday. That's in response to the club’s controversial clampdown on ticket touts, which has led to United being accused of targeting innocent fans without proper evidence.

It was the subject of debate for more than an hour at the latest fans’ forum at Old Trafford in July, according to the minutes of the meeting which have now been released.

Five men will appear in court in January charged with an assault of a 49-year-old man during a post-match protest after the Manchester derby in April 2025

They reveal that supporters’ representatives ‘highlighted fans’ frustrations, anger and confusion with the communications between club and fans, with particular reference to the first wave of communications which were aggressive in tone, vague and anxiety provoking’.

United were also ‘asked whether the club recognised the growing perception among sections of the fanbase that long-standing season-ticket holders are being pushed out in favour of higher-yield hospitality and premium customers, and requested assurance that the purpose of the investigation was not to reduce the number of season ticket holders or facilitate a shift towards hospitality sales’.

United denied this was the case and chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘There are no hidden intentions, the club is not trying to make financial gains from this process nor trying to reduce the number of season tickets available.

‘We acknowledge there are learnings to be made from this investigation, and the initial communications should have been better to explain to fans what we are trying to do, and we will improve on this as a club. The relationship with our fans is fundamental and we want to protect them and the club.’

Sabah a hard sell

It may have been more than two years since United played in the Champions League but that has not been enough of a carrot for supporters as tickets for Thursday's Sabah clash made their way to general sale.

United have thousands of registered members and yet with the game fast approaching, tickets are available as they look to pack out Old Trafford for a match which some supporters feel has the allure of a Europa League or Conference League fixture, against a team who were only founded nine years ago.

What the Sabah game has done is put those who opted into the cup scheme at the start of the season in a bind.

Fans were outraged on Monday night when a social media post went viral of a text message from Manchester United which read: ‘You don’t have a ticket for the Sabah game on Thursday – please do not come to Old Trafford. Tickets are still available to purchase here. If you don’t purchase a ticket, your season ticket will be deactivated for a future Premier League game and it may impact your away eligibility.’

United sources insist this is clearly marked out in the terms and conditions of any season ticket purchase and has long been the protocol for those who opt-in to cup competitions. They say the email was only sent to fans who had opted in but hadn’t paid for their ticket and didn’t respond to several emails – although the wording could have been better, which will be amended in future.

They also expect Old Trafford to be full for the Sabah game. But with the underdogs from Azerbaijan next up and Brighton at home in the Carabao Cup next week, it’s proving a very difficult sell.

Azerbaijani champions Sabah have qualified for the Champions League this season just nine years after being formed

Fosters? Good call

Foster + Partners have officially been appointed as the architects for United’s new £2billion stadium project.

Lord Foster, a close friend of United’s minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, has been at the forefront of plans to build the Ineos billionaire’s 100,000-seater ‘Wembley of the North’. Sources have confirmed the appointment of Foster + Partners after the club gave an update to the fans’ forum, saying ‘the focus now shifts to the design phase of the new stadium in partnership with Foster + Partners’.

United were asked at a previous forum meeting why an open tender was not held for the rebuild of Old Trafford, in keeping with the club’s fiduciary duty to its shareholders, after the controversial ‘tent’ design was unveiled at Foster + Partners headquarters in March last year.

United replied then that ‘a formal process to appoint a stadium architect is underway and will be made following appropriate due diligence and in line with our governance policies’. That process is now complete and not surprisingly Foster + Partners have emerged as the club’s choice.

Foster + Partners have been named as the architects of United's new stadium project

The firm released the first illustrations of what the new 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North' could look like

Amad’s waiting game

Amad Diallo has yet to resume training on the grass at Carrington and is not expected to return to action until after the international break – although Confidential understands the United winger has an outside chance of being fit for the trip to Fulham a week on Sunday.

Diallo was injured in training before United’s opening game of the season at Hull City, and did not feature in the last two matches against Ipswich and Everton.

In addition, Marcus Rashford was taken off at Everton as a precaution after he was spotted holding his hamstring, and Michael Carrick revealed that the player ‘was feeling a bit of something’.

Meanwhile, United are being patient with Matthijs de Ligt’s return from back surgery so as not to put any pressure on the Netherlands centre back.

De Ligt is back in training but hasn’t played since the end of November, with United reluctant to put a timeline on his comeback.

Amad Diallo has an outside chance of being fit for the trip to Fulham a week on Sunday

Kids copy Carrick tactics

Under Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, the decision was taken that youth teams did not need to play in the same game model as the first team. It meant that players were not as adept at making the step up, either in first-team training sessions or in attempts to break into the senior squad.

But this season the Under 21s have reverted from their standard 4-3-3 into a more recognisable 4-2-3-1 with a false nine up top, rather than a conventional striker.

Where Matheus Cunha has led the line for Carrick’s first team, Under 21s boss Adam Lawrence has leaned on Amir Ibragimov to play a similar role, with rising star JJ Gabriel taking on Bruno Fernandes’ No10 position. Carrick and Steve Holland have continued to attend Under 21s and 18s matches this season.

It raises the question, with Chido Obi out on loan and Louie Bradbury having left permanently for Stoke weeks after signing a pro deal, of whether or not the long-term plan includes an orthodox No9.

Lawrence lands Youth League role

Confidential understands Lawrence is set to take charge of United’s Under 19s on their return to the UEFA Youth League.

He oversaw United’s last Youth League campaign in 2024 and after internal discussions as to whether he or Under 18s boss Darren Fletcher would manage the Under 19s, the job has landed at Lawrence’s door.

Talent isn’t in short supply with Tynan Thompson, Cristian Orozco, Gabriel and Ibragimov all still inside the age limit, which requires players to be born after January 1, 2008.

Bendito Mantato and Godwill Kukonki, mainstays around Under 21s squads, are also available to Lawrence, while it’s worth keeping an eye on Yuel Helafu, Noah Ajayi, Jayden Ngwashi and Jay McEvoy. Both Kai Rooney and Jacey Carrick feel like potential wildcards as part of a strong Under 18s side.

United host Sabah at Leigh Sports Village at 2pm on Thursday, six hours before the respective first teams lock horns at Old Trafford.

Adam Lawrence is set to take charge of United’s Under 19s on their return to the UEFA Youth League

Jaume’s a star pupil

Teenage midfielder Jaume Camacho Sidos has shown that he is one of United’s brightest young prospects on and off the pitch.

As well as shining for the club’s Under 18s, the 16-year-old has just passed all nine of his GCSEs with a perfect set of grade nines – equivalent to (if not better than) the old A*. Last year, Camacho Sidos was filmed speaking to Sir Alex Ferguson on camera as part of the club’s Lifeblood documentary series, titled United at Heart.

United’s new scholars achieved a strong set of results, with 75 per cent of all grades between four and nine. The club’s other academic achievements saw 11 second-year scholars complete their sporting excellence professional apprenticeship.

Six of the Under 21s, meanwhile, are studying towards BA (Hons) degrees through the PFA's football and business management programme.

It underlines United’s commitment to the development of their young players. Academy education manager Ian Smithson said: ‘The results highlight the players’ dedication and commitment to their studies and work both on and off the pitch, but are also testament to the care, attention, and excellent level of support they’ve received from our education staff.’

Sports.title: Harry Kane lands Ballon d'Or nomination after record-breaking 73-goal season - but England captain faces fierce competition from two Three Lions team-mates
Sports.content:
Harry Kane lands Ballon d'Or nomination after record-breaking 73-goal season - but England captain faces fierce competition from two Three Lions team-mates

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England captain Harry Kane has been nominated for the Ballon d’Or after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season.

Bayern Munich’s former Tottenham striker netted 61 times for the German giants and 12 for England, helping his club to the Bundesliga title and DFB-Pokal and the Three Lions to a third-place finish at the World Cup over the summer.

Winning major honours is generally the key component to winning the Ballon d'Or but Kane's 2025-26 season suggests things may pan out differently this time.

Kane left some giants in his wake with those numbers, including Bayern legend Gerd Muller (72 in 1972-73), Cristiano Ronaldo (66 in both 2011-12 and 2014-15), Ronaldo (66 in 1996-97), Erling Haaland (64 in 2022-23) and Luis Suarez (64 in 2015-16).

Indeed, only Lionel Messi has scored more goals for club and country in a single season, with 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to claim the award, with Sky Bet pricing him at 4/7, ahead of Barcelona's Lamine Yamal (11/4) and Spain's World Cup-winning midfielder Rodri (9/2).

Kane said of his chances: ‘Of course, now it is out of my hands, it is down to the voters and the people who decide it.

Harry Kane lifted the Bundesliga title and DFB-Pokal with Bayern Munich, scoring 61 goals

Kane scored six goals for England in the FIFA World Cup before the Three Lions went out to Lionel Messi's Argentina in the semi-finals

'The season I had was my best season by far, and we'll have to wait and see. I'm happy that I am in contention, so we will have to wait and see.’

Should Kane win the award, he would become only the fifth English player to do so after Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

He faces stiff competition from his national team-mate Jude Bellingham, however, who has also received a nomination alongside Real Madrid galactico Mbappe.

Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, Manchester City's Erling Haaland and Arsenal's Gabriel, William Saliba and Declan Rice make up the Premier League contingent.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain also set a new record, with ten players among the 30 nominees.

Messi, who took Argentina to the World Cup final, has been nominated for a 16th time. He is second only to Cristiano Ronaldo's 18 for number of nominations.

The Ballon d’Or returns on Monday October 26, with a ceremony in London and a host of prizes up for grabs.

Premier League champions Arsenal were among the nominations for Team of the Year, with manager Mikel Arteta on the list to be considered for the season's best coach after guiding the Gunners to their first title in 22 years.

He will face stiff competition for that from Spain's triumphant Luis de la Fuente after their World Cup triumph against Argentina. La Roja conceded only once in 12 and a half hours of World Cup football in the Americas and, of course, are favourites to take team of the year.

Luis Enrique led PSG to another Champions League triumph and was once again nominated for the Manager of the Year award.

Another Spaniard and former Arsenal boss, Unai Emery, also finds himself nominated after Aston Villa's Europa League success. Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany makes up the five nominees.

Meanwhile, Lionesses Alex Greenwood and Alessia Russo have been nominated for the women's prize.

WSL winners Manchester City have four additional nominees alongside captain Greenwood, with Golden Boot winner Bunny Shaw, Kerstin Casparij, Yui Hasegawa and Vivianne Miedema also making the cut.

London City Lionesses' midfielder Alexia Putellas is hunting a record-equalling third award after winning the Champions League with Barcelona last season.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister admits he nearly left Liverpool this summer - as midfielder reveals he is 'very sad' the Reds haven't offered him a new contract
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister has revealed he is ‘very sad’ that Liverpool have not offered him a new contract.

The Argentina star, 27, has watched his midfield colleagues, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch, sign new deals – and insists there were chances for him to leave the club this summer.

Asked how close he got to leaving, Mac Allister said: ‘There was a chance. As everyone knows, I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which of course makes me very, very sad.

‘Because everyone can see I give 100 per cent for this football club every single day. In training and games. I can have good games, bad games, like everyone – but I always give my best.

‘I see Dominik and Ryan renew their contracts. That makes me very happy because they deserve it but also at the same time it makes me very sad I didn’t get mine.

‘Of course, there is still time, the fans don’t have to worry because I will give 100 per cent until my very last day I am here. We will see what happens. There were options to leave this summer but I think right now I am in the right club.’

Mac Allister is contracted for two more seasons, including the current one, and will be close to turning 30 by the time his current deal expires

Mac Allister has won a Premier League medal and the Carabao Cup in his time at Anfield

Mac Allister is contracted for two more seasons, including the current one, and says there is ‘maybe’ a chance that the situation could change – though he will be close to turning 30 by the time his current deal expires.

When asked if the club could alter their decision, the former Brighton midfielder replied: ‘Maybe, I don’t know. It depends on how I perform during these years. Like every football player. And they (have a) right to make their decision as well.

‘But as I said, the fans do not need to worry because I am going to give my 100 per cent and hopefully or maybe they will change their minds.

‘In my three years at the club, I have done very good things, we went through difficult times and won a Premier League and Carabao Cup. For me it has been a very successful period of my life, I don’t think I have to prove something but of course I need to show my level.

‘I love this club, I love being here, I love the fans, as a player it sometimes happens when you are at a club for a long, long time and you don’t realise where you are. That doesn’t happen to me, I know this is an amazing club and this city is very special. I love being here.’

Liverpool host Atletico Madrid on Wednesday evening in head coach Andoni Iraola’s Champions League debut. The Basque boss said the main thing is that Mac Allister wants to be at the club and he ‘rates him very highly’.

New signing Bradley Barcola is ready for more minutes after a cameo in the 2-0 win at Ipswich last Friday night.

Sports.title: Don't ask about the tour from hell: Pakistan cut short questions during tetchy chat with captain Babar Azam after sending home seven players and  coach before third Test against England
Sports.content:
Don't ask about the tour from hell: Pakistan cut short questions during tetchy chat with captain Babar Azam after sending home seven players and coach before third Test against England

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Pakistan called an abrupt halt to questions about their tumultuous Test tour on Tuesday with captain Babar Azam fronting a tetchy pre-match press conference.

After answering questions in Urdu, Babar fielded half a dozen from Sky Sports in English, but was then shepherded away before the written press were given a chance, with Pakistan media manager Syed Naeem Ahmed saying: ‘We are short on time.’

The cutting of the chat after just nine minutes came after focus turned to the internal discipline inquiry launched by the Pakistan Cricket Board on Monday.

Asked if he could shed any light on what was being investigated, Babar said: ‘No, I don’t know. I have no idea’, adding that he had not been involved in discussions on the subject - oor with the decision to send seven players plus coach Sarfaraz Ahmed home after Pakistan went 2-0 down at Lord’s.

The huge upheaval of personnel between the second and third Tests means that the tourists, now being led by limited-overs coach Mike Hesson, are set to make five changes at Edgbaston.

However, quizzed on whether recent events had been difficult for him personally, Babar said: ‘Not difficult. Yes, a surprise for us, but the new players are coming. They have a golden opportunity to grab things and play.’

Pakistan captain Babar Azam during a short press conference at Edgbaston on Tuesday

Sports.title: Battle of the US Open billionaires: Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro are heiresses to business empires... now they face New York showdown
Sports.content:
Battle of the US Open billionaires: Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro are heiresses to business empires... now they face New York showdown

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Does this count as losing in your own backyard? Three weeks ago, Emma Navarro suffered a straight-sets defeat by compatriot Jessica Pegula at the Cincinnati Open.

There are few obvious ties binding Navarro to the rust belt of Ohio: she was born in New York City and raised in Charleston, South Carolina, before studying Arts and Science at the University of Virginia.

But, for the world No 27, the Cincinnati Open stands out from the other events on her summer swing – because her father owns the tournament.

On Tuesday night, Navarro and Pegula face off once more. They meet for a place in the semifinals of their home Grand Slam; it is the first all-American women's quarterfinal at the US Open since Serena and Venus Williams collided in 2015.

It is also one of the more intriguing match-ups of this fortnight because both Navarro and Pegula are the daughters of billionaires, the heiresses to business empires worth a combined $15billion.

Navarro's father Ben, the son of late college football coach Frank Navarro, began his career on Wall Street before making his fortune in credit cards and debt collection. In recent years, the co-founder of Beemok has reportedly spent more than $300million to buy two tennis tournaments: the Cincinnati and Charleston Opens. His net worth is estimated by Forbes to be $3.2billion.

Jessica Pegula, the No 3 seed, will face compatriot Emma Navarro in the US Open quarterfinals

Both Navarro and Pegula are the daughters of billionaires and heiresses to business empires

Pegula, left, with her family after her parents Terry and Kim bought the Buffalo Bills in 2014

Ben Navarro began his career on Wall Street and is estimated by Forbes to be worth $3.2billion

Terry Pegula, meanwhile, is thought to be worth nearly $12billion. He grew rich through oil and gas – he founded East Resources in 1983 with a loan of $7,500 before selling most of its assets in 2010 for nearly $5bn.

Together with his wife, Kim, Pegula now invests in sports teams. They own the NHL's Buffalo Sabres and in 2014 they beat groups spearheaded by Donald Trump and Bon Jovi to buy the NFL's Buffalo Bills for $1.4bn.

It all makes the US Open prize pot – which guarantees $1.45million to the winner of Tuesday's quarterfinal – seem like pocket change. But for Pegula and Navarro, victory would take them one step closer to the biggest reward of all: a first Grand Slam title.

Before the two Americans step on to court, it is easy to be cynical, to dismiss them as two rich kids propelled toward the top by the bank of mom and dad, to paint their success as proof that it pays to be wealthy in a sport that – for ambitious youngsters – can be cripplingly expensive.

It is tempting, too, to suggest that this matchup belongs at a tournament where ticket prices are skyrocketing, where influencers have converted Arthur Ashe into a catwalk, where on Monday, fans formed long lines outside pop-ups offering yoghurt, coffee and photo opportunities while, on some courts, row upon row of seats remained empty.

But it would also be unfair. As Pegula, the No 3 seed and a 2024 finalist at Flushing Meadows, told Daily Mail Sport a couple of summers ago: 'It's funny when people assume that I fly private everywhere, or that I have had a chauffeur driving me around since I was five… I grew up pretty normal, and a lot of that [her family's wealth] didn't happen to me until I was already older and playing.

'My goal since I was six or seven was to be No 1 in the world… I was just a normal kid growing up in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, taking lessons after school.'

That hasn't shielded Pegula, 32, from allegations that, to win a Grand Slam, she 'needs [a] dynamic that family billions can't buy.'

'I don't love being referred to as whoever with however much money's daughter,' Navarro said

Pegula, a 2024 finalist in New York, has said: 'I was just a normal kid growing up in Pittsburgh'

As for Navarro? It did no harm, of course, that her father bought a tennis complex just for his children. Or that he arranged for 'whatever [she] needed' in terms of coaching and training. Or that he is, as Navarro once explained, 'probably the smartest guy I know' who 'sent [her] on this journey' and has 'dropped a lot of knowledge and wisdom on my siblings and I over the years.'

But? 'I didn't grow up being handed things,' she told Tatler. 'We grew up in a sort of traditional way. We'd get up at 6 am on a Saturday morning and go play tennis… growing up it was a priority that we learnt toughness and we learnt work ethic and how to be intentional and purposeful and live productive lives.

'So I don't love being referred to as whoever with however much money's daughter.'

Who can blame her? The 25-year-old has been grinding at this sport since fourth grade. There are few shortcuts on the professional tennis circuit and, at the end of 2018, Navarro was ranked No 763 in the world.

Within six years, she had cracked the world's top 10. In 2024, for the first and only time, she reached the US Open semifinals.

Earlier this year, however, the American took two months off amid a reported battle with hypothyroidism, which occurs when the body doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone. Symptoms can include fatigue and weight gain, and Navarro faced cruel comments over her appearance.

'I haven't been feeling my best for probably a couple of years now—a year and a half, maybe,' she told Bounces back in May. 'I felt like I could play through it and just continue playing and it'd be fine, but then it kind of got to a point where I felt like I've got to just stay home and focus on my health.'

Thankfully, Navarro is back on court and she can reach a second Grand Slam semifinal with victory over Pegula.

In China, some supporters have christened Pegula 'Big Rich' and Navarro 'Second Rich'

But her record against the No 3 seed currently reads: won none, lost four. And among some fans, she will always play second-fiddle to her compatriot.

In China, supporters have christened Pegula (career prize money $26.15m) 'Big Rich' and Navarro ($6.68m) 'Second Rich.'

As Zheng Qinwen, who beat Iga Swiatek on Monday, previously told Pegula: 'In China, some people wonder why such a rich girl got into tennis… they say that because it's an extremely demanding sport. Like: "Why not just live a high-society life?"'

On Tuesday night, everyone inside Arthur Ashe Stadium will be grateful that both Navarro and Pegula resisted that temptation.

Sports.title: The story of Bill Shankly's lost Scottish village: Why it's being rebuilt, the memorial stone where Liverpool fans lay scarves, the two-room house where he grew up with NINE siblings and the ghost football pitch of the Glenbuck Cherrypickers
Sports.content:
The spirit of Bill Shankly still shines in Liverpool, in the form of the supporters’ union which takes his name and is a vital presence as wealthy Americans trade shares of the club he rebuilt from the ground up in the 1960s.

But on the 113th anniversary of the iconic manager’s birth, plans have been revealed to revive the ‘lost’ hilltop village on Scotland’s East Ayrshire former coalfield, where he was born and raised, as a social history heritage site.

All that remains of Glenbuck are the foundations of a few houses in its main terrace, called Monkey Row, including the two-room dwelling where Shankly and his nine siblings were raised. A memorial stone to Shankly, which stands on the hill there, is still visited by Liverpool fans whose scarves and mementoes are testament to his enduring legend.

A project led by Shankly’s eldest granddaughter Karen Gill is now quite literally building on those foundations, through the reconstruction of the Shankly home and creation of a small visitor centre and sustainable accommodation, to form a heritage destination.

Work has been underway for some time, with the formation of a not-for-profit social enterprise company. The next step is to undertake feasibility studies, commission architect's plans and fund the recruitment of a project manager. To that end, a crowdfunding initiative has been launched through the social enterprise organisation – Shankly Glenbuck Village Community Interest Company – to raise £250,000 initially needed.

As Glenbuck's coal seam was finally exhausted, the stone-built terraces emptied out and were demolished, though nearly 100 years on, it has become clear that the remnants of the village and the beautiful surrounding hills retain a huge appeal.

Bill Shankly, Liverpool's legendary manager, rebuilt the club and led the Reds to three league titles

The Scottish pit village of Glenbuck, where Shankly grew up with his nine siblings, has disappeared but is being rebuilt as a tourist attraction

The Scottish Government, National Lottery Heritage Fund and East Ayrshire Council have helped fund a basic industrial heritage site with information boards.

These tell the story of Glenbuck’s history as an iron ore and coal mining village and a production line of an extraordinary number of footballers, who played for the Glenbuck Cherrypickers, a team coached by Shankly’s father. The pitch the team played on is still visible.

Shankly’s parents raised their 10 children – five boys and five girls – in a tiny house which had no running water or electricity and other households faced the same tough existence. ‘The only way they could survive was if they worked together and I think this is where my granddad got so many of his ideals,’ said Ms Gill.

That same community spirit seems to explain why a place so small had such an extraordinary football team. The Cherrypickers, who possibly took the appellation from the nickname for miners who sifted coal, delivered stars for big English and Scottish clubs, including multiple members of the Shankly family, and Sandy Brown and Sandy Tait, both members of the 1901 FA Cup-winning side.

Shankly initially left the village for Carlisle United and enjoyed a long playing career at Preston North End before turning to the management role which brought him to an ailing Liverpool in 1959.

‘There was nothing left to signal that this was such a special place,’ said Ms Gill. ‘Our first stage is to rebuild his house as it was. That is part of a larger regeneration project to bring people to this beautiful place and join other communities together. It is what my granddad would have wanted. This is not a commercial project. It is community based.’

The statue of Shankly, built in 1997, which stands outside Anfield

Rebuilding Glenbuck 'is what my granddad would have wanted,' says Shankly's granddaughter Karen Gill. 'This is not a commercial project. It is community based'

Glenbuck, like its most famous son Shankly, was fuelled by a firebrand spirit. The mine owners tried to subdue political debate, warning families that anyone offering hospitality to socialist Keir Hardie, when he visited during a miners’ struggle in the 1870s, would be turned out of their homes. But Glenbuck stood defiant.

‘We had our pride and our characters, who made their own world, the best of a bad lot, the best of isolation,’ Shankly said of the village. ‘We talked to each other and about each other. We had fun, jokes, laughs and exaggeration.’

He would still return to the place after what would prove to be a painfully premature retirement in 1974. His granddaughter’s memories are of Shankly joining the family in walks through the surrounding hills. ‘We want to complete the circle and help others to discover this beautiful place,’ said Ms Gill.

Visit www.shanklyglenbuckvillagecic.co.uk to learn more about and support the venture.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay will return to Napoli training in two weeks after heart surgery in Manchester was a 'complete success'
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay will return to Napoli training in two weeks after heart surgery in Manchester was a 'complete success'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay is set to return to training in two weeks after successful heart surgery.

The Scotland international, 29, has been diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place in Manchester on Tuesday and McTominay – who moved to Italy from Manchester United in 2024 – will be out of action for a fortnight.

A statement from the Serie A side read: 'On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital. The operation was a complete success.

'McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training.'

Scott McTominay went to the World Cup with Scotland, playing all three of their games

McTominay's partner Cam Reading sent a message of support ahead of his surgery

Napoli announced McTominay’s upcoming short absence last week, saying he would be 'available again after the international break'.

McTominay featured in their first two games of the season, against Genoa and Como.

As well as sitting out his club’s Champions League opener against Arsenal on Wednesday evening, the 29-year-old former Manchester United man is set to miss the first four Nations League matches of Sebastien Pocognoli’s Scotland reign – two against Slovenia, as well as one against Switzerland and North Macedonia.

McTominay's fiancée sent a touching message to her partner after the news of the surgery was made public.

Accompanied by two heart emojis, Cam Reading wrote: 'By your side, always so proud of you.'

The couple have been together since around 2022, and became engaged soon after.

McTominay also spoke about his impending surgery, and insisted the issue is nothing to worry about.

I'm fine,' he told reporters. 'The procedure was something I'd planned to do with the club for quite a while.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable YouTube cookies or to allow those cookies just once.
