World.title: Govt committed to scaling up nutrition
World.content:
Muchinga Province Deputy Permanent Secretary (DPS) Brian Sichande says the Government remains committed to providing good nutrition among children and communities.

Mr Sichande said nutrition is key to effective service delivery stressing that a poorly nourished population cannot effectively perform its daily activities or contribute to national development.

He made these remarks when a team from the Ministry of Health and National Food and Nutrition Commission (NFNC) paid a courtesy call on him at his office in Chinsali district.

Mr Sichande said initiatives such as the Scaling Up Nutrition has been of great help in promoting good nutrition, hence evaluation of the Scaling Up Nutrition is imperative to identify gaps and maximize service delivery.

He added that there is a serious need for stakeholders to work together to ensure that nutrition programmes such as the Scaling Up Nutrition are effectively implemented.

He further said it was the desire of President Hakainde Hichilema and the government to ensure that the country has a well-nourished population as this would contribute to improved service delivery and national development.

Mr Sichande said the assessment of the Scaling Up Nutrition programme would help stakeholders determine how effective the programme had been, identify gaps and build on interventions that had yielded positive results.

Meanwhile, NFNC representative Jungwa Nambeye said the team of enumerators and consultants from UNICEF are in Muchinga Province to assess the effectiveness of the Scaling Up Nutrition programme.

Ms Nambeye said the programme, which is being supported by UNICEF, is being implemented across some districts including Chinsali and Isoka.

She said the programme includes nutrition support groups of peer mothers who support each other on nutrition matters.

Ms Nambeye said the programme is targeting children aged zero to 2 years, caregivers and pregnant women.

“The purpose of the assessment is to see how effective the Scaling Up Nutrition programme was, how well it was implemented, the challenges encountered and what UNICEF and the nation at large can learn,so that future programmes can be implemented better,” she said.

Ms Nambeye said data would be collected through focus group discussions, community members and community based volunteers.

She said Key Informant Interviews will be conducted among health workers and lead community-based volunteers to assess the effectiveness of the nutrition support groups.

Ms Nambeye said that in Chinsali, the assessment would focus on one health facility in one ward.

She said the information gathered would be compiled into a report and shared with the provincial administration to help guide future nutrition intervention.

World.title: 400 artisanal miners converge in Kabwe for training
World.content:
Over 400 miners from across the country have gathered in Kabwe for artisanal small scale mining training aimed at promoting safe mining and shaping the country’s mining sector.

And Small-scale miners have commended the government for reviving the small scale mining sector and placing high premium on the promotion of safe mining.

Speaking on behalf of miners at the ongoing 20-day training programme for artisanal miners, Jonathan Kankomba said the government deserves to be commended for revamping the sector.

Mr Kankomba said the mining sector has so far recorded tremendous improvement in the last five years because of the good government policies.

“As small scale miners, we are happy with the efforts the government is making in the promotion of safe mining in the country through organising training programmes such as this one in safe mining for artisanal miners and other initiatives. This is the way to go,” he said.

Mr Kankomba said small scale miners are indebted to the government for recognising them as key players in the mining sector.

He said the artisanal small scale mining training programme, which has been organised by the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development, is a clear demonstration of the importance the government attaches to the sector.

He said small-scale miners will use the knowledge from the training programme to improve their operations and effectively contribute to the country’s economic development.

“We will formalise our businesses in accordance with the guidance we are receiving from the government,” Mr Kankomba said.

The 20-day training has been organised to equip artisanal miners with knowledge on how to engage in safe mining.

World.title: Zambia’s post-election conduct breaches Commonwealth legal standards, says CLA
World.content:
The Commonwealth Lawyers Association has expressed deep concern over post-election developments in Zambia, citing threats to access to justice, judicial independence and the safety of lawyers following the country’s national election on 13 August 2026. The CLA said its mandate is to promote the rule of law across the Commonwealth through an independent and efficient legal profession, and stressed that its statement addresses rule-of-law, access-to-justice and lawyer-safety concerns only. It said it does not take a position on the merits of the election outcome and does not favour any political party.

The association, in a statement dated 7 September 2026, said a number of serious events reported since the election, taken together, required urgent attention. These included, but were not limited to:

the deployment of the army during the election, including military personnel taking control of tallying centres in Mufulira and the deployment of armed military vehicles in parts of Lusaka; serious incidents and procedural irregularities during the counting and tabulation, and alleged breaches of ballot-box security, giving rise to concerns about the transparency and credibility of the electoral process; an armed raid on 14 August 2026 on a property linked to the opposition presidential candidate, during which former Cabinet Minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was fatally shot by law enforcement; the physical sealing and cordoning off of the Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and local courts by heavily armed police on 24 August 2026, the last day for filing presidential election petitions challenging the election outcome; and reports that lawyers seeking to file election petitions have left Zambia because of concerns for their personal safety.

“Taken together, these developments raise serious concerns that the rule of law has been undermined,” the CLA said.

The association noted that Zambia is a Commonwealth member and hosted the Commonwealth Law Conference in 2019. It said it would be of profound concern if the Law Association of Zambia, its members, or lawyers acting in election-related matters, were unable to uphold the rule of law without fear of intimidation or harm. It condemned any actions, by whomever committed, that undermine access to justice, and called for election petitions lawfully brought under Zambia’s Constitution to receive full and independent judicial consideration.

The CLA also raised concern over the timing and manner of the removal of experienced judges from the Constitutional Court, and over Parliament’s ratification in May 2026 of the appointments of 40 new judges across the superior courts, particularly given that those courts may be required to determine constitutional and election challenges. It said the independence of the judiciary, and the ability of courts to uphold the rule of law and hold the Executive to account, are fundamental to democracy under the rule of law.

The statement invoked the Commonwealth (Latimer House) Principles, which recognise that an independent and impartial judiciary, together with an independent and effective legal profession, is essential to the rule of law and the proper administration of justice. It also cited the UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers, which require governments to ensure lawyers can perform their professional functions without intimidation, hindrance, harassment or improper interference, and that they are adequately safeguarded by the authorities where their security is threatened because of their work.

“These principles require more than formal recognition,” the CLA said. “Lawyers must be able to advise their clients, approach the courts and pursue lawful proceedings safely and independently. Courts must remain accessible and able to determine disputes without interference or intimidation.”

The CLA set out five specific calls:

calls for a prompt, independent and transparent investigation into the fatal shooting of Mutotwe Kafwaya, including the circumstances of the security operation and the delayed confirmation of his death;

calls on the authorities to restore public confidence by affirming their respect for the rule of law and judicial independence, restoring effective access to the courts and establishing an independent enquiry to consider the closure of the courts and the removal of constitutional judges;

stands ready, together with other Commonwealth legal organisations, to support independent observation of election petitions and other Constitutional Court challenges;

offers, in consultation with the Law Association of Zambia and other relevant national institutions, appropriate assistance from Commonwealth legal organisations to support and develop capacity within the legal profession and judiciary; and

calls for urgent public assurances that all lawyers may act on behalf of their clients safely, independently and without improper interference, regardless of the political affiliation of their clients.

The CLA describes itself as an international non-profit organisation that exists to promote and maintain the rule of law throughout the Commonwealth by ensuring an independent and efficient legal profession, with the highest standards of ethics and integrity, serves the people of the Commonwealth.

Source: Commonwealth Lawyers Association, “Statement on the post-election situation in Zambia,” 7 September 2026. https://www.commonwealthlawyers.com/statement/statement-on-the-post-election-situation-in-zambia/

World.title: Chief Mpepo demands answers over Kafwaya’s killing
World.content:
Chief Mpepo of Kanchibiya District in Northern Province has demanded that government reveal who killed former transport and communications minister Mutotwe Kafwaya, shot dead by soldiers during a raid on opposition leader Brian Mundubile‘s Kabulonga residence on August 14, hours after voting closed in the general election.

Addressing family members and village elders in Lunte during the post-burial rite known as Isambo lya Mfwa, Chief Mpepo said the chiefdom would not rest until it knew who authorised the killing. The traditional leader said both the family and the nation had a right to know who ordered the shooting, and why. No one, he said, had the right to take a life. Kafwaya was shot dead by soldiers during the operation at Mundubile’s residence, an operation government says uncovered weapons at the property.

“Tulefwaya ukwishiba uwamwipeye no koca ifyakufwala fyakwe no wamupele insambu. We demand to know who killed our son and who took away his clothes and burnt them. We want to know where those clothes are,” Chief Mpepo said.

Chief Mpepo pressed government to produce those weapons publicly, the way such discoveries have historically been handled. He said it was tradition and precedent that whenever such weapons are recovered, they are displayed to the nation. The chief’s demand strikes at a case that has remained unresolved since the night of the vote. Kafwaya, a former transport and communications minister, was killed inside a residence government has since linked to a treason investigation, with Mundubile among 18 suspects now in custody over the events of August 14.

“We cannot bury our son and remain in the dark. Government must give us answers. We just heard that they found weapons; let them show the nation those weapons they found on them. It is tradition and precedent that whenever they find such weapons, they display to the nation, but in Mutotwe’s killing we are still waiting to see the weapons they found that warranted the killing of our son,” Chief Mpepo said.

Chief Mpepo said the family could not find closure while basic questions about the raid remained unanswered. He said the chiefdom wanted to know not only who fired the shots, but under whose authority the operation was carried out. The demand for transparency extends beyond Kafwaya’s case alone. The State has restricted access to the 18 treason suspects, with the Zambia Correctional Service limiting visits to close relatives and lawyers only.

That directive affects Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu, businessman Harry Valden Findlay, lawyer George Chisanga, retired Anglican Bishop Trevor Mwamba and others held on treason charges arising from the election. A check at Mukobeko Maximum Security Correctional Facility found relatives, journalists and members of the public blocked from entering the complex. Human rights activist Brebner Changala has called for transparency in how the cases are being handled. Findlay’s lawyer, Milner Katolo, said his legal team also needed to observe the condition of the other treason-accused persons while pursuing separate efforts to secure Findlay medical attention.

“We need to observe how they are, as well as Mr Findlay, Mr Chisanga, Mr Mundubile and others,” Katolo said.

Findlay himself intends to ask the High Court to order the State to allow him access to medical treatment, with Katolo saying his client is battling advanced diabetes and high blood pressure that the State has so far declined to treat. Those separate legal efforts, unfolding alongside Chief Mpepo’s demand, point to the same underlying question hanging over the operation of August 14: whether the State will account, in full public view, for what happened to the people caught up in it, living and dead. Government has taken responsibility for the shooting that killed Kafwaya. It has not yet responded publicly to the chief’s specific demands for the weapons to be displayed or for the chain of authority behind the operation to be disclosed.

For a community burying one of its own, the post-burial rite became the moment to formally place those questions on record. Chief Mpepo’s intervention adds a traditional authority’s voice to a case that, weeks after the shooting, still lacks a public account of how Kafwaya died. The chiefdom’s position is now clear: the burial has happened, but the accounting has not. Government’s next move is to respond to the chief’s demand, produce the weapons it says were recovered, and name who authorised the operation that killed Kafwaya.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 8, 2026
World.content:
press review

Nigeria Reportedly Agrees to Secret Ceasefire With Boko Haram

Nigeria has reportedly maintained a secret ceasefire with Boko Haram for the past three months, following negotiations that helped secure the release of 360 civilians abducted from Ngoshe village in Borno State. Three sources with contacts within the jihadist group told The New Humanitarian that the truce, which has reportedly stopped attacks around Ngoshe, is likely to be extended by another 40 days. The agreement allegedly involved a ransom payment of $3.7 million. The government has denied making such a payment. The reported ceasefire highlights a possible shift to talks after 17 years of conflict, even as the government publicly rejects negotiations with Boko Haram and continues with efforts to strengthen the military. Analysts caution that the truce may be only a temporary tactical arrangement rather than a path to lasting peace. Negotiations are further complicated by Boko Haram's rivalry with Islamic State West Africa Province, which is not part of the agreement.

Sudan Faces Fresh Scrutiny Over Alleged Chlorine Weapons

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Sudan's war is facing renewed scrutiny over allegations that the Sudanese Armed Forces developed and deployed chlorine-based chemical weapons against the Rapid Support Forces during the battle for Khartoum. Investigations by The New York Times and The Washington Post, based on more than 150 leaked intelligence documents, photographs, videos and intercepted communications, reportedly detail an alleged programme that began in 2024, including plans for chlorine-filled warheads, testing operations and efforts to conceal the programme. The records also identify possible sources of chlorine, including a reported shipment that entered Sudan through Egypt and supplies stored at water-treatment facilities. However, there is no evidence that chlorine supplied by UNICEF for civilian water systems was diverted for weapons. Sudan's military has denied producing, stockpiling, or using chemical weapons. The United States previously sanctioned Sudan in 2025 over separate allegations of chemical weapons use. The latest claims are expected to increase pressure for an independent investigation to establish whether the weapons were produced or deployed, who authorised them and how the chlorine was obtained.

Namibia HIV Groups Warn of Impact From U.S. Funding Cuts

Namibia's planned phase-out of United States financial assistance for its HIV response has raised concerns among organisations supporting people living with HIV, despite the country being recognised for reaching key United Nations HIV targets for testing, treatment and viral suppression. The United States plans to provide $45 million for Namibia's HIV response during the 2027/28 financial year as funding shifts from direct financial assistance towards technical cooperation. Victoria Kamule, executive director of the Tonata People Living with HIV Support Network, said the reduction could have a major impact because many treatment, prevention and support programmes have relied heavily on donor funding. Tonata represents about 29,000 people living with HIV across six regions. Kamule warned that support groups and established community programmes could struggle without adequate government funding. More than 220,000 people currently receive antiretroviral treatment through Namibia's public health system. The government says it is committed to maintaining national ownership of the HIV response. Officials are also seeking alternatives to replace about N$730 million in annual HIV funding if an agreement with the United States cannot be reached over health data and specimen-sharing arrangements.

Mozambican Opposition Leader Faces Trial Over Post-Election Unrest

Mozambican opposition politician Venâncio Mondlane is preparing to face trial before the Supreme Court over five charges linked to protests that followed the disputed October 2024 presidential election. Prosecutors accuse him of public advocacy of crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to a crime, instigation to terrorism and incitement to terrorism, allegations he denies. Mondlane, who finished second to ruling party candidate Daniel Chapo, rejected the election result and claimed he had won, triggering months of protests in which more than 300 people were killed. He left the country after the election before returning in January 2025 and later held meetings with Chapo in an attempt to address the political crisis. The case gained further significance after Mondlane joined the Council of State and his immunity was suspended to allow the proceedings to continue. Legal and political observers say the trial could deepen concerns about using the justice system to resolve a fundamentally political dispute and could affect Mondlane's ability to contest the 2029 presidential election.

Close 

Morocco Earthquake Survivors Wait for Aid Three Years On

Three years after a devastating earthquake struck Morocco's Al Haouz region, killing more than 2,900 people and injuring over 5,500, reconstruction has progressed significantly in some communities but left thousands of families still waiting for assistance. In Ighermane village, about 90% of homes have reportedly been rebuilt, with 114 of around 150 families receiving some form of state support. But in nearby Azgour, one of the worst-hit areas, dozens of families are still waiting for reconstruction assistance, while some residents whose homes have been rebuilt elsewhere face problems accessing water and electricity. The High Atlas Development Agency says more than 54,000 homes have been built or rehabilitated and that the government has provided over 7.2 billion dirhams in assistance. However, more than 3,000 families have reportedly complained that they have received no state support, with some excluded because of residency or property-status disputes. Victims and advocacy groups are calling for greater transparency and an independent investigation into how aid has been distributed. Some survivors remain in tents or damaged homes nearly three years after the disaster.

World.title: South Africa: Police Union Demands Better Protection - South African News Briefs - September 8, 2026
World.content:
press review

Police Union Calls for Tougher Action Against Cop Killers

Twelve police officers who died in the line of duty between April 2025 and March 2026 were honoured at a ceremony at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, reports EWN. The number is lower than the 27 officers killed the previous year. The South African Policing Union (SAPU) has said that more must be done to protect police officers. It called for tougher laws and harsher consequences for those who kill members of the police.

Man Due in Court Over Fatal Spring Day Stabbing

A 53-year-old man accused of fatally stabbing 20-year-old Tshepang Nyathi during Spring Day celebrations in Refilwe, Cullinan, is set to appear in the Cullinan Magistrate's Court, reports SABC News. The incident allegedly occurred after young people splashed bystanders with water. The accused said to have retaliated by stabbing Nyathi through the heart. The killing has sparked mixed reactions within the community and fuelled national debate.

Inquest Hears Details of AKA's Call Before Anele Tembe's Fatal Fall

The inquest into the death of Anele Tembe heard that Kiernan "AKA" Forbes made a frantic call to hotel staff shortly before her fatal fall from the Pepperclub Hotel in Cape Town, reports EWN . A staff member testified that Forbes sounded panicked and said someone was on the balcony and wanted to jump, before she heard a scream and a loud bang. The testimony comes as the Forbes family has chosen not to be represented at the inquest. AKA's father, Tony Forbes, has previously indicated that he intends to testify.

World.title: Africa: NITDA, NDPC and Galaxy Backbone Back CyFrica 2026 as Nigeria's Leading Cybersecurity Summit Returns
World.content:
As Nigeria's digital economy accelerates towards an estimated $18.3 billion in 2026, the country is confronting an equally urgent challenge: protecting the digital infrastructure, data and financial ecosystems powering that growth.

With more than 281,500 accounts reportedly breached in the first quarter of 2026 alone, the widening gap between digital opportunity and cyber risk is placing cybersecurity firmly at the centre of Nigeria's economic and national resilience agenda.

Against this backdrop, CyFrica 2026 , Nigeria's premier cybersecurity summit, is set to return on 8 October 2026 at the Eko Convention Center in Lagos, bringing together leading government authorities, regulators, cybersecurity experts, technology innovators and enterprise decision-makers to address the country's most pressing digital security challenges.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The summit will provide a high-level platform for strategic dialogue on cyber resilience, data protection, emerging technologies and public-private collaboration, while exploring practical pathways for strengthening Nigeria's digital defences in an increasingly complex threat environment.

NITDA, NDPC and Galaxy Backbone Join as Supporting Partners

Adding significant institutional weight to this year's summit, the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and Galaxy Backbone Limited (GBB) have joined CyFrica 2026 as Supporting Partners.

Their participation reinforces the summit's role as a strategic meeting point for Nigeria's cybersecurity and data protection ecosystem, bringing together policymakers, regulators and industry leaders at a critical moment in the nation's digital transformation.

World.title: Ghana: Supreme Court Controversy - Bishops Call for Greater Caution, Not Resignation
World.content:
Accra — The Chief Justice of Ghana, Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, should exercise greater caution when making public statements, but there are no grounds to call for his resignation. This, in essence, is the position of the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference regarding the controversy sparked by remarks made by Baffoe-Bonnie on September 2, 2026, during working visits to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) and the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF).

The Chief Justice made a critical reference to the "last eight years" which, in Ghana's political context, could reasonably be interpreted as a comparison between the current administration and the previous one. What might have been intended as an assessment of institutional performance therefore appeared, at least on the surface, to take on the character of a biased judgment, prompting strong criticism from the opposition.

In a statement signed on September 6 by its President, Msgr. Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi, Bishop of Sunyani, the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference stressed that "the independence of the judiciary is not only a matter of actual impartiality; it also depends on the visible and unmistakable appearance of impartiality. A judge, and especially the head of the judiciary, must be, and must be seen to be, above partisan political struggles."

"The Chief Justice, like any citizen, is entitled to his own convictions," the Bishops said. "The question is not whether he may hold them, but whether his public conduct in office should ever create room for reasonable doubt about where he stands."



The Bishops nevertheless believe that "calls for his resignation on this basis alone strike us as disproportionate to the offense," adding that "the same standard of restraint must be asked of every public office holder, regardless of who occupies it or which party is in government."

"We continue to hold the Judiciary, and all who serve the nation in public office, in our prayers, and we pray that God may grant our leaders the wisdom to serve truth, justice, and the unity of our common home," the Bishops concluded.

World.title: Craig Carton blasts Michigan fans for storming field after controversial win: 'They’re a bunch of morons'
World.content:
Craig Carton scorched Michigan Wolverines fans for celebrating the team’s controversial victory against the Western Michigan Broncos on Saturday night.

There’s no argument that Michigan needed a little bit of luck to get past Western Michigan 13-12. Bryce Underwood received a second Hail Mary opportunity as officials determined that a Western Michigan defended touched his first throw in the final moments with one second left on the clock. Underwood found J.J. Buchanan for the game-winning score.

Is that a real reason to storm the field and act like you beat Ohio State? An emphatic no, says Carton, whose "Craig Carton Show" premieres on OutKick on Tuesday. Carton put it better than I could.

CRAIG CARTON: I'M BRINGING MY 'UNWAVERING, UNAPOLOGETIC' OPINIONS TO OUTKICK

"The thing that bothers me more than the hubris of adding a second to the game and giving Michigan another opportunity to win that game was the fact that there was 110,000 people at Michigan for that game and at the end of the game they stormed the field like they were Western Michigan knocking off a Big Ten team on the road," Carton said. "And it just was a good reminder to me that even though Michigan is thought of as a top educational experience for the kids that take the six years they normally take to graduate, the reality is that they’re a bunch of morons.

"Now, we already know that Michigan is a corrupt athletic program. We know that it’s a dirty athletic program. We know that coaches like to sleep with coeds there. Coaches like to steal signs there. Coaches like to cheat there. But what I didn’t know as a fact until Saturday night is that that 18-27 year olds that call Michigan their undergraduate home are morons. The fact that you would storm the field when barely beating and, let’s be honest, needing the Big Ten to cheat for you to win the game, the fact that you would storm the field when you won by a single point because you were given an extra second of time while 27-point favorites tells me everything I need to know about the type of kid that goes to Michigan."

SUBSCRIBE TO 'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW' ON YOUTUBE

Remember, it’s not as though Michigan was unranked (they were 16th going into Saturday) and were up against Ohio State or Texas or Alabama or Oregon or even Rutgers for that matter.

The Wolverines were playing Western Michigan that plays in the Mid-American Conference and have been an FBS program since 1962. The Broncos have never beaten an opponent inside the top 20 of the Associated Press poll.

"That’s not a game to be celebrated if you’re a Michigan fan or a Michigan alumni," Carton added. "That’s a game to give you a warning about what’s to come for the rest of this season. Michigan football is dead. Michigan football is an embarrassment. Michigan football pays their quarterback $10 million a year and I would be better.

WATCH THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW ON OUTKICK

"So, just remember what you saw Saturday night. You saw a Wolverine program that needed cheating and needed secretive clocks to beat a MAC team while favored by 27 points. And the kids there are either so drunk, so high or so stupid that they stormed the field like they had accomplished something. You didn’t accomplish a damn thing but embarrassing yourselves on Saturday night."

Western Michigan has been ranked in the AP poll once ever – that coming in 2016 when they were 13-1 under P.J. Fleck. A victory over a blue blood would have been the biggest win in the program’s history.

The Big Ten and Mid-American Conference both released statements on the clock controversy after the game, reiterating that a Broncos defender touched the ball while out of bounds with one second left.

Michigan fans’ celebration was certainly silly and they will be needled for it until the next cray thing happens.

For now, the team itself has to prepare for noon ET showdown with Oklahoma on Saturday as questions surround Underwood about his status as QB1 for the future.

World.title: Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll aim to turn the Tennessee Titans into AFC South contenders
World.content:
With defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh taking over the program and veteran offensive coordinator Brian Daboll arriving to shepherd quarterback Cam Ward in his sophomore year, the Tennessee Titans are aiming to prove that its painful baseline rebuild is finally giving way to a competitive new era in the AFC South.

Last Year

The Titans endured a brutal 2025 campaign, stumbling to a 3–14 finish and landing near the bottom of the league in both scoring offense and scoring defense. Rookie starter Cam Ward showed occasional dynamic flashes under pressure, while Tony Pollard provided steady work out of the backfield with a 1,082-yard rushing season. In fairness, the NFL didn’t do them many favors, giving them a really tough schedule even after a bad year. Ultimately, the lack of success on both sides of the ball led to the mid-season exit of Brian Callahan.

Offseason additions and subtractions

To reset the organization, general manager Mike Borgonzi orchestrated a sweeping offseason overhaul.

The headline moves started at the top by hiring former New York Jets head coach Robert Saleh as head coach and bringing in Brian Daboll to call plays. The problem I have is that neither has really proven successful with rebuilding teams – maybe Daboll more than Saleh.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

I do like teams that are intentional about upgrading areas. When you have a lot of areas to upgrade, there are only so many areas you can really make an impact. They signed former New York Giants wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson and tight end Daniel Bellinger, added edge rusher John Franklin-Myers and defensive tackle Solomon Thomas, and bolstered the secondary with cornerbacks Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott alongside safety Tony Adams.

They also brought in veteran quarterback Mitchell Trubisky as high-end insurance. In the draft, Tennessee made massive moves by taking wideout Carnell Tate at No. 4 overall and trading back into the first round for pass rusher Keldric Faulk. Major subtractions included letting lingering free agents walk and restructuring line depth to accommodate their fresh rookie class.

Roster

The offense features a far more dynamic receiving corps with rookie Carnell Tate on the perimeter alongside Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley, providing Ward with the quick-separation weapons he lacked as a rookie. Their line isn’t exactly top-notch, coming in at 29th for the year, but I do think there is potential they are better than they are graded at currently.

HOUSTON TEXANS' 2025 WIN TOTAL SET AT 9.5 AS CJ STROUD FACES QUESTIONS ABOUT OFFENSIVE LINE

Betting Outlook

If you plan to bet the over 6.5 wins for Tennessee, I think you attribute it to the improved weapons for Ward, the tough schedule from last season that still saw them get three wins, and the new coaching staff. If you want the under, it is looking at an offensive line that is ranked at 29th, and a defensive line ranked at 17th. The Texans have a great defense, but there are questions on that roster as well. The Colts have a quarterback coming back from an Achilles tear, and the Jaguars lost some key pieces. I have them right at six wins this year, which improves from last year, but I don’t think I can bet one way or another on them.

World.title: SEC accuses LSU of letting Lane Kiffin run wild as expulsion vote coming Thursday in explosive court filing
World.content:
The SEC filed an amended complaint Tuesday morning in an Alabama federal court, indicating that the conference is seriously considering drastic action against LSU.

After what unfolded last week in a Louisiana district court, it has become clear that the fight launched by LSU over the potential rostering of athletes with NFL experience has not gone over well with officials inside SEC headquarters.

Last Thursday, while SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey took the stand in a Baton Rouge courtroom, the conference filed a federal lawsuit against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and athletic department staffers. The lawsuit argued that the school was preventing SEC officials from exercising their First Amendment rights to govern the conference.

LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN

Sankey testified for more than three hours, a hearing OutKick attended, and the gamesmanship quickly disappeared. Behind the scenes, the SEC was preparing to take action against LSU over a fiasco that had placed the conference and its leadership at the center of what was viewed as an embarrassing situation in Birmingham.

"The SEC does not bring this action to declare any student-athlete ineligible or to prevent any student-athlete from participating in any athletic competition. This action is directed solely at the state actors who have violated, continue to violate, and threaten to further violate the SEC’s rights under the First Amendment," the complaint noted.

LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE'

Will LSU be expelled from the SEC? The games continue off the field

The fight is now moving beyond the courtroom.

On Thursday, SEC officials will hold a special meeting to determine whether LSU could face expulsion from the conference. The meeting centers on concerns that school officials have lost control of Kiffin and the football program.

In the filing, SEC presidents and chancellors made it clear during a Sept. 4 meeting that they feel as though LSU has let Lane Kiffin run the football program however he wants, without guidance from the athletic department.

"Expressed great concern that Defendants Rousse and Ausberry have no meaningful control over Defendant Kiffin or the football program at LSU...The consensus at the September 4 meeting was and continues to be that LSU’s demonstrated lack of institutional control at the University level—including complete lack of control over Defendant Kiffin’s actions."

Simply put, the SEC feels as though the comments made by Kiffin over the past few weeks regarding this matter go against conference rules, and they feel as though the LSU athletic department has allowed Kiffin to run the football program without pressure from his own bosses.

Will this actually take place?

That's up to the member institutions, though the likelihood of the SEC expelling LSU from the conference feels pretty slim in the grand scheme of things.

But, in their updated filing on Tuesday, the SEC made it clear that they have the power to expel LSU from the conference, if enough votes are cast in favor of the move.

"Membership of a member may be terminated involuntarily at a meeting of the Chief Executive Officers. A vote of at least two-thirds of all the Chief Executive Officers is required to terminate membership. Any motion to terminate membership shall specify the effective date of the proposed termination," the complaint notes.

Right now, we are witnessing a fight between one of the biggest schools in the conference, and SEC members who are tired of being made fools of by Kiffin.

LSU'S LANE KIFFIN ADMITS HE LET TIGER STADIUM WEATHER DELAY DRAG ON IN ORDER TO HURT CLEMSON

And, when Sankey took the stand last week inside a Baton Rouge courthouse, the stakes were raised in this matter to the point where the SEC has now made it clear that they are not going to just brush this under the table because LSU decided not to roster players like Dae'Quan Wright this past weekend.

This has obviously ruffled plenty of feathers, and Kiffin's comments during the Clemson game this past weekend regarding how much worse the outcome could have been if LSU had been able to roster pro players were seen as the school having zero control over its head coach.

LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES

"Defendant Kiffin’s statements and position, along with the numerous other statements and actions by Defendants alleged herein, stand in sharp contrast to the silence by the President and Athletic Director of LSU after Defendant Rousse voted for the Policy Statement on August 25, 2026," the SEC noted in its amended complaint.

"And they confirm the lack of institutional control over the athletics program at LSU that is required by Article 6 of the SEC Constitution and by the remaining provisions of the Constitution and Bylaws referenced above."

LSU has zero influence on decisions made by Lane Kiffin ... SEC notes

Not only is the SEC under the impression that LSU is allowing Lane Kiffin to run his football program without guidance from school officials, they see this as a slap in the face to the rules enacted regarding pro-athletes coming back to college.

"In light of the recalcitrance, lack of institutional control, and serious harm caused by the statements and conduct of LSU, the 15 SEC CEOs (other than LSU) have informally told the Commissioner (and President Plowman has directed the Commissioner) to issue a notice of the Special Meeting to be conducted on September 10, 2026, to consider the termination of LSU’s membership in the SEC, whether LSU renounces its intention to roster and play professional players on its football team, or not."

The SEC is obviously past the point of frustration with Lane Kiffin, and now we're about to find out how serious they are regarding penalties against the school in which they feel has embarrassed them enough.

Just when you thought the college football season would provide us an opportunity to talk about other things taking place outside a courtroom, the SEC decided to drop a public hammer on Tuesday.

Will they actually do it? Probably not, but they clearly want to embarrass LSU in the process.

World.title: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch is leaving amid fights with Trump
World.content:
Lonnie G. Bunch III will step down from his position as head of the sprawling Smithsonian Institution by the end of the year, he said Tuesday.

He will depart at a vulnerable time for the institution, which includes 21 museums, 20 libraries and the National Zoo. While it has traditionally operated independently of the party in power, the Trump administration has repeatedly criticized the Smithsonian’s presentation of America’s past. Last week, the Interior Department threatened to cut off support, alleging that Smithsonian facilities present a “radical ideology” that weakens “shared American identity.”

Bunch, who has worked at the Smithsonian for 38 years, said in a statement: “It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement.”

“I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian — it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together,” said Bunch, who became secretary in 2019.

He is the first Black person and first historian to lead the Smithsonian.

“I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward,” Bunch added.

Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian, praised Bunch in a statement.

“From his days as a young curator at the National Air and Space and American History Museums through his tenure as the founding director of the African American History and Culture Museum and culminating in his distinguished service for the past seven years in the Smithsonian’s top job, Secretary Bunch has pursued excellence in the telling of our nation’s story,” Roberts said.

“The Regents, and the Smithsonian, have benefited greatly from his wisdom, vision and leadership. We look forward to working with him in the coming months to ensure a smooth transition for his successor.”

World.title: New Hampshire primaries test Trump and the left
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again Tuesday in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.

Granite State voters are among the last in the country to choose nominees for November’s elections, and Tuesday’s contests will set the matchup in one of this year’s most competitive Senate races.

Trump is hoping his preferred candidate, former GOP Sen. John Sununu, prevails in the primary. On the Democratic side, Rep. Chris Pappas is looking to fend off a democratic socialist opponent for his party’s Senate nomination.

A supporter snaps a photo of former Sen. John E. Sununu as he campaigns for the GOP nomination for his old seat in Berlin, N.H., on Aug. 22. Holly Ramer / AP file

A divisive Democratic battle is also unfolding in one of the state’s competitive House seats, which Pappas left open, while another House Democrat is facing a primary challenger from the left.

Here’s what to watch Tuesday in New Hampshire, where poll closing times vary by municipality, ranging from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. ET.

Senate matchup

Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s retirement opened up this Senate seat, and Republicans are hoping to make the race competitive in November.

Pappas, who has won in a battleground seat since 2018, is considered the front-runner for his party’s nomination. He already appears to be gearing up for the general election, focusing his campaign on addressing high costs and political corruption and already launching an ad attacking a potential Republican opponent.

But Pappas is facing a challenge from the left from Karishma Manzur, a scientist and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who supports progressive policies like “Medicare for All.” Manzur has sharply criticized Pappas over support and funding for Israel, saying he is “enabling genocide.”

Dr. Karishma Manzur at a town hall in Merrimack last month. Mel Musto / Bloomberg via Getty Images file

The GOP primary includes multiple candidates, but the race is largely between Sununu and another former senator, Scott Brown, who held a Massachusetts seat for three years, previously ran for the New Hampshire Senate in 2014 and served as Trump’s ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during the president’s first term.

But the president backed Sununu, who also has support from Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Sununu represented New Hampshire in the Senate from 2003 through 2008 after serving in the House. He lost his bid for re-election in 2008 to Shaheen, but Republicans believe his well-known family name could give him a boost: Sununu’s brother and father both served as governors.

Trump lost the Granite State by just 3 points in 2024, giving Republicans hope about making this open-seat race competitive two years later. The GOP has not won a Senate race there since 2010, but New Hampshire does have a Republican governor, Kelly Ayotte.

Kelly Ayotte is sworn in as New Hampshire governor on Jan. 9, 2025. Charles Krupa / AP file

Ayotte is running for a second two-year term as one of two GOP governors up for re-election in a state Trump lost two years ago. Ayotte is not facing any major primary challengers.

The Democratic nominee is all but certain to be former New Hampshire Executive Council member Cinde Warmington, who also faces no major competitors and unsuccessfully sought her party’s gubernatorial nomination in 2024.

House battles

The Democratic Party’s divides are on full display in a primary in Pappas’ now-open seat in the 1st District, which includes Manchester, the state’s biggest city.

A crowded field of candidates is running in both parties’ primaries, and the race could be competitive in the fall. Pappas won re-election by 8 points in 2024, but then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried the district by just 2 points.

Two of the front-runners are viewed as the most establishment Democrats: Marine veteran Maura Sullivan, the former congressional candidate and former Defense Department official, and Stefany Shaheen, a health advocate, former Portsmouth City councilwoman and daughter of the retiring senator. Over the weekend, Army National Guard officer Christian Urrutia, who had been running as a progressive, ended his campaign and backed Shaheen.

Another top contender in the race is progressive Carleigh Beriont, a union organizer. Heath Howard, who was backed by the local Democratic Socialists of America chapter, is still on the ballot but dropped out of the race and endorsed Beriont.

On the Republican side, Trump and other Republican leaders have endorsed auto businessman Anthony DiLorenzo. He is facing competition for the GOP nod from state Rep. Brian Cole and Hollie Noveletsky, a military veteran and CEO of her family iron company.

In the state’s other congressional district, Democratic Rep. Maggie Goodlander is facing a primary challenge from state Rep. Paige Beauchemin, a former nurse who entered politics in 2023.

The challenger is running as an unabashed progressive, calling for halting data center construction, new regulations on the artificial intelligence industry, “Medicare for All,” labeling Israel’s conduct in Gaza a “genocide” and abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Although Beauchemin’s campaign is trying to tap into some of the progressive energy that has helped challengers topple incumbents this year, she has struggled to raise money — bringing in $44,000 to Goodlander’s $4.2 million — and hasn’t drawn any outside support from progressive groups.

Goodlander is a first-term lawmaker who recently gained national prominence as one of the national security-minded Democratic lawmakers who made a video telling the military that members could refuse illegal orders. She also worked in the Biden White House and Justice Department, and is married to former Biden national security adviser Jake Sullivan. Lily Tang Williams, a former Colorado libertarian who since moved to the state, is expected to win the Republican nomination after she lost to Goodlander in 2024.

World.title: 4 family members confirmed dead in Bahamas plane crash, relatives say
World.content:
The bodies of four family members were recovered during a desperate search after a small private aircraft crashed about 15 miles off the coast of the largest Bahamian island Monday, according to relatives.

The Miami-bound PA-34 Piper, a five-seater plane with four people aboard, took off from Great Harbour Cay around 11:15 a.m. Monday and crash-landed near Andros Island, Bahama police previously said.

“It is with profound sadness that we confirm all four of our family members have been found deceased,” the family said in a statement Tuesday, noting that relatives “located our loved ones and had to bring them aboard their own vessels.”

“We are now in communication and working with the U.S. Coast Guard to bring our loved ones home safely and with dignity,” the statement continued.

The family previously said that the plane was piloted by 80-year-old Mario Lamar and that his 79-year-old wife, Lili Lamar, and two of their grandchildren — 28-year-old Sofia Sosa and 22-year-old Christian Sosa — were also on board.

Silvia Larrieu, Lamar’s niece, told NBC News affiliate WTVJ in South Florida that her uncle had an apartment in the Bahamas and had spent “a wonderful long weekend together” with the grandchildren who were passengers on the plane and two other grandchildren.

She called Lamar “a lifelong, very experienced pilot” and said the family was “departing business as usual, like he’s done his entire life.”

FlightAware, a flight-tracking platform, showed the aircraft “flying into the edge of a storm” before it quickly reversed course, Larrieu told the station.

Larrieu’s cousin, the mother of the two adult grandchildren on board, called authorities when she didn’t hear from her kids after they were supposed to have landed.

Earlier Tuesday, the family pleaded for assistance in the search.

“We are heartbroken and desperate. As of this moment, we are not aware of authorities actively searching the waters for our remaining missing family members,” the family added. “We are begging for help.”

The U.S. Coast Guard began a search but had to pause the effort because of weather conditions, according to the Royal Bahamas Police Force. The Coast Guard said Monday that it was working with the Royal Bahamas Defense Force to search for crash victims.

It was not immediately clear when the search resumed.

The family stressed Tuesday that it was “asking anyone with a boat, anyone on the water, fishermen, members of the boating community, and other civilians who can safely assist to please help us search.”

After the grim discoveries, the family members thanked “everyone who supported us, searched alongside us, and kept our family in their prayers.”

World.title: Authorities identify 5 victims killed when Amazon-branded cargo plane overran runway in Miami
World.content:
An airline cleaning company was mourning the loss of five employees who were identified as those killed Sunday when an Amazon-branded cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, striking the company’s van and a passenger SUV.

Investigators continue work Monday to determine what caused the crash of an Amazon cargo plane at Miami International Airport. Joe Raedle / Getty Images

The deceased victims were Rolando Aleman Leon, 55, Yoel Rodriguez Narajo, 53, Julio C Pineda, 75, Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53, and Javierk Reyes Quevedo, 47, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said at a news conference Tuesday. They were all in the van, owned by Professional Ocean Service Corp., a contract cleaning company for airline companies.

Five other people were injured in the crash and taken to the hospital, officials said. Eugenio Corredor, 79, and Ridoel Averhoff Diaz, 32, remain in critical condition, and Roosevelt Sebastian Perdomo Torres, 36, is stable.

The two pilots of the Boeing 767-300 aircraft, Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37, and Joseph Carol, 55, were treated and released.

The cleaning company said in a statement Tuesday that it was “heartbroken” by the deaths.

“Our employees are far more than the people who work beside us each day, they are family, and they are deeply loved,” the statement read. “Our hearts and prayers are with every employee and every family whose lives have been forever changed. We grieve with those who lost a loved one and pray for the healing and recovery of those who were injured.”

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said that the National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation into the crash.

The aircraft was on its third trip that day when it overran the runway during a landing, NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said at a news conference Monday. Earlier Sunday, the plane traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, and then Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico.

It was returning from San Juan when it crashed.

Homendy said that upon landing back in Miami, the plane overran the runway and struck navigational aids and equipment before hitting the cleaning company’s Ford van, which was transporting the crew inside the airport.

The plane then careened through a perimeter fence and struck a Toyota SUV that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue outside the airport. The aircraft continued into the grass where it hit a fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed, Homendy said.

She described the scene as “devastating” and said the van had been “torn apart.”

Cellphone footage obtained by NBC South Florida showed someone jumping out of the plane after the crash. A photo sent to NBC News showed a crew member being taken away on a gurney at the airport.

An Amazon spokesperson had previously said that the flight was operated by 21 Air.

Keith Winters, 21 Air’s CEO, said in a message on its website that it is cooperating with federal investigators and offered condolences to the victims’ families.

Homendy said it was too early to release much information about the factors that contributed to the crash, but said the plane’s flight data and cockpit voice recorder have been recovered.

World.title: Names of victims in deadly Amazon cargo plane crash at MIA released
World.content:
The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office released the names of the five people who were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, slammed into vehicles near the airport and burst into flames.

All of those who were killed were in two vehicles that were hit during the crash, National Transportation Safety Board Chair Jennifer Homendy said Monday.

Five people were also injured, including the pilot and co-pilot, who have since been treated and released from a Miami hospital, according to officials.

The pilots have been identified as Joseph Carroll, 55, and Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37. CBS News has determined the names of the pilots using the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office release, LinkedIn profiles, and the FAA pilot database. LinkedIn profiles list Carroll as a captain with 21 Air and Jaime Felipe Silva Molina as a 21 Air first officer.

Miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said Tuesday that three people remain in the hospital, including two in critical condition.

Who were the victims of the Amazon cargo plane crash at MIA?

The five people who were killed were identified as:

Rolando Aleman Leon, 55

Yoel Rodriguez Naranjo, 53

Julio C. Pineda, 75

Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53

Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47

The five people who were injured were identified as:

Eugenio Corredor, 79

Ridoel Averhoff Diaz, 32

Roosevelt Sebastian Perdomo Torres, 36

Jaime Felipe Silva Molina, 37

Joseph Caroll, 55

Victims killed, injured in crash were in vehicles, NTSB says

Homendy said Monday that the flight, Amazon Air Flight 7598, was a Boeing 767-33 Alpha operated by 21 Air LLC. It had arrived from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and was on its third flight of the day, having gone from Cincinnati to Miami, then Miami to San Juan and back to Miami.

The plane overran runway 30 on landing, struck navigational aids and hit a 2012 white Ford Econoline van owned by the Professional Ocean Service Corporation, a contract cleaning company for the airlines, Homendy said. Seven people were inside the van at the time.

The plane then tore through a perimeter fence and struck a Toyota Corolla Cross LE that was traveling on Northwest 67 Avenue. It continued into the grass and hit another fence line in an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed. In total, the plane traveled about 1,300 feet past the paved surface, Homendy said.

Homendy said all victims were in those two vehicles. The van was inside the airport, while the Toyota was outside.

World.title: Lonnie Bunch, Smithsonian leader, to retire amid Trump criticism
World.content:
Washington — Historian Lonnie Bunch will leave his position as secretary of the Smithsonian at the end of the year, he announced Tuesday, after months of escalating criticism of the institution from the Trump administration.

"It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian," Bunch said in a statement. "I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been."

Bunch, who has worked for the Smithsonian for 38 years, said he leaves the position "with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward."

Bunch told The New York Times in an interview that his upcoming retirement wasn't due to the fights with the administration, saying simply that "now's the time."

"I have to be honest, it has been stressful," he said. "And at a certain point, I'd like to wake up in the morning and not look at my cellphone."

Lonnie Bunch poses for a portrait in May 2026 in Washington, D.C. Al Drago/The Washington Post via Getty Images

Bunch, 73, co-founded the Smithsonian's National Museum of African American History and Culture, which opened in 2016. He served as executive director of the museum until he became secretary of the Smithsonian in 2019. He was the first African American to hold the role in its 173-year history.

Chief Justice John Roberts, who serves as chancellor of the Smithsonian and sits on its Board of Regents, said in a statement that Bunch "has pursued excellence in the telling of our nation's story."

"The Regents, and the Smithsonian, have benefited greatly from his wisdom, vision and leadership," Roberts said. "We look forward to working with him in the coming months to ensure a smooth transition for his successor."

Since President Trump's second term began in 2025, he has stepped up criticism of the institution. The administration launched an internal review of some of the Smithsonian's best-known museums, and the president signed an executive order in March pushing for changes at the institution, including the removal of "improper ideology."

In July, Mr. Trump ordered federal officials to install signs outside the National Museum of American History to correct what he said was "inaccurate" information presented about American history.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum sent a letter to the Smithsonian last month accusing its leadership of having "sanctioned a radical institutional ideology to permeate" the American history museum.

"The ultimate effect of this radical ideology is to weaken our shared American identity. erase our heritage and condition the public to accept these attempts to weaponize our national institutions and traditions in support of a radical political agenda," Burgum wrote.

The Smithsonian Institution includes 21 museums, 20 libraries, numerous research centers, and the National Zoo in Washington.

In an interview with CBS "Sunday Morning" in 2019, Bunch said that the Smithsonian is "part of the glue that holds the country together."

"Culture is so important. Culture is something that sometimes is seen as dividing people, but in my mind, culture holds us together — the common cultures we have, the opportunity to find common ground," he said.
