World.title: Schools widely using exceptions to start classes before 9 a.m.
World.content:
Classes are supposed to start at 9 a.m. this school year, but many schools are using an exception to begin earlier to keep schedules aligned with bus routes and extracurricular activities.

In exceptional cases and for serious reasons, and with mutual agreement between the school and the school operator, the school day may begin earlier, according to new rules.

In reality, the picture across Estonia is very varied, because schools must take into account extracurricular activities, public transport and many other circumstances. The Ministry of Education does not have an overall overview of schools' choices.

Hele Liiv-Tellmann Autor/allikas: Priit Mürk/ERR

"The Ministry of Education and Research does not collect statistics on how many schools begin lessons before nine o'clock nor on the reasons why schools have decided to use the exception provided in the regulation," said Hele Liiv‑Tellmann, senior expert in the Ministry's basic and primary education department.

She added that schools do not have to coordinate their daily schedule or school day start time with the Ministry.

She also noted that if a school has already set that lessons begin earlier than nine, it does not need to apply for an exception again each school year, but the earlier start must continue to be a justified exception.

Start times vary across Tartu schools

In Tartu the school day begins at nine o'clock in about half of the schools, and at different times in the rest.

For example, Annelinna High School and Kristjan Jaak Peterson High School continue the existing practice of starting lessons at eight, Mart Reiniku School begins at 8:30, and Hugo Treffner High School from Tuesday to Friday at 8:15, but on Mondays at 9:20, preceded by an elective subject. Among Tartu private schools, there are both nine o'clock starters and 8:30 starters.

Students during a presentation at Kristjan Jaak Peterson High School (KJPG) in Tartu. Source: KJPG

High schools start the earliest because their days are longer, said Riho Raave, head of the education department of Tartu city government.

Several schools have already shifted the start of the school day to nine o'clock in previous years. The head of the education department said that starting the school day later and finishing at a normal time requires reorganizing the entire school day.

"This can be quite a challenge for large schools, because both lesson and break lengths are set by regulation," Raave said. "The city government's position is that if schools decide in favor of an earlier start, discuss it in parent councils and make a justified proposal to the school operator, then the city government accepts it."

The head of Tartu city government's education department believes that each school and its community should decide the start time of the school day.

"The regulation fortunately allows this, and we have used this option in Tartu," said Raave.

Tallinn approved all applicants

Tallinn education department communications manager Sille Tiitsmaa said that all schools that applied ultimately received approval to start the school day at a time suitable for them, but with some schools the department clarified reasons and discussed the possibility of starting at nine next school year.

"We value schools' autonomy, and if it is clear that the school community has jointly thought through the start of the school day and the organization of the entire school day, we see no reason from the education department's side not to support such a decision," Tiitsmaa said.

Classroom at Gustav Adolf High School in Tallinn. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

In Tallinn, 36 schools applied for an earlier start, and lesson start times among schools that applied for an exception vary from eight o'clock — as in School No. 21 and School No. 32 — to 8:50, when lessons begin for Gustav Adolf High School, Lasnamäe Basic School and the first six grades of Tallinn Secondary School of Science.

Several schools conducted surveys among students, parents and teachers to find out the preferences of the school community, Tiitsmaa noted.

Schools that wanted an earlier start were those where lesson start times are differentiated or where teaching is done in two shifts, where cafeteria or sports facilities are more limited, or where other space‑related constraints restrict the school's possibilities.

"An earlier start is also important for schools whose students travel across the city and whose traffic peak would coincide with a nine o'clock start. This is certainly one reason why we consider exceptions necessary in future years as well," Tiitsmaa added, noting that dispersing morning traffic load remains an issue.

Smaller places prefer earlier starts more often

In Võru municipality, lessons begin before nine o'clock in all general education schools, varying between eight, 8:15 and 8:30.

"In making decisions, the opinions of parents and students, the positions of parent councils, student transport arrangements, regional dispersed settlement, balance of the daily schedule and students' well‑being have been considered," said municipal public relations specialist Kadri Kauts.

She added that several schools conducted surveys among parents, and in many places it was also important that the school day end at a reasonable time and that students be able to participate in extracurricular activities.

Tarvastu High School. Source: Olev Kenk/ERR

In Viljandi, all four basic schools start lessons at nine, while in Viljandi municipality school start times vary from eight to 8:40, and the decision is related, among other things, to bus schedules and extracurricular activities.

For example, Tarvastu High School's parent council decided at its spring meeting that timely arrival at school and timely arrival home or to training depends on public transport, and many municipal children attend extracurricular activities in Viljandi, and the school cannot change their start times.

"There is no justified need to change the school start time," Tarvastu High School's parent council decided, voting unanimously for an 8:20 start.

World.title: South Africa economy shrinks ahead of local elections
World.content:
Johannesburg – South Africa’s economy shrank in the second quarter of 2026, snapping a nearly two-year growth streak as the war in Iran weighed on domestic demand, the national statistics agency said Tuesday.

The contraction comes less than two months before local government elections, putting the country’s sluggish economy squarely in the political crosshairs.

Gross domestic product fell 0.2 percent from the previous quarter on a seasonally adjusted basis, StatsSA said.

Mining was the biggest drag, shrinking three percent as production of platinum-group metals, manganese, gold and iron ore fell.

Trade contracted 1.9 percent, ending six straight quarters of growth, while manufacturing posted a third consecutive decline, with seven of its 10 divisions reporting weaker output.

The weakness was compounded by rising imports and a second consecutive quarterly decline in investment, as exports grew only modestly and businesses and public corporations pulled back on capital spending.

In June, StatsSA warned that the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East, which erupted in late February and sent fuel prices soaring early in the year, could weigh on second-quarter economic activity.

The economy is expected to feature prominently in November’s local government elections, with unemployment remaining stubbornly high at more than 33 percent, among the highest rates in the world.

Years of weak growth have added to frustration with the government.

Africa’s richest economy shed 345,000 jobs in the second quarter, with most of the losses coming in the community and social services sector.

The economic malaise has deepened disillusionment with the ruling African National Congress, which lost its national majority in 2024 for the first time since the end of apartheid and was forced into an uneasy coalition government with rival parties.

World.title: Iraq advances Chevron, UCC-backed pipeline to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is pushing forward with a vital oil pipeline project with US energy company Chevron, TI Capital, and Qatar’s UCC, which would link Basra to Fishkhabur and branch west toward Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said Tuesday.

Khudair said at the start of the fourth Iraq Oil and Gas Projects and Licensing Rounds Exhibition that the project is critical to Baghdad’s efforts to diversify export routes and provide Iraqi petroleum more flexibility in reaching global markets.

He said that Iraq is working with a consortium of US corporations, including Chevron and TI Capital, as well as its Qatari partner UCC, to build the Basra-Fishkhabur connection and its planned branch to Baniyas.

The route would be especially important for Iraq since the majority of its petroleum exports now depart from southern Arabian Gulf terminals and go via the Strait of Hormuz.

A link between Basra and the Mediterranean would give an alternate outlet during times of difficulty.

The initiative comes as US President Donald Trump has publicly emphasized the construction of new oil pipelines in the Middle East.

Speaking at the White House last week, Trump applauded the trucking of Iraqi oil toward Syria’s Mediterranean coast and said that “many oil pipelines” were being constructed in the area.

Baghdad is also building its northern export route. Khudair said that a deal with Turkey would assist in revitalizing and developing Iraq’s northern exit, complementing the projected routes to Baniyas and providing the nation with several export possibilities.

The Minister said that Iraq’s larger goal goes beyond pipelines to increase production and exports, enhance refining capacity, develop gas resources, and reduce flaring, all while attracting foreign investment and boosting Iraqi energy firms.

According to Khudair, Iraq’s oil exports increased to over 3 million barrels per day in September, up from roughly 200,000 bpd when the present administration took office.

He also revealed that Japan’s JGC has decided to return to Iraq after discussions with the ministry to begin work on the FCC project at the southern refineries, which is part of Baghdad’s aim to enhance local refined petroleum product output.

Khudair said that the government’s ultimate goal is to achieve self-sufficiency in petroleum products, use more of its gas domestically, and eventually grow exports of higher-value refined goods.

Meanwhile, Iraq has maintained its commitment to meeting its OPEC production targets, with output not anticipated to surpass 4.2 million barrels per day.

World.title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300 mn deal
World.content:
London – Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced on Tuesday.

No fee was disclosed by the club, but the BBC reported that the five-year deal was worth £300 million ($406 million) in total.

A contract worth more than £60 million a season, would represent an increase on the current £50 million-per-season deal with retail bank Standard Chartered, who have been the Reds’ front-of-shirt sponsor since 2010.

Liverpool’s new deal is believed to be the most lucrative purely front-of-shirt agreement in Premier League history, with Arsenal and Manchester City’s agreements with Emirates and Etihad Airways respectively also involving stadium naming rights.

By contrast, six-time European champions Liverpool’s home ground is still solely known by its original name of Anfield.

In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League.

Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

Standard Chartered will remain as the shirt sponsor this season before becoming a “global partner” of Liverpool from 2027/28 onwards.

It is understood that talks with Turkish Airlines started before 1892 Holdings — a consortium led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia, the Liverpool vice-chairman, purchased a stake of around 38 percent in the club last month.

Chief commercial officer Ben Latty said that the front of the shirt “holds a special place in the history” of Liverpool, adding that the partnership will build on “strong foundations” from the club’s Champions League final win in the Turkish city of Istanbul in 2005.

Turkish Airlines chief executive Ahmet Olmustur said: “This partnership brings together two global brands united by their international reach, commitment to excellence and ability to inspire millions of people around the world.”

Turkey’s national flag carrier boasts that it flies to 356 destinations in 132 countries. A pet soft-power project of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the company is controlled by the country’s wealth fund, which owns 49.1 percent of its shares.

The company’s network centres on Istanbul airport, which overtook London Heathrow as Europe’s busiest airport in the July summer peak with more than eight million travellers.

World.title: South Lebanon town buries its dead after Israeli strike
World.content:
Kfar Rumman – Hundreds of people in south Lebanon gathered on Tuesday to mourn two Hezbollah members and their family, among them a three-month-old infant, killed by an Israeli strike a day prior.

The two brothers’ coffins, draped in the Iran-backed group’s yellow flag, portraits of them in camouflage fatigues fixed to the front, led the procession through the village battered by repeated conflict over nearly three years.

Another 10 coffins were covered in Lebanese flags, indicating that the rest of the Farhat family killed when Monday’s strike levelled their home were civilians.

Israel has launched airstrikes and a ground invasion in south Lebanon during the Middle East war, which erupted with joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran and spread to Lebanon after Hezbollah targeted Israel in support of its backer.

The fighting in Lebanon had calmed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon were both agreed in June.

But Beirut still reports recurring Israeli strikes, which it says have killed more than 4,300 people in total since March, and Israeli forces continue to occupy what it calls a “security zone” in the south.

A separate strike on Kfar Rumman on Monday killed an 18-year-old rescuer with the Risala Association, linked to the Hezbollah-allied Amal movement, the organisation said, who was mourned alongside the Farhat family on Tuesday.

“We have 13 killed including grandfather and grandmother, husbands and wives, and their children including a three-months old infant,” deputy mayor Nureddine Nureddine told AFP from the funeral.

“Someone put an end to these crimes,” Nureddine said, adding that the strike that killed the Farhat family “occurred at night, while they were sleeping”.

“There was no military activity, nothing.”

An AFP correspondent saw people marching to the cemetery, waving Hezbollah flags as women dressed in black wept, holding pictures of the dead as an Israeli drone flew overhead.

“Death to America, death to Israel,” mourners yelled.

– ‘A shred of honour’ –

The Israeli military said on Monday that it had struck Hezbollah “infrastructure sites” across southern Lebanon after the launch of two explosive drones towards its troops, as well as “several terrorists” it said were transferring weapons.

“The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed,” it said, adding that the military “will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement”.

Since Friday, at least 28 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon’s health ministry.

Standing next to a picture of his own son, a Hezbollah member killed by Israel, Ghaleb Baalbaki slammed the Lebanese government for continuing direct talks with Israel.

“If they have even a shred of honour, the first thing they should do would be to stop the negotiations,” he said.

The lull in violence that began in June had allowed hundreds of thousands of displaced people to return home.

“Kfar Rumman was coming back to life, there were more than 1,400 people” in the town before the latest escalation, Nureddine said,

“Now, they can be counted on your fingers.”

World.title: West Qurna-2 staff threaten strike over dues, risking 324K bpd output
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Dozens of technical, engineering, and administrative personnel operating at the giant West Qurna-2 oilfield in Basra Governorate demonstrated on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, demanding the regularization of their contractual status and the disbursement of overdue wages and entitlements, warning of a general strike if their demands are not addressed within one week.

Speaking a local news agency, protest representative Mashreq Abdul-Moneim declared that Basra Oil Company (BOC) and the operating consortium have been formally notified of the one-week ultimatum. Failure to reach an administrative settlement risks triggering an immediate shutdown of extraction and export infrastructure across one of the country’s most critical hydrocarbon assets.

Core Grievances and Operational Demands

Binding Employment Contracts: Protesters demand formal labor contracts that safeguard statutory benefits, matching the legal and operational standards previously established under Russian operator Lukoil.

Settlement of Financial Arrears: Demonstrators call for the immediate liquidation of all outstanding monetary arrears owed to staff by Basra Oil Company (BOC) without further administrative deferral.

One-Week Strike Ultimatum: Operating staff issued a seven-day deadline to operating partners and state managers, after which personnel intend to stage an open-ended work stoppage.

Disruption to Strategic Production: Abdul-Moneim warned that unresolved labor disputes directly threaten field logistics, where current crude extraction stands at roughly 324,000 barrels per day (bpd) and export volumes reach approximately 347,000 bpd.

West Qurna-2 Operational & Labor Risk Profile

Parameter Current Metric / Indicator Risk Scenario Field Location Northern Basra Governorate Strategic onshore super-giant reservoir Current Crude Output ~324,000 bpd Complete shutdown in case of full operational strike Current Export Volume ~347,000 bpd Severe disruption to southern maritime export streams Operator Framework Lukoil consortium / Basra Oil Company (BOC) Dispute centers on contract parity and state arrears Labor Deadline 7-day formal ultimatum (September 15, 2026) Staged escalations leading to general walkout

West Qurna-2 represents a major pillar of southern crude flows feeding into the Basra Oil Terminal for Basra Medium and Heavy grades. Any labor-induced operational halt would remove over 300,000 bpd from Iraq’s seaborne supply, directly undermining export schedules and tightening the state’s hard-currency revenue streams during a period of acute macroeconomic scrutiny.

World.title: Police clash with degree holders outside Finance Ministry in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Demonstrations organized by long-term university graduates, top-ranking achievers, and higher degree holders turned violent outside the Ministry of Finance in central Baghdad on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, marking the second straight day of confrontations over central public appointments in the draft 2027 federal budget.

Riot police and law enforcement units deployed batons, electric stun devices, tear gas canisters, and rubber rounds to repel hundreds of protestors marching toward the ministry’s perimeter gates. Demonstrators, some wearing burial shrouds to signal resolve, represented a demographic bloc estimating over 100,000 unemployed graduates from past academic cycles across Iraq’s governorates.

Demonstrator Demands and On-the-Ground Clashes

Central Employment Quotas in 2027 Budget: Demonstrators demand the statutory inclusion of centralized recruitment allocations and public service civil numbers for older graduating cohorts within the forthcoming 2027 Federal Budget Law.

Scale of the Crisis: Mobilization organizers emphasized that the national backlog of unhired graduates spans more than 100,000 degree holders across disciplines—some holding computer engineering and technical credentials dated as far back as 2014 without public sector absorption.

Security Escalation and Use of Crowd Control: Protesters reported physical assaults with clubs, electric stun guns, and tear gas. A security source confirmed that while live ammunition was strictly withheld, anti-riot police deployed smoke bombs, tear gas canisters, and rubber bullets to maintain security perimeters.

Arterial Highway Blockades: Following friction on Monday, security forces cordoned off approaches to the strategic Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway after protesters threatened to shut down the arterial transit route.

Key Incident Parameters

Parameter Operational Detail Protest Location Ministry of Finance Headquarters, Central Baghdad Participant Profile Long-term graduates (2014+), top achievers, master’s/PhD holders Estimated Demographic 100,000+ unabsorbed graduates nationwide Core Legislative Demand Statutory civil service quotas / contractual hiring in the 2027 Budget Crowd Control Tactics Smoke grenades, tear gas, electric stun devices, rubber rounds Key Transport Disruptions Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway approach closures

The unrest flared despite an executive directive issued on Monday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, instructing the Ministry of Finance to audit actual ministerial staffing requirements and allocate civil or contractual appointments for older graduates in the upcoming federal budget.

However, demonstrators deemed the directive conditional and inadequate without fixed legislative quotas. The crisis underscores the chronic fiscal dilemma confronting Baghdad: while public compensation and social transfers already swallow an average of 7.438 trillion IQD monthly from the federal treasury, severe private sector employment deficits continue to channel intense popular pressure directly toward state payrolls.

World.title: Baghdad drivers queue for hours as gasoline supplies run low
World.content:
Baghdad — Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war.

Despite being OPEC’s second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand.

In recent weeks, as regional hostilities drag on, long queues have been reappearing every few days, mostly outside government-run fuel stations in Baghdad and other provinces.

Baghdad resident Ibrahim Hashem waited for two hours outside a fuel station on Friday without any luck, only to return early the next day hoping to fill his car.

“It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs,” Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.

“We already suffer from traffic congestion because of the roads and lack of services. Now, it has become worse due to the gasoline shortage,” he added.

Iraq’s average daily consumption of gasoline is 33 million liters, but demand rises to 38 million when people panic over shortages, according to authorities.

The oil ministry said Friday that “regional events and the ongoing conflict are causing logistical challenges to tanker traffic, delaying their arrival at Iraqi ports.”

It urged citizens to buy only the quantities they need and avoid crowding fuel stations for small amounts of gasoline.

Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Friday that his ministry was addressing the “temporary shortage of gasoline” and that new shipments will arrive soon to help stabilize supplies.

Like other oil producers, Iraq has been greatly affected by the US-Iran conflict, which has choked off the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq is hugely dependent on oil exports, which make up about 90 percent of its budget revenues.

Before the war erupted in February, Iraq produced around four million barrels per day, and exported an average of 3.4 million bpd, mostly via Hormuz.

After a significant drop, Iraqi oil exports recovered to more than 2.2 million bpd in August, according to the oil ministry.

Last month, Iran’s state news agency IRNA said that over the past six months, Tehran has granted permission to “a number of Iraqi oil tankers” to pass through Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq rules out airspace closure, launches 9 international routes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Transport ruled out any imminent closure of national airspace amid regional security tensions, announcing the successful activation of alternative air transit corridors alongside the launch of nine new international flight destinations connecting Baghdad, Kirkuk, and Basra to regional and global hubs.

Speaking to the official state newspaper reported on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, the Director General of the General Company for Airport Management and Air Navigation, Ihab Saad, affirmed that Iraq’s flight information region (FIR) remains safe, stable, and fully operational, logging over 500,000 passengers during the third quarter of 2026 alone.

Airspace Stability and Navigation Measures

Alternative Air Corridors: In technical collaboration with international civil aviation bodies (including ICAO), the ministry established flexible alternate transit routes to bypass regional friction zones, with technical evaluations underway to open additional corridors.

Continuous Open Skies: Saad stressed that Iraqi airspace did not experience any operational closures over recent months despite sharp regional escalations, maintaining uninterrupted overflight transit revenues and commercial passenger flows.

Overflight Readiness: Authorities maintain direct operational coordination with transit carriers, anticipating a return to historical direct flight paths as regional de-escalation takes hold.

Q3 2026 Passenger Milestone: Robust passenger throughput surpassed 500,000 travelers across domestic airports in Q3 2026, underscoring sustained commercial confidence in Iraqi civil aviation infrastructure.

The Ministry of Transport’s civil aviation expansion program establishes direct point-to-point connections across three key domestic gateways:

Departure Airport New International Routes Strategic Corridor Baghdad International Airport (BGW) Moscow, Tunis, Muscat Eastern Europe, North Africa & GCC integration Kirkuk International Airport (KIK) Antalya, Beirut, Dubai, Trabzon Tourism hubs, Levant link & GCC transit Basra International Airport (BSR) Baku, Delhi South Caucasus trade & South Asian commercial link

Saad noted that routing alternatives and destination additions form part of a structured civil aviation strategy to maximize sovereign revenue from overflight transit fees and airport usage charges:

World.title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta found hanging at Noida residence, dies by suicide
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Delhi chief secretary

, who served during chief minister

âs tenure, allegedly died by suicide at his residence in Noida, officials said on Tuesday.

Mehta, 74, a 1975-batch IAS officer, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at his Sector 82 residence on September 6, officials told news agency PTI.

Noida Police recovered a purported suicide note in which he cited his "mental and health issues" as the reasons behind the extreme step.

Mehta's body was cremated at the Lodhi Road crematorium on Monday.

Mehta served as Delhi's chief secretary for more than three years, taking charge in 2007 and retiring in November 2010. The 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi were organised during his tenure.

He was credited with overseeing the execution of several key transport, power and civic infrastructure projects in the national capital.

Mehta held several positions in the Delhi government during his career and also served as commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, according to his former colleagues.

(with inputs from PTI)

NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has demolished 24 properties and sealed seven illegal structures across the capital following the building collapse in south Delhiâs Satya Niketan that killed seven people.According to the MCD data, quoted by news agency PTI, the civic body stepped up its enforcement drive against unauthorised construction, carrying out demolition action against 17 properties and sealing five on Tuesday alone. It also issued nine show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, two notices for sealing and 15 demolition orders, the report said.On Monday, the MCD had demolished seven properties, sealed two and issued 26 show-cause notices for unauthorised construction, four notices for sealing and 12 demolition orders.The action follows the collapse of a five-storey building in Satya Niketan on Sunday, which killed at least seven people and injured several others. World.title: No rooms, Rs 2.3 lakh a night: BRICS Summit sends Delhi hotel rates soaring
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As India prepares to host the 18th BRICS Leadersâ Summit, luxury hotels in the national capital are facing a sharp squeeze in room availability, with tariffs at some marquee properties climbing beyond Rs 2 lakh a night ahead of the September 12-13 gathering.

The summit, which brings leaders of the expanded BRICS grouping to Delhi and marks two decades since the blocâs founding, is driving concentrated demand for high-end accommodation, with several premium hotels showing limited or no availability and others quoting rates of more than Rs 2 lakh per night, according to news agency PTI.

Booking checks showed no room availability at Taj Mahal and The Oberoi in New Delhi for September 11-12, while Taj Palace had no rooms available for September 10-12.

The Leela Palace, New Delhi, was also not accepting bookings for stays between September 10 and 12.

At ITC Maurya, New Delhi, rooms available for September 10-13 were commanding tariffs starting at more than Rs 2.3 lakh a night.

The surge comes as delegates and other visitors are expected to arrive in the capital ahead of the two-day summit and extend their stays, putting pressure on room inventory, particularly in central Delhi.





K B Kachru, president, Hotel Association of India (HAI) and Chairman - South Asia, Radisson Hotel Group, said the summit was highlighting the pressure on India's hospitality infrastructure.

"India is commanding global attention at a defining moment -- as the nation prepares to host marquee international events and cements its position as a premier MICE destination, the world is watching how we scale to meet our tourism targets.

"The BRICS Summit alone will put considerable focus on room inventory and that spotlight is exposing a hard truth: our hospitality infrastructure has not kept pace with our tourism ambition," he said, according to PTI.

Kachru said India currently has only about 200,000-220,000 branded hotel rooms, which he described as inadequate for the country's tourism ambitions.

The demand is also being felt beyond central Delhi. Rahool Macarius, Market Managing Director, Eurasia, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, said the summit was creating a distinct demand pattern across Delhi-NCR.

"At Ramada Encore by Wyndham, Dwarka Expressway, this event-led demand is reflected in occupancy for September 12-15, currently tracking at 65 per cent, significantly ahead of the broader market demand," he said.

For tourists, business travellers and families visiting Delhi during the period, the squeeze could mean higher accommodation costs or a shift towards hotels outside central areas and lower-priced properties.

World.title: India, China hold first high-level military flag talks in Arunachal amid LAC tensions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and China have held their first Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting in the Arunachal Pradesh sector, with talks taking place on both sides of the frontier earlier this week.

The meeting followed understandings reached during the Special Representatives dialogue between National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi. The talks are part of efforts by the two countries to maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and gradually improve bilateral ties.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.

New military mechanism along eastern frontier

Jaiswal said the meeting followed agreements reached during the Special Representatives talks in August 2025 and August 2026, along with subsequent discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination.

"Pursuant to the understandings reached between the Special Representatives of India and China in August 2025 and August 2026, and subsequent discussions at the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination meetings held in Beijing and New Delhi in May and August 2026 respectively, the first Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and Damai on the Chinese side on September 7," Jaiswal said at his weekly media briefing.





"A similar mechanism also exists in the Western Sector," he said.

The talks took place amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops along the LAC in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh.

Jaiswal also said that India-China relations are gradually moving in a "positive direction".

Border peace remains key to improving ties

Doval and Wang, who are the designated Special Representatives for the India-China boundary talks, held their latest dialogue in Beijing last month.

During the meeting, the two sides discussed the delimitation of the boundary, trans-boundary cooperation and the need to maintain peace along the LAC.

The Indian side stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border are important for the continued development of bilateral relations.

The latest military engagement comes days before Chinese president Xi Jinping is expected to visit India for the BRICS summit. Xi is likely to arrive in New Delhi on Saturday.

World.title: Channi vs Warring: Why Sachin Pilot may be Congress's best bet in Punjab
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress leadership last week finally responded to 'Mayday' calls from Punjab rebels and brought in

, replacing

, to prevent a crash landing of the deeply fractured state unit ahead of the assembly elections early next year.

Months of open infighting between Charanjit Singh Channi, the former chief minister leading the rebel camp, and Raja Warring, the state unit chief, not just embarrassed the Congress but also threatened to derail its 2027 campaign.

Before being put in the driver's seat in Punjab, Pilot was in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel remains a key Congress leader and former chief minister.

Why Congress was forced to budge

The Congress had sent former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhagel to Punjab in February this year to defuse the brewing Channi vs Warring crisis in the state unit.

Ironically, as things turned out, Baghel faced resistance and became part of the crisis, with the Channi camp openly accusing him of siding with Warring. More so, since July, after the partyâs central leadership decided to ignore Channiâs claim for the top post in the state and announced that it would continue with Warring as state Congress president.

Bhupesh Baghel had asserted that it is not a 'child's play' and the decision of the high command will not change.

With several senior state leaders backing Channi, the fight turned ugly and Baghel became ineffective.





Congress meetings in the districts saw open âGo back Baghelâ chants from Channi supporters, taking the infighting to the streets and embarrassing the top leadership.

So, while the ruling Aam Aadmi Party was already in full election mode with chief minister Bhagwant Mann at the centre of its campaign, the Congress was still struggling to get its senior leadership to sit across the table.

Not just the AAP, even the BJP and the Akalis had their house in order and were planning their electoral moves on the ground.

With the party's 2027 campaign failing to take off under Baghel, the Congress was forced to budge and turn to Pilot.

Why Sachin Pilot

The Congress decision to send Pilot to Punjab, while ironic, may still be the best bet for the leadership. Sachin Pilot, during his years in the Congress, has seen enough internal wars to know how quickly a fight over one post can turn into a larger battle over leadership, political space and, of course, eventually the chief minister's chair.

Throwback to Rajasthan, where he spent years at the centre of a similar leadership tussle with senior leader Ashok Gehlot. Pilot brings something the Congress needs badly right now: the experience of being at the centre of a difficult internal power struggle.

Punjab Congress working president welcomed Sachin Pilotâs appointment, saying it will help iron out differences within the state unit.

Pilot has led the Rajasthan unit, worked closely with the high command, weathered the bitter internal battle, survived the fallout and then rebuilt his position within the Congress.

He was appointed Rajasthan Congress chief in 2014, after the party's abysmal performance in the 2013 assembly election. Over the next four years, he emerged as one of the key faces of the party's rebuilding effort before Congress returned to power in 2018. That victory, however, did not give him the chief minister's chair.

Ashok Gehlot became chief minister, while Pilot was made deputy chief minister and continued as PCC president.

While both sides got something, the arrangement never really settled the rivalry between Gehlot and Pilot.

By 2020, those differences exploded into an open rebellion.

Pilot left Jaipur with a group of MLAs and challenged the Gehlot government. Congress responded by removing him as deputy chief minister and state president. The Gehlot camp even accused him of working with the BJP. A truce was eventually worked out, and Pilot stayed with Congress.

But he never quite returned to the position he had occupied before and has been on the sidelines ever since. He remained a prominent face in the party and was later given charge of Chhattisgarh, but his role in Rajasthan remained limited.

It is interesting how, in Rajasthan, Pilot was the leader asking the Congress high command to listen to a dissatisfied camp. In Punjab, he now has to convince dissatisfied leaders to accept the high command's decisions and work together.

That may be why Congress believes he is best suited for the job.

Baghel gone. Will Warring be next?

But will Pilotâs appointment end the crisis in the Punjab unit?

Channi's supporters had demanded Warring be removed as Punjab Congress chief, and the Jalandhar MP be declared Congressâs chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly polls. The Congress has not accepted either of the two demands. So, while Channi has not made any significant gains, Warring has been left wondering if he will be the next to be axed.

Warring was picked up to lead and rebuild the Punjab unit after the Congress was decimated in the 2022 assembly polls. Channi, who was the chief minister then, led the Congress to its worst-ever performance in the state. The Congress not just lost its government to AAP but was also reduced to 18 seats in the 117-member assembly.

The leadership tussle between the two had been brewing for quite some time. But as is the Congressâs wont, the party kept dilly-dallying on the issue for nearly 4 years.

Finally, when the Congress did take a decision, it ended up opening deep faultlines.

For now, both camps have welcomed his appointment. Warring said Pilot's energy and dynamism would "for sure" add to the vigour of the party ahead of the crucial polls, while Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, a close associate of Channi, said Pilot's experience, leadership and connect with the people would give new strength and momentum to the Congress in Punjab.

Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka hopes that under Pilotâs leadership all state leaders would come together. "Pilot knows all leaders of Punjab, and they also have confidence in him," said Verka.

For Pilot, this may be his first real test. If party leadership decides to keep Warring, he has to get Channi, Randhawa and other leaders to fall in line. If Warring goes, he has to make sure one problem is not replaced by the other.

Congress has a lot at stake

The Congress, which remains the main challenger for now, cannot afford this infighting because Punjab is one of the states where it still has a real chance. There is anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government.

In 2022, AAP swept 92 of the 117 assembly seats, while Congress was reduced to 18. But the 2024 Lok Sabha election brought some relief for the grand old party. The Congress won seven of Punjab's 13 seats, compared with AAP's three, showing that the party still has enough ground to be a serious challenger.

AAP is perhaps no longer riding the wave that brought it to power in 2022 and is now defending its record under Bhagwant Mann. Raghav Chadha's exit has also added to the churn in the party.

The BJP and the Akalis are still on the margins of the stateâs politics. But the scenario could change very fast. The BJP is going all out to broaden its organisational base and rope in leaders from other parties. There are also reports of talks between the BJP and the Akalis to revive their old alliance.

The Congress needs to remember that the BJP is coming off a massive victory in West Bengal and is looking to expand its footprint in Punjab as well.

Punjab could shape Pilot's Rajasthan future

Pilot has already made it clear that he sees Punjab as a comeback opportunity for the Congress. On Monday, he said he was confident that with a strong organisation, collective effort and the energy of party workers, Congress could return to power in the state.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Pilot has the experience of being a part of successful strategising in Himachal Pradesh in the previous assembly polls and has also been a senior observer for the Kerala polls, where Congress returned to power after a decade.

If Pilot can manage to bring the rival Punjab camps together and help the Congress put up a strong show in 2027, it will add to his standing within the party at a time when Rajasthan is already looking ahead to the 2028 assembly election.

There has long been speculation over a bigger role for Pilot in Rajasthan. He may not have got it yet, but a successful Punjab stint could considerably strengthen his case.

For a leader who has had to rebuild his own position in the party before, Punjab could well become the next big step in that comeback.

World.title: 'Not intended to hurt anyone': CM Vijay clarifies gesture in TN assembly after DMK protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday clarified that a gesture he made during his Assembly speech was inadvertent and "not in any way intentional" .

This comes as

accused him of attempting to body-shame former chief minister MK Stalin.

The clarification came amid a major uproar in the Tamil Nadu assembly, where DMK MLAs demanded that Vijay's remarks, including references based on Enforcement Directorate documents and the Sarkaria Commission, be expunged from the records. The protesting legislators were later evicted from the House by marshals after Speaker JCD Prabhakar rejected their demand.

In a post on X, Vijay said his body language during his response to the police department's grant request on September 7 should not be interpreted as a personal attack.

"I wish to clarify that, during my response speech on the police department's grant request in the Legislative Assembly on 7.9.2026, my body language, which inadvertently came across in between, was not in any way intentional. Therefore, I kindly request that it not be interpreted as an act intended to hurt anyone's feelings on a personal level," Vijay said.





The controversy centres on a gesture Vijay made while referring to the history of the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), when he placed his right palm against his jaw. The gesture was widely interpreted as a reference to Stalin's broken jaw, which he suffered after being assaulted during his detention under MISA during the Emergency.

CPI(M) leader P Shanmugam criticised Vijay, accusing him of making a personal attack on Stalin.

"It is a well-known historical fact that the Emergency period in India witnessed massive struggles to protect democracy, accompanied by repression and excesses. During that time, former chief minister MK Stalin was brutally assaulted by the police, resulting in a broken jaw," Shanmugam said in a post on X.

"Ridiculing someone's physical appearance is condemnable, regardless of who engages in it; for the Chief Minister himself to do so is an act of irresponsibility," he added.

DMK protests over Vijay's remarks

The assembly witnessed heated exchanges on Tuesday after DMK Whip EV Velu demanded that Vijay's references to ED allegations of graft and the Sarkaria Commission be removed from the records.

Velu also objected to references to people who were not present in the House to defend themselves, as well as references to deceased individuals.

He argued that the Sarkaria Commission had examined 28 charges and claimed that no legal action could follow as the charges were not proved.

"Bringing this up without evidence is misleading," he contended.

Velu also objected to Vijay's references to the MISA period, saying that repeated discussion of the issue and personal attacks on individuals were inappropriate.

State law minister R Nirmal Kumar defended Vijay's remarks, saying they were based on official ED documents and the Sarkaria Commission report. He also reiterated allegations of corruption against the then DMK regime.

Kumar disputed claims concerning Stalin's arrest under MISA, arguing that it was linked to derogatory comments made against former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi regarding her "21-point programme".

Leader of the House K A Sengottaiyan said there was no reason to expunge Vijay's remarks, citing a precedent in which late Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa had also spoken about the issue.

The DMK members continued to protest after Speaker Prabhakar ruled against expunging the remarks. Several MLAs gathered before the Speaker's podium and raised slogans despite repeated appeals to return to their seats.

Prabhakar eventually ordered marshals to evict the protesting MLAs. The legislators continued raising slogans as they were taken out of the Assembly hall.

World.title: Digital asset firms seek sovereign funds’ backing at Delhi meet
World.content:
Digital asset companies from BRICS and partner countries will seek a bigger place in cross-border payments and institutional investment

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Digital asset firms will seek sovereign investorsâ backing at a Delhi roundtable this week as India pursues faster, cheaper international payments while maintaining that replacing the dollar is outside its financial agenda.The September 12 BRICS Digital Asset Round Table will bring together 50 industry leaders at The Oberoi. Organiser Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute (SWFI) says investors attending the accompanying iBRICS summit manage $1 trillion across sovereign funds, pension funds and family offices. The figure represents assets under management.Held alongside the BRICS leadersâ summit, the industry meeting will examine linking national digital currencies and payment networks, including Indiaâs UPI and Brazilâs Pix. Separately, companies will explore investment in infrastructure, energy, property and critical minerals through digital tokens representing rights in underlying assets.The payments argument has a practical basis. International transfers can involve several banks and currency conversions, adding costs and delays. Connecting domestic systems could shorten that chain, benefiting businesses and people sending money abroad.RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said on August 11 that BRICS discussions covered central bank digital currencies and fast-payment links, with reducing costs a priority. The options remained under discussion. India has also supported wider use of local currencies for trade.That agenda carries diplomatic sensitivities. New Delhi has said de-dollarisation is outside its financial programme, while US President Donald Trump has threatened 100% tariffs against BRICS countries seeking to replace the dollar.Indiaâs participation in Project Nexus, designed to connect domestic instant-payment systems, shows its engagement extends beyond BRICS. Another initiative, mBridge (Multiple Central Bank Digital Currency Bridge), was developed with China and other central banks to enable payments using central bank digital currencies. These parallel projects suggest that decisions about who governs payment networks will accompany choices about speed and cost.At the Delhi meeting, participants are expected to sign an industry charter covering issuance, custody, settlement and investor protection. Regulators and officials implementing digital currency programmes are expected as observers, organisers said.Linking central bank currencies, investing in tokenised projects and regulating private digital assets involve separate policy decisions. The charter would set industry principles within the rules laid down by governments. For investors, enforceable ownership and reliable custody remain central to assessing tokenised projects.âUntil now the allocators of sovereign capital and the builders of those rails have sat in different rooms,â SWFI chairman Lakshmi Narayanan said. The roundtableâs proposed charter seeks to give investors and authorities a shared reference for transactions across borders.

World.title: NIT-T team earns patent for paver blocks developed from soil-like material in landfills
World.content:
A patent has been granted to two professors of National Institute of Technology – Tiruchi (NIT-T) for the invention of paver blocks using Soil-Like Material (SLM) obtained from landfill biomining, it was announced on Tuesday.

According to an official press release, the patent has been granted to the institute recognising the inventive method on September 3, 2026. The patent is valid for a term of 20 years from April 29, 2025, in accordance with the provisions of the Patents Act, 1970.

Led by civil engineering professor S. T. Ramesh and Prime Minister’s Research Fellow G. Saravanan, the initiative provides a circular-economy answer to using up remains of biomining legacy waste. While plastics and combustibles find downstream uses as Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF), the process leaves behind an overwhelming volume of SLM.

The research was carried out in collaboration with the Tiruchi City Corporation and biomining contractor Zigma Global Environ Solutions Pvt. Ltd.

For long, SLM has had no steady commercial market as most municipalities resort to depositing it into low-lying land, risking persistent groundwater and soil contamination as residual pollutants leach out over time, said the researchers. “Finding a safe, structurally viable outlet for fine landfill soil has been the missing link in remediating urban dump sites,” they noted. Rather than treating this fraction as an environmental hazard, the NIT–T team examined its geo-environmental behaviour and found that it mirrors standard construction-grade fine sand.

Through intensive trials, the team developed specialised building units named ‘SLiM Blocks’. According to laboratory tests, replacing conventional sand with processed SLM at an optimum 15% ratio delivers the necessary compressive durability for pedestrian and light-vehicular traffic.

The fabrication process stabilises the material matrix, dramatically arresting the leaching of heavy metals and toxins that would otherwise escape into the ecosystem.

Over 130 dumpsites are currently undergoing active bioremediation in Tamil Nadu. If adopted by municipal corporations for municipal sidewalks, civic parks, and pedestrian plazas, the patented innovation could substantially lower consumption of virgin river and manufactured sand while clearing the very dumpyards suffocating Indian cities, said the NIT-T researchers.

World.title: Farmers’ association seeks special initiatives to support samba cultivation
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam, affiliated to the Communist Party of India, has urged the State government to implement special initiatives to support samba paddy cultivation this year.

“As income from the kuruvai season has been lost, there is a need to protect the samba crop. The government should initiate steps to support the cultivation, right from its commencement to harvest,” a resolution adopted at the association’s State committee meeting held here on Tuesday.

Samba and thaladi paddy has to be raised on 16 lakh acres and farmers cannot afford to lose the crop too. Hence the State government should take steps to get Tamil Nadu’s quota of Cauvery water due from Karnataka by launching a legal battle. From November 15, 16,000 cusecs of water should be released in the Cauvery from Mettur Reservoir, and water should be distributed from Kallanai on a turn system. The Water Resources Department should deploy laskars to monitor and ensure that the water reached the tail-end areas.

The government should supply seeds of short and medium paddy varieties and inputs, including fertilizers, at 50% subsidy. Fifty per cent subsidy should be given for machine planting. Funds should be allocated immediately for all the initiatives and farmers should be given necessary advice and technological support through the season. The crop insurance scheme should be implemented by the government and not by private companies.

Further, the government must withdraw the Bill introduced in the Assembly to amend the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971, seeking to dispense with the requirement of obtaining prior concurrence of District Collectors for the development of wetlands in non-planning areas and to empower the Director to grant prior permission to the local authority in respect of such wetlands. The Bill, if adopted, would ruin agriculture in the name of urban development, another resolution said.

The meeting was attended S.Gunasekaran, State president, and P.S.Masilamani, State general secretary, and other office bearers of the association.

World.title: Russia welcomes India’s contribution to end Ukraine crisis: Kremlin spokesperson
World.content:
A week after Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated his call for an end to the Ukraine-Russia war on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, in a virtual press interaction with the Indian media on Tuesday (September 8, 2026), said that both India and Russia want a peaceful end to the war that has continued for more than four and a half years. Mr. Peskov provided a positive outlook for the upcoming BRICS Summit, to be held in New Delhi on September 12-13, and announced that President Vladimir Putin will hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of the summit, and welcomed India’s contribution to end the war.

“We know the position of India on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent, it corresponds with our own position, because we do want the solution of the Ukrainian conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open to this process,” Mr. Peskov said, adding, “We welcome the willingness of the Indian side to contribute.”

Mr. Peskov noted that there are Indian citizens who are on the front lines with Ukraine, saying that Russia has asked for a list of such individuals, whom India claims were fraudulently lured to fight in Ukraine on Russia’s behalf. “They will be sent back,” Mr. Peskov said. The Official Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) said that there are around 24 Indian citizens who continue to remain in the Russian armed forces and are engaged in the Russia-Ukraine frontlines.

Mr. Peskov said Mr. Modi and Mr. Putin will meet on Friday (September 11, 2026) ahead of the BRICS Summit, and added, “Like always, they will touch on the bilateral agenda. Trade and economic cooperation have a very wide scope.” He referred to the challenges of sanctions from the U.S. for Indian energy purchases from Russia. “You know that lots of issues cannot be discussed publicly, having some unfriendly countries that are trying to put obstacles in the way of further development of our cooperation. So, it is being discussed discreetly, but in a very, very constructive manner,” Mr. Peskov said.

India has been arguing that the purchase of Russian oil is a policy that is taken in light of the energy requirements of the Indian people. Mr. Peskov exuded confidence about an increase in the bilateral energy trade. “I won’t give you a figure. Every month we have a new record,” he said. He referred to the U.S.’s Russia Sanctions Bill, which seeks to impose sanctions on countries that do energy trade with Russia, as “illegal, unfair, unacceptable”.

On the expectations and challenges ahead of the BRICS Summit that will be chaired by India this time, Mr. Peskov said that BRICS is not “anti-Western”, and that it is a grouping of countries that share an outlook. He further confirmed that President Putin will meet Prime Minister Modi on the sidelines of the summit. Earlier, in May 2026, big differences between Iran and the UAE had prevented the BRICS Foreign Ministers’ meeting from coming out with a joint statement, and there are lingering feelings that these differences could hamper a joint statement at the summit. Mr. Peskov referred to hostilities between Iran and the UAE, saying Russia is a “good friend” of both countries, and that Moscow is ready to contribute in normalisation of ties, if necessary.

World.title: YSRCP Vizianagaram president Majji Srinivasa Rao joins TDP
World.content:
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Vizianagaram Zilla Parishad Chairperson and District president Majji Srinivasa Rao has joined the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in the presence of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at the CM’s camp office on Tuesday.

Mr. Naidu welcomed Mr. Srinivasa Rao into the TDP by draping the party scarf around him. Mr. Srinivasa Rao’s daughter Siri Sahasra also joined the party and was welcomed by the Chief Minister

Earlier on Tuesday Mr. Srinivasa Rao submitted his resignation letter to former Chief Minister and YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, citing personal reasons. He also resigned from the post of YSRCP in-charge for the Bhimili assembly constituency.

According to sources Mr. Srinivasa Rao who belongs to the Kapu community, had reportedly developed differences with his uncle Botcha Satyanarayana, former Minister and Leader of the Opposition in the A.P. Legislative Council. Sources said: “Mr. Srinivasa Rao’s move to join the TDP comes ahead of the local body elections.”

Mr. Srinivasa Rao had played a key role in YSRCP’s victory in the 2019 local body elections. The YSRCP had won all 34 Zilla Praja Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) seats and more than 90% of the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) seats in the district.

World.title: Rejecting Dhirendra Shastri’s advice, several BJP leaders say Bengalis will eat non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja
World.content:
A day after the president of the West Bengal unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Samik Bhattacharya said Bengalis would eat fish and meat during Durga Puja, rejecting the advice of the chief priest of Bageshwar Dham Dhirendra Krishna Shastri to follow a vegetarian diet during the pujas, several other BJP leaders came out in Mr. Bhattacharya’s support.

From Ministers of the West Bengal government to veteran party leaders, everyone followed the line taken by Mr. Bhattacharya. However, none of them criticised the self-styled godman, and some said that there was nothing wrong in promoting vegetarianism.

“Our State party president has clearly said that any person coming from outside will not understand our culture. In other States, during Durga Puja, everyone eats vegetarian food. But if he thinks that the same culture is here, it is not the case here. Here (in West Bengal) we save money so that we can have mutton and fish,” Minister for Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Agnimitra Paul said.

There was a tradition of offering animal sacrifices during Durga Puja and Kali Puja, and meat is offered as ‘prasad’’, Panchayat Minister and former State BJP president Dilip Ghosh said. “Some saints say that eating vegetarian food is good, but that is not a compulsion in West Bengal,” Mr. Ghosh said.

Senior BJP leader and West Bengal Industries Minister Tapas Roy, said that “each religion has its own rules but people will eat whatever they want”. “Our president Shamik Bhattacharya has also clarified that people will follow their own rules relating to religion and eat what they want,” Mr. Roy said.

West Bengal BJP veteran and former Tripura Governor Tathagata Roy said Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks were a non-issue. “Those who want to follow him, do so by all means — not eating non-veg food will hurt no one. And those who, like me, will eat non-veg food anyway, will ignore him. So, what’s all this hullabaloo about?” Mr. Roy said.

Dhirendra Shastri, also known as ‘Bageshwar Baba’, made the remark while addressing his devotees at an event in Liluah on September 6, 2026. “I want to appeal to the Hindus of Bengal that during Navratri, even if you don’t keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell non-veg near the idols,” the self-styled godman said.

The remark had triggered strong reactions from the people of the State, including leaders of Opposition parties. The Madhya Pradesh-based religious preacher was welcomed to the State by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who, along with members of the Cabinet, had dinner with him.

On September 7, Mr. Bhattacharya appeared to attempt damage control by saying nobody could ask Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food.

“How can Bengalis not have fish and meat? Even Swami Vivekananda said Ma Kali will have mutton [as an offering]. It is dangerous if someone tries to rise above Vivekananda. This is his (Shastri’s) personal opinion,” Mr. Bhattacharya had said. The BJP leader, however, added that there was no sin in advocating vegetarianism.

Political parties in the Opposition have targeted the BJP over the issue. While the Congress party lodged a police complaint against Dhirendra Shastri at the Bhawanipur police station, Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) leader Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said it was not Bageshwar Baba but those who had invited him to the State who were to be blamed.

Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh said the State government, and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who was patronising Bageshwar Baba, should offer clarification. “This is not just a matter of filing a complaint…There is a government that is patronising all this. The friends of this government come and insult Bengal and Bengalis whenever they wish,” Mr. Ghosh said.

World.title: Delhi High Court declines urgent hearing on plea for Delhi University hostels
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday declined to take up for urgent hearing urgently a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking hostel facilities for students in all Delhi University colleges, observing that such a direction could not be issued at the interim stage.

A Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia questioned the need for urgent listing of the plea and asked the lawyer to file it for auto-listing on Wednesday.

The plea was mentioned for urgent listing following the building collapse at Satya Niketan near Delhi University’s South Campus, which claimed seven lives.

The plea sought a direction to every Delhi University college to provide hostel facilities to students. The lawyer told the court that the PIL was distinct from another petition heard on Monday, which sought, among other reliefs, compensation for the families of those killed and injured in the collapse.

The Bench, however, said it could not issue such a direction at the interim stage.

“Can we issue such a direction in the interim? File it. It will be taken up tomorrow,” the Bench said.

High-level inquiry ordered

The court had on Monday ordered a high-level inquiry by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) into the building collapse and made it clear that the government could not evade responsibility for the tragedy.

Calling the incident “most unfortunate”, the High Court said such tragedies reflected inadequate measures by the MCD and other authorities and directed them to intensify rescue efforts to save lives.

The court had also flagged concerns over the lack of adequate hostel facilities run by Delhi University and the government, as well as the safety and security of students and the regulatory measures governing paying guest accommodations.

Meanwhile, building owner Hariram Gupta and his wife were produced before a trial court on Monday and remanded in judicial custody. Their son was sent to two days’ police custody.

World.title: HC sets aside death sentence, acquits convict of all charges
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday set aside the death sentence imposed by a trial court in Sivaganga district on a woodcutter. He was acquitted of all charges.

The court was hearing the referred trial and the criminal appeal filed by Chandran against the judgment of the Principal Sessions Court (POCSO Act Cases), Sivaganga district. In April, the trial court had imposed the death sentence on him for sexually assaulting five girls.

A Division Bench of Justices N. Anand Venkatesh and K. K. Ramakrishnan said on an overall consideration of the record, the court was unable to hold that the accused received a fair and meaningful trial.

The cumulative effect of the denial of an effective opportunity to consult and instruct counsel, the absence of counsel on material occasions, the inadequacy of the record regarding effective cross-examination, procedural irregularities concerning the victims, the deficiencies in identification, and the failure to adhere to the safeguards governing capital sentencing had resulted in a fundamental failure of the trial process, the court said.

The proceedings, in the considered opinion of the court, have been reduced to a mockery of the constitutional guarantee of a fair trial and have resulted in a grave miscarriage of justice. The deficiencies go to the root of the proceedings and cannot be treated as mere irregularities capable of being overlooked, the judges said.

The court held that the conviction and the sentence imposed by the trial court were vitiated by fundamental violations of the accused’s right to a fair trial. The judgment therefore is liable to be set aside, the court said.

The court said the duty of a criminal court is not to convict because the accusation is grave, nor because public sentiment is strong, but to ascertain, with disciplined judicial detachment, whether the prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt.

The court cannot shut its eyes to either the vulnerability of children or the danger of an innocent person being convicted upon evidence which does not attain the standard required by law. The court must remain faithful to evidence even when the allegations evoke strong concern, because the legitimacy of criminal justice lies precisely in its refusal to substitute emotion for proof. Justice must reach the truth, the judges said.

The court must also remember that children should not be made the casualties of an unsuccessful prosecution and an unsuccessful prosecution should not become a source of further suffering to children. Accordingly, in the peculiar facts of the case, the compensation already received by the children need not be recovered, the court said.

Justice Anand Venkatesh, in a postscript to the judgment authored by Justice Ramakrishnan, said the case stands as a classic textbook illustration of how draconian statutory provisions can be weaponized, holding an innocent person beneath the suspended sword of a death sentence. In an era where trial by media often pronounces guilt long before the judicial process concludes, high-profile cases generate intense public expectation. Courts cannot and must not be guided by popular clamor or media narratives. Yet, intense public scrutiny places an extra duty of care upon the bench to ensure every shred of evidence is exhaustively analysed, leaving no stone unturned.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi to take part in multiple events in Rae Bareli
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi reached his parliamentary constituency Rae Bareli on Tuesday for a two-day visit during which he will take part in multiple events. Mr. Gandhi is scheduled to chair a meeting of the District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee. The Congress leader is scheduled to meet bullion traders at Prabhu Town in the city and later meet office-bearers of the Central Bar Association as well as delegations of sportspersons, medical professionals and chemists. On Wednesday, Mr. Gandhi will inaugurate development works completed at a cost of ₹3 crore from his MP Local Area Development Scheme funds. State Congress leaders welcomed Mr. Gandhi at the Lucknow airport while he was enroute to Rae Bareli from New Delhi.

The Congress said people welcomed Mr. Gandhi when he reached Rae Bareli. “A huge crowd, unwavering faith and immense love from loved ones. Today, when ‘Jananayak’ Rahul ji set foot on the land of Raebareli, the entire city thronged to get a glimpse of their beloved leader. Every road from Lahi Border, Maharajganj, Hardaspur to Gol Chowraha was waiting to welcome him with open arms. This selfless love of the people is the real strength of Rahul ji, which gives him the courage to stand firmly against every injustice. This bond of love with the soil of Rae Bareli will remain unbroken,” the Congress posted on X.

World.title: PM Shehbaz seeks input from business community as he stresses export-led growth
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday sought recommendations from industrialists and businesspeople on how to increase export-led growth in the country.

“Whatever growth we have to achieve, it has to be export-led growth, period,” the premier remarked while addressing a meeting with prominent leaders of the business community.

He added that any other kind of growth had “no meaning” and reinforced that economic growth had to be export-led.

“Today’s meeting is because we’re in the first quarter, in the month of September. I need your opinions on how to increase our exports, as well as what challenges we will face and how to address them,” PM Shehbaz said.

The prime minister gave the example of special tax relief to exporters as a means to achieve this growth.

He recalled that in the run-up to the federal budget presented in June this year, the government held multiple meetings and had “intense consultations” with the business community.

“Through your consultations in difficult times, the way we brought structural changes over the past two-and-a-half years … it’s teamwork. It’s a tremendous teamwork,” PM Shehbaz said.

“As a result, we made overdue structural reforms. It’s a long journey, but through enforcement we recovered Rs800 billion in one year. No new taxes were imposed.”

PM Shehbaz praised the teamwork involved between the business community and the government, adding that Pakistan was ready to pursue growth with their input.

In July, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the government was pursuing a strategy to diversify exportable products and market portfolios to achieve a target of six per cent sustainable economic growth.

“Our destination is not only stabilisation but sustainable growth of at least 6pc. That growth has to be export-led; otherwise it will become another economic bubble that bursts within a few years,” he said.

Last Monday, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that the government’s focus was on building an ecosystem to support sustainable growth that was led by the private sector and export-driven.

The minister said Pakistan had moved from stabilisation towards growth, but the key challenge now was to ensure its sustainability.

Earlier this week, PM Shehbaz welcomed the launch of export insurance coverage by the Export Development Fund (EDF) and the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan, saying the facility would help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) expand the country’s exports.

Chairing a meeting on the EDF, he said the Rs3bn risk pool would expand access to export credit insurance, especially for SMEs, and help the business community increase export volumes.

He described the initiative as a highly welcome step to promote small and medium-sized businesses and strengthen the national economy.

World.title: Sindh AG interrupts Mir Raza commission proceedings during police surgeon's testimony, objects to family's queries
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to probe the circumstances and possible negligence around the Mir Raza Ali murder case issued a notice to Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar after the Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero interrupted the proceedings on Tuesday and objected to the lawyer representing the victims’ family asking any questions.

The interruption came during Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed’s testimony.

The order issued after the commission’s proceedings stated: “It is regrettable that the commission’s proceedings have been interrupted by Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero. He has objected to the family’s counsel asking any questions on behalf of the deceased’s family.

“The highest law officer of the Sindh government making such a submission surprised me. It is more meaningful that the disturbance comes at a time when the police surgeon was explaining the role of senior police officers during the post-mortem examination.”

The murder case has been mired in controversy, particularly after Dr Syed pointed out flaws in the findings of Ali’s first autopsy. Following that, Ali’s body was exhumed a second post-mortem was conducted.

Dr Syed was part of the medical board that conducted the second autopsy, whose findings ruled out the possibility of suicide — a likelihood around which the law enforcers had initially tried to build the case. Meanwhile, Ali’s family accused police of trying to bury the facts.

The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, heard the case today and noted in its order that Sindh Assembly member Faryal Talpur had suggested its formation to the provincial chief executive “for a transparent and impartial comprehensive investigation”.

The order cited a Dawn report dated Aug 9, according to which, it said, Talpur stressed that justice for Ali must be ensured and “public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case. The newspaper further cites her as saying that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system was the fundamental responsibility of the government and relevant institutions”.

Sindh Home Minister Lanjar and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had echoed these sentiments, the order stated.

Justice Sial further wrote in the order that he was saddened that the advocate general had objected to requests by Ali’s family through their counsel for certain clarification.

“It is the commission’s discretion to determine whether a query is relevant to the proceedings or not. Further, the commission’s terms of reference required it to find the true facts and circumstances of the case,” he said, adding that a notice was being issued to Lanjar to appear before the commission on Sept 10 and “put forward his stance […] as to whether the family is barred from asking questions to satisfy themselves that justice is being done”.

Justice Sial further stated, “In my opinion, a deliberate attempt has been made by the Sindh advocate general to restrain the commission from addressing the family’s queries in a transparent manner.”

Plea against FIR

In a separate development, a two-member bench of the SHC, headed by Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and including Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri, took up a petition seeking the quashing of a case registered on August 27 against “around 100 people” for staging a protest in connection with the case.

In the first information report (FIR), the protesters have been accused of blocking the road for vehicular movement and pedestrians at Karachi’s Sharea Faisal.

The plea, a copy of which is available with Dawn, named Ammar Ahmed Khan, Muhammad Zubai Ali, Taha Shaikh, Zarar Khalid, Saad Shehriyar, and Hassan Surya as the petitioners.

The SHC issued notices to the Sindh advocate general, the prosecutor general and other respondents for Nov 11 after hearing the plea today, directing that in the meantime, no coercive action should be taken against the petitioners.

The court further directed that the investigation should be conducted strictly in accordance with the law and directed the petitioners to cooperate when required.

“It is clarified that this order shall not be construed as an impediment in conducting the investigation strictly in accordance with law,” the court said.

The case so far

The body of 25-year-old Ali was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28.

Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Dr Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted.
