Tech.title: Insta360 X6 Review (2026): A Great 360 and Action Camera Hybrid
Tech.content:
The combination of good video quality and user-friendly software has kept Insta360 at the forefront of the 360 camera world even as competitors like DJI and GoPro have carved out their own niche. With its latest camera, the Insta360 X6, the company is hoping to leap ahead of the pack again.

The Insta360 X6 brings a slightly larger sensor, faster video frame rates, better low-light performance, and tools to help you spend less time editing and more time filming. While it’s not a huge leap over its predecessor, the X6 is a solid improvement with several new features that might make upgrading worth it for some users.

What’s New

The X6 looks a little bit like if the X5 and the GoPro Max 2 had a baby. It’s shorter, squatter, and a tad bit wider than the X5, but not as small as the Max 2. That might sound like I’m setting it up to say it’s the Goldilocks size, but that’s not really the case. I actually like the individual sizes of the X5 and Max 2 better, the first for its narrower profile and the second for its much smaller overall size.

Along with the smaller size come two other major changes from the X5: the screen is smaller, and the physical buttons at the bottom are gone. Though there is noticeably less coverage, I didn’t find the smaller screen to make much difference. I could still see what I wanted to shoot, but the point of a 360 camera is you don’t need to frame shots. The main thing I use the screen for is making sure that the stitch line isn’t on my main subject.

Tech.title: Gen AI Tools Are Now Being Used to Push ‘Slop Jihad’
Tech.content:
Over a decade ago, the Islamic State released a disturbing video that depicted its members lowering men locked in a cage into a swimming pool and drowning them. Today, that video has been reproduced as a SpongeBob SquarePants cartoon depicting fish in orange jumpsuits inside the cage, as SpongeBob lowers the cage into the water while Squidward films the scene.

The video, shared on TikTok, is part of what a new report from the Institute of Strategic Dialogue (ISD) calls “Slop Jihad,” a trend where young supporters of Islamic terror groups like ISIS and al-Qaeda appear to use generative AI tools to create fan edits, cartoons, and memes designed to radicalize a new generation of online backing.

This shift “signals a fundamental transformation in the aesthetics of jihadist propaganda online,” concludes the report, which was shared exclusively with WIRED.

“The principal concern is the growing volume and diversity of material,” says Adam Hadley, executive director of Tech Against Terrorism, a UN-backed counterterrorism organization that has also written a report about the Slop Jihad trend. “Highly stylized AI-generated content can make violent Islamist extremist material more accessible to younger audiences while reducing the visibility of conventional terrorist branding. Users may encounter perpetrator glorification inadvertently through fan edits, cartoons, memes, and other entertainment-oriented formats, after which engagement can drive algorithmic recommendations of related, more overt propaganda.”

Islamic terror groups have long demonstrated their capacity to adapt to new media environments to get their messages to a wide audience online, leveraging new and emerging technologies to aid recruitment and create a decentralized network of propaganda. This was seen in the early 2020s Alt Jihad movement, which sought to co-opt the aesthetics of the alt-right in the Islamic terrorism content.

These groups have also been making use of generative AI technology for a number of years. In 2024, the Islamic State–affiliated news program News Harvest began using AI-generated anchors to help disseminate propaganda videos quickly and cheaply.

But today, the look and feel of the content produced with generative AI is markedly different.

“This is new, and it's still growing; it has not peaked by any means,” says Moustafa Ayad, the research chair in global Islamism and counterterrorism at ISD. “There's always been really shoddy content that's been produced in the support ecosystem, but it wasn't SpongeBob SquarePants as the Islamic State.”

Generative AI tools have also been utilized to quickly and cheaply turn official content from terror groups into animated videos. In one example, one TikTok account was turning the weekly al-Naba newsletter from ISIS into anime.

The Slop Jihad trend has seen some pushback from more traditional supporters who don’t like the new aesthetic. “There seems to be some animosity towards it, because they don't believe the producers of Slop Jihad are true believers,” Ayad says, referring to some reactions to the SpongeBob video. “But again, some accounts that have shared traditional official propaganda are sharing the newer videos. So there seems to be a love-hate relationship with the Slop Jihad content.”

For years now, TikTok has been central to Islamic terror groups' online messaging campaign, taking advantage of the platform’s powerful algorithmic recommendations to spread their message. A report from the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development in 2024 found that TikTok was among the top 10 platforms used to spread terrorist and extremist content.

While Ayad did find a limited number of Slop Jihad videos on other platforms like Instagram and Facebook, the vast majority of the videos were found on TikTok. In total, he found 150 Slop Jihad videos from 71 accounts with more than 5.4 million total views on the platform. Ayad believes the prevalence of this content on TikTok is due to the platform’s For You Page algorithm “that is hyper-targeted to user interests.” He also credits the high level of general AI slop on the platform and “an existing entrenched ecosystem of jihadist support on the platform.”

Tech.title: Nintendo Reveals Ocarina of Time Remake Release Date, a Zelda Switch 2 and a Real Ocarina
Tech.content:
Nintendo held its The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct on Tuesday to reveal a new release for one of its biggest franchises. The big news was the reveal of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake release date or a special edition Nintendo Switch 2. But the gaming giant also announced an actual ocarina that fans can buy to annoy their friends and family while learning how to play.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will launch on Nov. 5, according to Tuesday’s presentation. A week before its release, a special edition Switch 2 for the 40th anniversary will be released on Oct. 29, along with a Switch 2 Pro Controller and carrying case. Then, to complete the anniversary package for Zelda fans, Nintendo plans to release an official ocarina identical to the one Link plays throughout Ocarina of Time. There will be a traditional acoustic model and an electric version made by Hori.

The main star of Tuesday’s direct was the Ocarina of Time remake. As expected, it will make full use of the Switch 2’s graphics power to give a modern look to the almost 30-year-old game, first released for the N64. Visuals weren’t the only upgrades, as controlling Link is much easier using both analog sticks, which weren’t around in 1998, and instead of jumping automatically near any ledge, there’s a jump button to let Link get across gaps.

Another interesting feature involves the ocarina Link uses in the game. This is a key item as it lets Link do various magical feats when a certain tune is played by pressing the correct buttons. Something different is that players can now hum the tune, and the game will recognize the sound via the Switch 2’s microphone and complete the input to activate the song.

Only the intro sequence of the game in Kokiri Forest and the first section of Hyrule Castle Town were shown during the presentation. All the characters received a visual upgrade as well as voices, with new fully voiced cutscenes. Link, however, is still not going to talk.

First-time players who get lost or a little confused in the game will be able to check out Zelda Notes, a new feature added into the Nintendo Switch app that lets players track their progress, gives some hints on in-game location and provides other info for players.

Before playing Ocarina of Time remake, fans can pick up the Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition system. The new Switch 2 variant will have a unique look on the console and dock inspired by the game. There will also be a Switch 2 Pro Controller and a carrying case with their own inspired looks that will be sold separately. Nintendo also plans to have an exclusive Switch 2 Pro Controller with its own display stand for sale only at the Nintendo Store in New York City and San Francisco.

Nintendo

Then, there’s the ocarina. Two ocarinas will be available for purchase: a standard acoustic ocarina and an electric one made by Hori that can play songs via a button. Eiji Aonuma, the producer of the Zelda series, gave a demo of how the ocarina sounds during the show. Nintendo didn’t provide a price or release date for these ocarinas, but it said in a press release that they will be available later this year.

Nintendo/Screenshot by CNET

Other Zelda news mentioned in the show was the April 30, 2027, release date for a film based on the game, officially called The Legend of Zelda. A 40th anniversary concert series featuring the game’s music will also kick off in January in Japan and in February in the US, starting in Chicago. Also out next year are the Young Link and Young Zelda amiibo figures.

Nintendo didn’t officially put a price on the Ocarina of Time remake, but the digital version is expected to be $60. There is a listing for the physical version of the game on the Nintendo Store for $70 that appeared shortly after the presentation and was taken down by Nintendo. It’s unclear what items shown during the event will be available at other retailers and which ones will be available only through the Nintendo Store.

Tech.title: Everything We Expect to See (and Not See) at Tomorrow’s Apple ‘Surprise and Shine’ Event: A Folding iPhone, New AirPods and Watch Series 12
Tech.content:
The wait is almost over. Apple is set to reveal its fall hardware lineup on Wednesday, Sept. 9, at its “Surprise and shine” event. And from everything we know so far, the event will be unlike most others.

For one, this year’s event is a bit sentimental for the Cupertino company. Tim Cook announced in April that he is stepping down from his role as CEO, a job he has held for nearly 15 years after legendary Apple co-founder Steve Jobs stepped down in 2011. John Ternus, the company’s hardware engineering chief, stepped into the role just days before the event.

Apple is also heavily rumored to break with its usual routine by holding off on releasing a base iPhone 18 until next year, meaning only the more expensive Pro models will be revealed in September. That would give another highly anticipated release center stage: the foldable device expected to be called the iPhone Ultra.

We’ll be keeping a close eye on the price tags. Apple raised prices across its computer and home devices this summer, attributing the cost increases to memory chip supply chain issues, largely driven by the AI race. Additional price hikes on Apple Music and Apple TV subscriptions aren’t helping cash-strapped consumers, either.



New iPhone 18 models, joining the foldable fun

Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup is likely going to look a little different this year. One of the biggest rumors is that Apple is going to do an extended rollout. This September, we expect to see the foldable iPhone Ultra, the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, but we likely won’t get the base iPhone 18, iPhone 18E and a possible iPhone Air 2 until spring 2027.

The iPhone Ultra, as Apple’s much-rumored first foldable phone is tentatively named, has a book-style design, according to analyst leaks. Think more Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which opens like a book into a mini tablet — not like an OG ’90s flip phone.

But the possible $2,000 price tag means the Ultra likely won’t be a replacement for the base iPhone 18. More likely, it will be more of a luxury option. That may be one reason why a majority of US adults (75%) don’t care about foldable phones, a recent CNET survey found.

We had CNET’s creative director show us what we could expect from the new potential iPhone 18 colors. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max models are rumored to have bigger batteries, variable-aperture cameras and run on the new Apple A20 processor. More satellite connectivity, a smaller Dynamic Island and tweaked back camera islands are also possibilities. And these new phones could come in colors such as light blue, dark cherry and dark gray.

Running on all these devices is the already announced new family of operating systems. iOS 27, with the anticipated Siri AI revamp, is likely to be released this fall, along with MacOS Golden Gate, Apple TVOS 27 and more. Since we learned about these at WWDC in June, we’ve been playing around with the public betas to see what’s inside.

Apple Watch Series 12: Apple Health and Touch ID?

A Series 12 Watch is “all but guaranteed,” CNET wearables expert Vanessa Hand Orellana says. Less likely are a new Apple Watch SE and Ultra model since they were refreshed in 2025. But any new watches, the Series 12 and Ultra 4, are likely to come with a new processor, which should extend their life and usefulness for you.

The biggest design change expected is largely mechanical, not aesthetic. A more energy-efficient screen technology could be included to extend the watches’ battery life without sacrificing screen brightness. A new processor — probably named the S12 to match the line-up’s naming, despite “S11” being next in line — would also help with this.

The next Apple Watch Series 12 may bring back TouchID. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

Another potential addition could be biometric authentication — in other words, a Touch ID for Apple Watch. Some internal code leaks suggest Apple is working on integrating this tech into its wearables, but it’s unclear when it will be publicly available. Health features, like blood pressure monitoring, are also rumored to be in progress, but again, no guarantees. The Apple Health App’s AI overhaul has also reportedly run into issues.

Our early testing shows WatchOS 27 with Siri AI will bring a big boost to devices — at least, for the ones it’s compatible with, which isn’t all of them. Watches were excluded from Apple’s summer price hike, but similar raises from watches by Google and Samsung mean a higher starting price isn’t out of the realm of possibility.

AirPods with or without cameras

Possibly the biggest Apple rumor has been that the next generation of Apple AirPods will be equipped with a new, tiny infrared camera — not to take photos, but to scan its physical environment to power its visual intelligence, or AI, answers.

The AirPods 5 could look similar to the AirPods 4 (shown) but have performance upgrades. David Carnoy/CNET

These rumored “AirPods Ultra” sparked a lot of concern and outrage from tech enthusiasts, who have spent most of the summer criticizing other AI-and-camera-enabled wearables, like Meta’s smart glasses. Apple is known to tout its focus on privacy, so it will be interesting to see if Apple ultimately comes out with these earbuds and, if so, how it defends them.

AirPods are generally on a two-year refresh cycle, so we may get the AirPods 5 and AirPods 5 Pro this year. The previous model, the AirPods 4 with active noise canceling, is “something of a technological marvel,” CNET headphones expert David Carnoy said. Effective noise canceling is hard to achieve with an open-earbud design, but Apple’s previous success sets the foundation for even more progress here. The Apple-owned Beats 360 headphones could also get refreshed this fall.

For more, check out the best iPhones and best MacBooks for 2026.

Tech.title: All 10 New Dyson Products Released Last Week at IFA 2026
Tech.content:
We’ve always been eager to get our lab gloves on Dyson’s latest releases. The way the brand is rolling out products these days, it’s becoming a full-time job. Gone are the days when Dyson, one of the top names in home tech, allows its new fans, hair dryers and vacuums to trickle out.

Last week alongside IFA, the massive Euro tech showcase, Dyson unveiled a whopping 10 new products at a solo event in Berlin. At “Dyson Unveiled,” the brand unleashed new floor care tools, air purifiers and health and beauty tech, including its first-ever toothbrush — and we got a peek at all of them.

Dyson is tackling oral care with a camera-equipped toothbrush and a water flosser. Dyson

The 2026 trove of new products is matched only by last year, when the brand launched 11 new products and Dyson isn’t just churning out products faster, as Dyson’s Chief Engineer Jake Dyson explained.

“The latest innovations combine Dyson’s decades of mechanical engineering with AI, vision systems and machine learning to create products that can see, understand and respond to the environments around them,” he said.

CNET’s ground team got hands-on with everything Dyson has coming to market this year. Here’s what’s new from Dyson in 2026 and when you can expect it.

CameraJet toothbrush

At IFA 2026, we’re seeing all the upgraded, AI-powered, repairable, camera-equipped tech. And then some. Tara Brown/CNET

This is Dyson’s first toothbrush, and it houses a tiny camera for the most detailed possible cleaning. According to the brand, it’s the first oral care tool to use AI-powered vision to detect and target gaps between teeth. It brushes, liquid flosses and even dispenses mouthwash.

The toothbrush costs $499 and is available now.

Dyson Airsmooth dryer brush

Dyson has unveiled its first-ever dryer brush. Tara Brown/CNET

Dyson’s releases aren’t limited to air care and cleaning. The brand released its first-ever dedicated dryer brush, which uses smart heat control and novel dual-bristle technology to dry, smooth and lift hair all in one motion.

The Airsmooth will retail for $249 and will be available to order starting on Sept. 8.

Dyson Corrale CoolShine straightener

Tara Brown/CNET

The success of Dyson’s cult-favorite Airwrap inspired this next-generation straightening tool, featuring flexing plates with active cooling that dries hair without exposing it to as much heat, as heat can damage hair.

The Corrale CoolShine costs $329 and hits shelves on Sept. 15.

HushJet Pure Cool Plus Formaldehyde air purifier

Dyson’s new HushJet air purifiers are a total redesign. Tara Brown/CNET

This new compact high-performance purifier and fan is designed for large spaces. The brand says it delivers three times the power of its predecessors. You can grab this model in the fall for $599.

HushJet Big Plus Quiet Cool Pure Plus Formaldehyde air purifier

Dyson’s new HushJet Big Cool has an angled pipe design and a rotating mouth. Dyson

Dyson’s most powerful purifier is engineered for long-range air projection and multiroom purification. It has a three-stage filtration system that captures particulates and gases, and it destroys formaldehyde.

This model will cost a whopping $1,099 and hits retailers in the fall.

HushJet Hot Cool Pure Plus air purifier

Dyson’s most powerful three-in-one purifier was on display in Berlin. Tara Brown/CNET

Dyson’s most powerful three-in-one purifier combines purification, heating and personal cooling in one machine for year-round home comfort.

This also launches in the fall and retails for $599.

Read our full coverage of Dyson’s new HushJet lineup here.

R3 Nurovi Spot Plus Scrub UV

Dyson is calling the R3 Nurovi Spot Plus Scrub UV its most advanced robot vacuum to date. Dyson

The brand is calling this its most advanced wet-and-dry robot vacuum to date. It features UV enhancement and, you guessed it, AI elements to help identify up to 200 types of stains and substances. The self-cleaning wet roller uses a 12-point system that continuously applies water heated to 158 degrees Fahrenheit to simultaneously lift and remove stubborn stains.

The robot vac costs $1,199 and is available starting Sept. 15.

R1 Nurovi Dry

Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry robot vacuum cleaner.

The Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry is engineered for deep cleaning on hard floors and carpets. It uses Dyson’s Twin-capture technology and intelligent floor and dust sensing.

This simpler robot vac will be available sometime in September for $549.

R2 Nurovi Wash Plus Dry

Dyson’s R2 Nurovi Wash Plus Dry robot vacuum.

Another robot vac is joining the lineup. This one has triangular cleaning pads to clean those pesky room corners.

The Wash Plus Dry is now available exclusively at Costco for $699.

W1 PencilWash Plus Dok

The PencilWash weighs less than 5 pounds and is just as thin as the PencilVac. Dyson

The new handheld cleaner is slimmer and lighter than the older model and includes a more absorbent roller and a hygienic waste system. It also has self-cleaning features built into the dock.

It will cost $349 and will be available in the fall.

Tech.title: An Hour of Gundam: Rogue Orbit Made Me Feverish for More Robot Combat
Tech.content:
When I’m piloting a big robot in a video game, I want it to have a big personality and an even bigger punch. After playing an hour of Gundam: Rogue Orbit, it seems the game will have both. But there’s still a lot to discover about Bandai Namco’s next entry in the giant robot franchise, due out March 5, 2027.

My virtual preview offered two missions and three premade mobile suits (the franchise’s name for the piloted robots) to choose from. The hour was enough to run through both stages with all three mobile suits, each equipped with a different melee weapon. One stage was an enemy gauntlet ending in a miniboss, while the other was a full-fledged boss battle. In the final game, you’ll be able to customize your robot kits, but we didn’t see that functionality because Bandai Namco wanted us focused entirely on the gameplay.

One thing was clear: This isn’t another Armored Core copy. While I loved 2023’s Armored Core 6: Fires of Rubicon, its dizzying array of parts and weapons could be a chore to optimize for the game’s blindingly fast, three-dimensional combat. From what I saw in the preview, Rogue Orbit takes a different, simpler approach. Forget about the Z-axis; just worry about jumping and dashing around, as in most modern melee action games.

True, I had to suspend my disbelief that my mobile suit was hopping around with normal-feeling gravity on the outside of a space station, but I’m betting this trims away a lot of zero-g bother to avoid the awkwardness of floaty jumps.

Unlike other mech games filled with long-range beam cannons and missiles, Rogue Orbit’s fights seem constrained to melee range only. Whether that was the result of our preview being limited to a trio of mobile suits with swords, lances and whips, or reflects the whole game, I didn’t mind. Ranged combat was limited to support equipment, like a set of orbiting drones that fired when I dashed.

Throughout the preview, I ran across space stations cutting and stabbing through an assortment of enemies, using different skills tuned to my weapons. The sword got a rad slash with trailing explosions, while the whip could be uncoiled for slightly longer-ranged swipes and the lance got a drill-dash to reposition my mobile suit. The combat felt polished, even with half a year to go before the game’s launch, with every attack triggering a momentary pause on contact — a satisfying touch that let me relish the damage I was dishing out and savor my assortment of rad skills.

Ultimately, Rogue Orbit’s combat gameplay felt like Dynasty Warriors or Virtual On (without the twin stick controls), using special skills until my ability gauge ran out and peppering in normal attacks until it charged back up. I had an ultimate attack as well, which, in the preview, gave me unlimited dashes for a limited time until I pulled the ability’s trigger, sending a volley of beams lancing down at my target. In the full game, players will be able to switch between different ultimate attacks.

The short preview was more a tease than a dive into the complexities of the game, and it sure was fun to pummel foes with something that looked like a mobile suit. But the big question I left with was: Does this feel like a Gundam game yet?

The current HUD for the game — from left to right: health, support items, ultimate ability (in the middle), special attack skills and weapon skills. Bandai Namco/Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

How much Gundam is there yet to discover in Rogue Orbit?

Given the brevity of the preview, I didn’t expect to get much context about the characters or plot. Like most latter-day Gundam media, Rogue Orbit is set in a new universe, so don’t expect to see anything from the Federation or Zeon of the original Universal Century setting. Haro, the friendly green, ball-shaped droid from the first Gundam show, does appear in the marketing. (I’m also praying that a masked, Char Aznable-like character will show up, a recurring feature of the franchise.)

From details dropped in the recent trailer and the preview, players will control RE-X, a seemingly human male who was “created” to control a Gundam, the franchise’s special category of humanoid robot mobile suits (his is called Gundam Helix). There are a few other characters in your ship’s crew, including the commander April and the heroine Sophia, who will accompany you.

The Giant is one of many foes awaiting players in Rogue Orbit. Bandai Namco/Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

Where many Gundam shows and media lean into a political clash between factions of humanity and their armadas of mobile suits, Rogue Orbit seems to be setting up a xenomorphic threat. The enemies I attacked in my preview all seemed organic and monstrous rather than mechanical. While the skulduggery and power clashes result in some of the best conflicts and themes in Gundam, centering Rogue Orbit on a humans-versus-aliens threat (or enemies looking like aliens) opens the door to some intriguing opportunities — by which I mean, huge fantasy-esque bosses that aren’t mechanical Mobile Armors.

At the end of the first mission on the space station exterior, I was clashing with an ogre-like humanoid mini-boss labeled The Giant, who had his own health bar and stagger meter. Similar to other games with those features, once I whittled the latter down enough, the mini-boss went down for a few moments to let me get a few hits in. When I whacked a limb enough, it became disabled, limiting the boss’s attack capabilities.

Players must face the Drake, a large boss with flying attacks, in one mission. Bandai Namco/Screenshot by David Lumb/CNET

The second mission was entirely set around confronting a massive alien dragon called the Drake, which took awhile to wear down. In addition to dodging swiping claws and avoiding strings of beams, the Drake has a tail and wings I could hit hard enough to break to temporarily disable some of the meaner blows of the scaly boss. Neither mission was too difficult and I finished both multiple times, but during the preview I only had the three premade kits and no additional difficulty levels to try out.

From what little I saw, there’s a lot waiting for action-combat fans, though there’s plenty of mechanics, kit customization, story details and encounter complexity left to be revealed about the game. I’m still on the fence for how “Gundam” it may end up feeling in the long run, but the combat’s polish is promising — and enough to have me looking forward to when I can climb into the cockpit again.

Gundam: Rogue Orbit will release on March 5, 2027 for PC, Xbox X/S and PS5.

Tech.title: Over Half of US Adults Want Better Battery Life, but Can Apple Deliver with its New iPhone Lineup?
Tech.content:
What’s motivating smartphone owners to consider upgrading hasn’t changed much over the years. Zain Awais/CNET

Charging your phone in the middle of the day can be annoying and inconvenient, especially when you’re on the go. Instead of fumbling with chargers, how about more battery life for your smartphone?

That’s what’s driving 52% of US adults to consider upgrading their phone according to a CNET survey. Besides that, 55% say a better price would convince them to get a new phone. With Apple’s Surprise and Shine event planned for Wednesday, Sept. 9, we’re expecting Apple’s first foldable phone and two phones from the iPhone 18 series. Analysts say the iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max could have better battery life than older models. But don’t expect lower prices thanks to RAMageddon.

With Apple’s event just days away, here’s what US adults are looking for in a smartphone and how it may be able to deliver.

Key findings The top three motivations for US adult smartphone owners to consider upgrading their devices are price (55%), longer battery life (52%) and more storage (38%). That’s the same top three as last year: In 2025, price was the top motivator (62%), followed by longer battery life (54%) and storage capacity (39%). Only 13% of smartphone owners would be motivated to consider upgrading to a new phone concept, such as a foldable or flip phone. Over half of smartphone owners (58%) experience frustration with their phone’s battery life, and 31% say their phone’s battery doesn’t hold a charge as well as it did when it was new.

Most US adults aren’t motivated by new smartphone features and designs

Smartphone brands, like Samsung and Apple, are building in convenient features, such as a tool to remove unwanted objects from pictures, AI call screening and the ability to draft a message from a prompt. However, CNET found that US adults would consider upgrading for more practical reasons. Over half (55%) of US smartphone users are motivated by price, including 53% of Apple users and 56% of Samsung users.

Yet brands are still exploring new concepts and features, like Apple Intelligence, a built-in AI feature and even Siri AI which will debut with iOS 27. Analysts expect Apple to unveil a book-style foldable iPhone, which could be named the iPhone Ultra or iPhone Fold. But that’s not what most smartphone owners are after.

Smartphone owners are more convinced by other design and feature factors when deciding on a new phone, such as camera features (27%) and the phone’s display or screen size (22%). Here are the top motivators to consider upgrading for all smartphone users.

Zain Awais / CNET

You’ve probably noticed the price of a basic smartphone has increased drastically over the years and now there’s a rumor that the price for the iPhone 18 series could be higher at Wednesday’s event. A TrendForce analyst predicts that the iPhone 18 Pro could start between $1,199 and $1,299, and $1,299 to $1,399 for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Meanwhile, the iPhone Ultra could start between $2,099 and $2,299.

Higher prices may be a good reason to buy the iPhone 17 now if you see a good deal, especially if Apple doesn’t release the base model of the iPhone 18 next week.

The top upgrading motivators haven’t changed much over the years

Looking back at CNET’s survey data from 2024 and 2025, and now, people’s motivators for upgrading their phones haven’t changed much. Price, longer battery life and more storage have been top drivers in the past, and despite small dips this year, they’re still key upgrading factors.

Despite design upgrades and new features, smartphone owners are still focused on how much they’re paying and how long they can use their devices without needing a charger. Consumer sentiment about AI integrations dropped hard from 2024 to 2025, but it has edged up slightly in 2026. And smartphone owners aren’t as easily persuaded by phone color or the phone being thinner, either.

Even with these nice-to-have capabilities, smartphone owners are looking at the basics. That includes practical features like battery life and more storage to hold their many important files, photos and apps.

Most smartphone owners want better battery life

Taking a closer look at smartphone users’ hope for longer battery life in a new phone, over half (58%) are frustrated with their current phone’s battery life. Roughly 1 in 3 (31%) say their phone doesn’t hold a charge.

The reality is, battery life will decline the longer you have your phone, so you may find your phone’s battery charge doesn’t last as long as it used to. Even though you can replace your phone’s battery, most phone batteries have a lifespan of two to three years before they start degrading.

CNET Director of Editorial Content Patrick Holland examined battery life tests on over 35 current smartphones. And it’s not just iPhones that pack impressive batteries.



Based on CNET’s lab testing, the $1,200 iPhone 17 Pro Max had the best overall battery life, with a 5,088-mAh capacity. Another top performer was the $900 OnePlus 15, with a 7,300-mAh battery. There’s a rumor that if Apple releases a foldable phone in the future, it will be even better than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, but we’ll have to wait and see.

If you’re looking for a phone with better battery life, consider one with a silicon-carbon battery to increase capacity without requiring a larger phone. The OnePlus 15, Poco F7 Ultra, OnePlus 13R and OnePlus 15R all feature silicon-carbon batteries with large capacities and all performed well in Holland’s testing. Keep in mind that other factors can impact your battery life, like your carrier’s signal, software efficiency and processor.

Methodology

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample comprised 2,486 adults, of whom 2,407 owned a smartphone. Fieldwork was undertaken from April 29 to May 1, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

Tech.title: Should You Buy a New iPhone From Apple, a Carrier or Unlocked? Here’s What to Know
Tech.content:
You might be planning to get a new iPhone, be it the rumored iPhone 18 Pro or the highly anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra. But besides choosing which phone to get, the next big question you might be pondering is “Where should I buy my phone?” Should you get it directly from Apple or through a carrier?

Both methods have their pros and cons, and neither is best for everyone. Perhaps you like the idea of owning your phone outright without going through a third party. Or maybe you’d rather spread out your payments over time. Or perhaps you’re looking to upgrade your phone and switch carriers at the same time. Depending on your answer, you might prefer one path over the other.

In this guide, we walk you through the process of deciding exactly where to buy your new iPhone, be it directly from Apple or through a wireless provider.

This article was made possible in part by T-Mobile. It was written and edited independently without partner oversight.

Buy directly from Apple

Apple will glady sell you its newest phone and revamped its Upgrade program to let people lease their next iPhone. Jeff Carlson/CNET

Since Apple makes the iPhone, it makes a lot of sense to simply buy the phone directly from the Apple Store. Though buying your iPhone from Apple is a common practice in a lot of countries, it’s not quite as popular here in the US due to the attractive financing options that wireless carriers offer. But buying your phone straight from Apple has its benefits.

The primary reason to go through Apple is that you can buy the phone without being beholden to a wireless carrier. You have options. Instead of locking yourself down to one wireless carrier for multiple years, buying directly from Apple lets you get the phone completely unlocked.



Apple sells both unlocked iPhones and models tied to a specific carrier. The price is nearly the same, depending on which iPhone you get. But Apple drops the price by $30 when you buy and activate a new iPhone on a carrier at the time of purchase for models like the iPhone 17, which costs $829 unlocked or $799 after a carrier discount.

Unlocked models can be used with nearly any carrier you want, whether it’s a major carrier such as T-Mobile and AT&T or a smaller one such as Mint Mobile or Cricket Mobile. You can also swap out carriers every so often if you feel like it. While your iPhone may cost a pretty penny in the initial purchase, you could save on monthly bills in the long run, depending on your plan.

Another strong reason to get an unlocked phone is if you travel a lot and want to use international travel eSIMs from companies such as Airalo or Saily. These eSIMs only work on unlocked phones. Otherwise, you’re stuck with your carrier’s international data plans, which are often a lot more expensive.

If you don’t have the means to purchase the phone outright, you could opt for Apple’s Upgrade program, which lets you lease the phone through Klarna for 12 or 24 months. The phone will still be unlocked, but you’ll have to commit to one of the big three carriers: AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon.

Buy from a wireless provider

T-Mobile, Verizon and AT&T offer a variety of installment plans and trade-in deals on new iPhones. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

While there is a lot of freedom in buying an iPhone directly from Apple, it comes at a considerable cost. Even the most entry-level iPhone will cost you more than $600 upfront, while more premium handsets can easily cost over $1,000. On top of that, rising component costs could mean even higher prices going forward. It’s no wonder that so many Americans opt for carrier-based financing to purchase their phone. The iPhone 18 Pro could see a price hike, according to a Bloomberg report.

Not all carriers will offer financing, but the big three (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon) certainly do. In addition to 12- and 24-month installments, some also offer financing up to 36 months, which is more than what Apple’s Upgrade program does. This can really help spread out your payments if you don’t mind sticking with one carrier for an extended period.

Beyond just being able to pay over time, purchasing an iPhone through your wireless carrier has other benefits, too. Carriers like T-Mobile, for example, offer a 5-year price guarantee on future handsets, which is especially attractive in times of economic uncertainty.

If you do plan to switch carriers when you buy a new phone, there are potentially even more incentives. Carriers often have new phone deals and could even offer financial assistance to pay off your current phone if you make the switch. There are also some that offer steep discounts if you trade in an existing phone. Sometimes, these incentives come in the form of bill credits, instead of an upfront discount or cashback.

Now that you have an idea about buying a new iPhone, check out our comprehensive guide to switching carriers if you’re looking for more insight on how to navigate the process.

Tech.title: People’s Picks: 4 Phone Brands Dominate, but 1 Reigns Supreme and It’s Not Apple
Tech.content:
Every few years, you may think about upgrading your smartphone. A lot of thought and research goes into your next choice, whether it’s the price, features or brand reputation. Maybe you’re eyeing the latest and greatest, or considering a different phone brand or model altogether. Our readers’ opinions may help you decide.

CNET’s People’s Picks dives into what our readers really think about their tech devices and services, like their internet service provider, TVs and even their mobile carrier.

This round was all about readers’ phone brands, just in time for Apple’s Sept. 9 Surprise and shine event, where we expect new iPhone models to be revealed. We asked about everything from brand loyalty to battery life, durability and even price-to-value. The results came down to four big-name tech brands. While there’s only one overall winner, other brands win in key categories that can make a big difference in your day-to-day tasks if you’re upgrading soon.

Overall winner: Google

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Google is the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Picks for Phones. CNET averaged the scores across three categories to determine the overall satisfaction rating, which includes customer satisfaction, battery longevity and price-to-value.

Google wins with a score of 4.52 out of 5, while Motorola trails closely behind with 4.45.

“It’s no surprise to me that Google and Motorola scored top marks because both sell some of the most affordable phones that people can buy. Motorola’s Moto G series costs hundreds of dollars less than Apple’s cheapest iPhone,” said CNET’s Director of Content, Patrick Holland. “At $500, Google’s Pixel 10A is one of the best values that you can buy today, especially as phone prices spike due to the ongoing RAM shortage caused by AI and data centers. It just goes to show that in 2026, you can spend less than $500 and still have a great phone that lasts you years.”

On the other hand, Samsung and Apple trail behind with scores of 4.19 and 3.87, respectively. Both brands have evolved in the smartphone space with AI-powered features, upgraded cameras, and thinner phone designs, but fell short in this category.

“There are a few factors at play here, most notably that Google and Motorola ship a fraction of the phones that Samsung does — so Pixel and Razr buyers are a more devoted core of customers than the many who buy Galaxy phones,” said CNET Managing Editor of Mobile David Lumb. A Counterpoint Research report on phone shipments in the first quarter of 2026 noted that Google (3% of the US market) and Motorola (10%) combined accounted for half of Samsung’s market share (26%).

The other thing to remember is that Google sells mostly premium phones.



“Aside from the Pixel 10A as a midrange device. Motorola and Samsung have wider ranges of more affordable and cheap phones, so I’d guess there’s less consumer fondness at the lower end of the device price scale,” Lumb said.

Apple’s fourth-place spot is a tougher nut to crack. Perhaps consumers haven’t seen as many upgrades in successive years as they would like in new iPhones, or they’re miffed at the higher prices Apple’s phones sell for. What’s most likely the case, Lumb suggested, is that there are simply more people buying new iPhones. In the Counterpoint report above, Apple handsets accounted for 58% of all phones shipped in the US.

AI features

AI features like photo editing, live translation and AI-powered summaries are becoming the focal point for new smartphone models. But what matters more is how much you’ll use those built-in features. Google Pixel wins with 88% of its users saying their phone’s AI features are essential and occasionally useful.

“Out of the four brands, only one is a true AI company, and that’s Google. In fact, Google’s Gemini AI can run on phones from all four brands, including the iPhone via an app. The Gemini Assistant can be used on Motorola and Samsung phones,” said Holland.

Lumb added that Google has led the charge in both including and promoting AI features in its Pixel phones that people actually use, like Magic Eraser and live translation.

“Pixel owners have been using AI features for years, and combined with Google aggressively inserting its Gemini assistant throughout the phone, it makes sense that Samsung Galaxy owners would feel a lesser impact from AI.”

Samsung has made plenty of AI advancements, like a health assistant and browser upgrades, but it falls behind, with only 64% of its users saying the same. Apple and Motorola trail behind with 14% and 8% each. Most Motorola users say the phone lacked built-in tools or ignored them.



What few AI features are available on iPhones were introduced more recently, so it’s unsurprising that their owners wouldn’t consider them essential to daily use, Lumb said. While Gemini continues to evolve, Apple’s advanced AI Siri was delayed for years and will finally launch with the upcoming iOS 27.

Battery life

Ties with Motorola



For a phone’s battery to exceed expectations, it must last a day or more. Motorola and Google tie in this category, with 74% saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations by lasting a full day or longer without needing to be charged. Comparatively, Samsung and Apple fall behind, with only about half (52%) saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations, while others say they just meet expectations. Apple finishes last, with only 31% reporting the same for their iPhones’ batteries. Most said their phone needed to be charged midday.

“The number one factor for battery life is how you use your phone. And I think this result speaks volumes about how much iPhone owners are on their phones,” said Holland.

CNET’s phone battery testing found that Apple’s phones had the longest battery life, with OnePlus placing second and Motorola third. However, the test doesn’t account for how you use your phone specifically each day – everyone is different. If you’re hyper-connected and your default is scrolling through social media apps or streaming videos, even the best battery life won’t be enough for you, Holland said. “Thankfully, Google, Motorola and Samsung, along with Apple, have all increased the charging speeds on their handsets to at least make topping them off less of a pain point.”

Motorola

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Value

Motorola wins in price-to-value, with 82% of its readers saying it offers exceptional value by delivering more than its price suggests. Only 4% rate the brand as overpriced.

“Before Motorola brought back the Razr as a foldable phone, its most popular handsets were its Moto G line that start as low as $200 and top out at $350,” said Holland. “Motorola has deep, long-term relationships with phone carriers, which often sell these phones at a discount.”

Compared with other brands, 45% of Pixel owners say Google’s phone offers exceptional value, and 35% of Samsung users say the same.

The surprising fact is that Apple places fourth in this category, with 58% of iPhone users saying it’s overpriced. Only 12% find the phone’s value exceptional. However, many tech brands are raising prices due to the RAM shortage, which makes it tough to determine what’s worth the high cost.

“The only company that hasn’t raised prices on its phones this year is Apple. There’s a chance it might announce a price hike at its Sept. 9 event. The cheapest iPhone the company sells starts at $600. You can find incredible Android phones for less, like the Google Pixel 10A for $500,” said Holland.

Apple

J. Hazelwood/CNET

Durability

Choosing a phone that doesn’t shatter, crack or leave you with a broken camera can make a big difference when you need one to last a few years. Some phones are more durable than others. Apple wins this category with 78% of readers saying it’s highly durable against drops and daily use with minimal to no damage. The remaining 22% either deal with normal wear and minor scuffs over time, report their phone as fragile or always have a heavy-duty case to protect it.

Holland said that when Apple released the iPhone 12 in 2020, it was the first to have a flat, dense build with squared-off sides to increase durability. In the years following, Samsung followed suit, adopting a flat build for its Galaxy S and S Plus models, and Google implemented a similar design with its Pixel phones.

Google follows closely behind with 72% saying their Pixel smartphone is highly durable, while 28% say it’s moderately durable.

Not as many readers with a Motorola say the phone is highly durable (65%), but even fewer readers with a Samsung (58%) phone say the same. Samsung users say their foldable phone and screens are fragile and only moderately durable. Some readers criticize the brand for the phone’s fragility and susceptibility to damage from drops.

Brand retention and loyalty

Despite Apple falling short in several categories, 86% of Apple users said they’re extremely likely to buy the same brand next time.

“Apple’s most popular product is the iPhone, but its iPhone-only features like iMessage and FaceTime, not found on Android, that keep people tied in,” said Holland. “Also, if you want to learn about how to use your iPhone or get it fixed, you can go to the Apple Store and talk with an actual human – I think those retail stores are Apple’s secret weapon.”

Whereas 79% of Samsung owners share the same sentiment for the brand. Over half of Google Pixel owners (58%) would buy a Google phone again, but only 42% of people with Motorola phones would. Other Motorola owners are using competitor research to determine their next phone purchase.

Methodology

CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,107 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from July 1 to July 28, 2026.

Tech.title: How to Watch Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ Event Tomorrow
Tech.content:
Apple

It’s almost time. Apple is holding its next event, which the company is calling “Surprise and shine,” tomorrow. Historically, Apple has used its September event to announce new hardware, particularly the newest models of iPhones. That means we only have a few hours left see if Apple will unveil the rumored foldable iPhone.

You can catch the Apple event on Apple’s website, Apple TV, the Apple Developer app and the company’s YouTube channel on Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 10 a.m. PT (1 p.m. ET, 6 p.m. BST). We expect to hear from Apple’s incoming CEO, John Ternus, for the first time in his role after he took up the mantle on Sept. 1.

Here are a few things Apple could announce at the event.

A foldable iPhone

Whether Apple calls it the iPhone Fold, iPhone Ultra or the iPhone Flip, the company could show off a foldable iPhone at its September event. Leaks and supply chain reports suggest the foldable iPhone will be a squat, book-style foldable, similar to the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8.

This is a mock-up of what a possible iPhone Fold might look like, according to CNET designer Jeffrey Hazelwood. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

Those same leaks also suggest the price of the iPhone foldable could be between $2,000 and $2,500, which could price many people out. According to a CNET survey, US adults are only willing to spend an average of $781 on a foldable iPhone, which is less than the price of the base model iPhone 17 ($799).

Patrick Holland, CNET’s director of content, said that foldable phones remain a niche interest among most shoppers, but that Apple is likely to price the device to reflect its expensive manufacturing costs.

New iPhone 18 Pro models

CNET’s Jeffrey Hazelwood created these custom renders of what an iPhone 18 Pro might look like. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

According to Bloomberg, Apple could unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max at its September event, too. Those iPhones could also see a price hike, with prices starting at $1,200, up from the iPhone 17 Pro‘s starting price of $1,100.

You might notice that entry-level iPhone 18 models are missing from that lineup. That’s because Bloomberg suspects Apple will split the iPhone launch this year. That means we could see the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September before Apple rolls out the iPhone 18, iPhone 18E and potentially a refreshed iPhone Air in the spring.

New Apple Watches

The (from left to right) Apple Watch Ultra 3, Apple Watch Series 11 and Apple Watch SE 3. Apple could show new Apple Watches at its event in September. Carly Marsh/CNET

Apple is also reportedly preparing to announce an Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its September event. According to Bloomberg, the new watches could include faster chips and new health and fitness features. However, the new watches likely won’t receive a design change.

There’s no solid information about how much these watches will cost. However, Apple has raised a lot of hardware prices this year, so while the starting price of the Apple Watch 11 is $399, the Apple Watch 12 could cost more at launch.

The AirPods 5

The AirPods 4 (pictured) are a few years old now, so Apple could show AirPods 5 at the company’s September event. Apple/CNET

Bloomberg also reports that Apple could debut the AirPods 5 at the September event, releasing an updated version of the company’s entry-level headphones. Apple released the AirPods 4 almost two years ago, in 2024. Apple isn’t expected to show the rumored camera-equipped AirPods at the September event. We could see those later this year, or in 2027.

The AirPods 4 had a starting price of $129 at launch, but given Apple’s other price increases, the AirPods 5 could also see a higher starting price.

Apple did not immediately respond to CNET’s request to comment.
